Project Title: AG DRIED TOMATO POWDER
Executive Summary: The AG Dried Tomato Powder project focuses on the production of high-quality, nutrient-dense tomato powder using sustainable, efficient processing methods. By harnessing local agricultural resources and leveraging innovative drying techniques, the project aims to reduce post-harvest loss, enhance food preservation, and provide a value-added product for both local and international markets. This initiative seeks to improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers, create job opportunities, and contribute to sustainable food systems while addressing global food security.
Innovation Description: The AG Dried Tomato Powder project addresses the significant issue of tomato post-harvest loss, which is a widespread problem in many agricultural regions, especially in sub-Saharan Africa. Tomatoes are highly perishable, and poor storage, transportation, and handling contribute to up to 50% of losses annually. This results in wasted resources, financial losses for farmers, and limited availability of nutritious food.  The innovation provides a sustainable solution by turning fresh tomatoes into a long-lasting, nutrient-rich tomato powder. This method not only preserves the tomatoes but also adds value by creating a versatile product that can be used in cooking, food processing, and other industries. The drying process reduces water content, extending shelf life and making the product easier to store and transport.  The solution is driven by a combination of sustainable farming practices and modern drying technology, which retains the tomatoes' flavor, nutritional content, and versatility. It offers a win-win for both consumers and farmers. For consumers, it provides an affordable and convenient option for accessing high-quality tomatoes year-round. For farmers, it opens new markets and increases their income by offering a value-added product that can be sold locally and internationally.  The immediate benefits include reduced food waste, improved food security, and increased incomes for local farmers. Long-term, the initiative will contribute to sustainable agricultural practices, climate resilience, and greater access to affordable, nutritious food, helping improve the livelihoods of communities and creating positive environmental impacts.

Project Title: ICTs, market access and food security for small-scale fisheries
Executive Summary: ABALOBI empowers small-scale fishers to adapt to climate change through digital tools, sustainable practices, and community food security initiatives. Our programme channels affordable, high-quality seafood to vulnerable communities, expands distributor networks, and trains fishers in sustainability and digital tools. Tailored workshops empower women and marginalized groups, ensuring equal access to opportunities. Together with the ABALOBI Marketplace, these initiatives enhance traceability, foster socio-economic resilience, and promote sustainable resource use, strengthening livelihoods and marine health
Innovation Description: Small-scale fisheries provide jobs to 60 million people (representing 90% of the total global fishing industry) and support over 160 million jobs in ancillary activities. In Africa, they account for 85% of all fishers, feeding over 200 million people annually. Yet, these fishers, especially women who are vital to the sector, face systemic marginalisation in markets and management forums. Many earn less than $1 per day, lack access to financial services, and remain unseen in governance due to insufficient data and digital identities. This exclusion leaves them vulnerable to exploitative practices, trapping them in cycles of debt and poverty. ABALOBI addresses these barriers with an innovative combination of digital tools and tailored training programmes. Fishers gain digital identities to record, track, and market their catches transparently, bridging critical data gaps and unlocking access to fair markets, financial tools, and governance platforms. Women and marginalised groups are empowered through tailored workshops and mentorships, ensuring equal access to opportunities. Training on sustainable fishing techniques and digital tools builds capacity for ecosystem-friendly practices, leading to healthier fish stocks, reduced ecological footprints, and greater resilience to climate change. To further address food security, ABALOBI channels affordable, high-quality seafood into vulnerable coastal and rural communities, expanding coverage through a growing network of trained distributors. This integrated approach delivers immediate benefits: improved incomes, financial inclusion, and food security. Long-term, ABALOBI fosters socio-economic resilience, sustainable fisheries, and ensures small-scale fishers play a pivotal role in tackling global food security and safeguarding marine ecosystems.

Flour availability, goes a long way to provide school going children with good food for the growth of brain to perform well in school, helps to have health communities and source of income to women groups whilst protecting environment.

Project Title: ARVUM I - Indoor Plant Factory Pilot
Executive Summary: AGRA is looking to construct a pilot of its indoor Plant Factory technology that is unique in its ability to sustainably grow crops at the same price as traditional methods. AGRA s Plant Factories grow without sun or soil, using artificial light and a nutrient rich mist, powered by renewable energy. The pilot will validate the technology at scale, paving the way for private investment, offtake from supermarkets and commercialisation.
Innovation Description: Crops are responsible for 11% annual GHG emissions, 30% of global water withdrawals, deforestation, habitat destruction, species extinction, land degradation, water contamination and eutrophication. Farming as a profession is in decline (11% between 2006 and 2011 in Australia), crop yields are expected to decline by 10-20% by 2050 while our production needs to increase by 70%. Farmers face uncharacteristically high instances of mental health issues and suicide (tied to a rural job ruled by the weather) with the FAO reporting Agriculture as one of the most hazardous jobs worldwide.  If we do nothing, we will face challenges in feeding the population while doing untold damage to our world.  Plant Factories are unique in that they can address all of these problems in one solution, something well established in industry and academia. However, they are historically expensive to build and operate. If the sustainable option remains expensive, we will never be able to solve agricultures challenges. Looking at the underlying costs, this doesn't have to be the case, its just extremely challenging to achieve and thus requires the efforts of a company with a strong ideological motive.  Through several years of rigorous R&D, AGRA have developed Plant Factory technology that, for the first time, can produce crops at price parity with the field. Able to grow consistently year-round independent of climate or weather, using 70% less N2O & CO2, 90% less water, 84-168x yield/m2, no pesticides/herbicides, 40% longer shelf-life, higher quality produce, located near urban centers and powered by renewable energy.

Project Title: Cold Chain as a service (CaaS) for Rural farmers in Offgrid Communities
Executive Summary: Our solution takes off the burden of acquiring cold chain infrastructure by small holder farmers which is quite expensive, and in turn provides Cooling as a Service (CaaS) with a  pay as you go  model to rural small holder farmers who cannot afford the upfront cost of a reefer, but yet get to enjoy cooling service for their farm produce. We provide cold storage assets at the farmgate and coldrom trucks for distribution too.
Innovation Description: Problem: 200 words KIPITFRESH addresses lack of access energy access for productive uses in off-grid rural farming communities; lack of access to sustainable cooling; and prevalence of post harvest losses with fruits and vegetables. Post harvest losses is more prevalent with fresh fruits and vegetables which have low shelf live and are highly perishable. Over 50% of fresh fruits and vegetables(FFV's) end up wasted in Nigeria due to lack of adequate cold storage facilities. In Nigeria alone, farmers lose over 9 billion dollars annually from post harvest losses. These losses play a critical role in influencing the life of millions of smallholder farmers by impacting the available food volumes and trade-in values of the commodities. Post Harvest losses results in increased carbon emissions with negative impacts on the environment. A report by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) using the life cycle perspective, estimated about 3.3 Gtonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions due to food waste, aside from land use changes. Furthermore, Postharvest losses reduces income of smallholder farmers, as harvested produce has to be sold at unfavorable prices due to lack of cold storage.  Solution: KIPITFRESH provides cold storage and distribution services to small holder farmers located in underserved communities with no access to grid connection, to help reduce post-harvest loss in Nigeria s fruits and vegetable sector. KIPITFRESH is a mobile cold chain solution comprising solar powered mobile reefers for storage, and hybrid cold trucks for long long haul distribution from farmgate to the final offtaker.

Project Title: Emattahu - Resilient Agriculture for Nutrition and Sustainability
Executive Summary: Emattahu empowers communities through sustainable agriculture and nutrition-focused solutions. By training 240 women in eco-friendly farming practices and improving school meals for 3,368 children, the project enhances food security and community resilience. Leveraging APOIAR's expertise in health, education, and community development, alongside specialized partners in agriculture and environment, it establishes a scalable model to combat food insecurity, support local economies, and promote environmental sustainability across Mozambique.
Innovation Description: In Niassa, communities face persistent food insecurity (UNOCHA, 2024) and low agricultural productivity due to traditional farming practices, climate vulnerabilities, and limited access to resources, as highlighted by Matavel et al. (2019) and confirmed through APOIAR s fieldwork. These challenges entrench cycles of poverty, malnutrition, and environmental degradation, undermining community resilience and sustainable development. Reliance on water-intensive crops, limited access to climate-resilient farming techniques, and unsustainable practices worsen soil exhaustion, water scarcity, and biodiversity loss. Inadequate food preservation and seed-saving knowledge further expose communities to seasonal shortages and malnutrition, disproportionately affecting children, pregnant women, and new mothers. APOIAR presents an innovative approach to fostering sustainable agriculture and food security leveraging science, traditional knowledge, and community engagement. Our solution addresses root causes of food insecurity by promoting climate-resilient practices, enhancing local food system nutrition, and integrating sustainable resource management. This includes supporting communities to transition to drought-resistant crops, intercropping to improve soil health and biodiversity, and adopting seed preservation and food conservation techniques for year-round nutritious solutions. Grounded in a comprehensive understanding of environmental, social, and economic dynamics, our solution empowers communities with the tools, knowledge, and support to transform local food systems into innovative, resilient, and nutritionally robust frameworks. This strategy fosters long-term self-sufficiency, ensuring profound and sustainable impact. Emattahu benefits:   Farmers and families: increased yields, improved nutrition, and new income opportunities.   Children, pregnant women, and new mothers: access to nutrient-dense foods supporting maternal and child health.   Environment: reduced soil degradation, biodiversity preservation, and optimized water use.

Project Title: Regenerative Agriculture in Oil palm production
Executive Summary: AQUA-OSUK Enterprises Limited is an agribusiness from Nigeria in Oil Palm Production. We are promoting Regenerative Agriculture in oil palm production to reverse deforestation and biodiversity loss caused by monoculture cultivation of oil palm. We are unique because we integrate regenerative agriculture in oil palm production via waste management, oil palm agroforestry system, and Fertilizer Drawn Forward Osmosis (FDFO). Collectively, they promote a circular economy in oil palm production.
Innovation Description: The African oil palm is a crop used to produce palm oil and palm oil is mainly used for cooking, production of cosmetic products, and as a source of renewable energy (palm oil biofuel). We promote regenerative agriculture in oil palm production via a. Waste Management: We sell oil palm seedlings to oil palm farmers in Nigeria. We integrated waste management into our production by collecting used plastic water sachets and reusing them as polythene pots for the seedlings and we also collect oil palm ash from oil palm mills and reuse them as organic fertilizers for the seedlings. We have been able to reduce the indiscriminate dumping of plastic and agricultural waste. Project Title: Cool Lion: Solar-Powered Refrigerated Containers for a Better Social Impact
Executive Summary: In Sub-Saharan Africa, post-harvest food losses represent USD$ 4bn/year - or enough to feed at least 48 million people. On average, African smallholder farmers lose up to 36% of their food produce which equates to significant wasted land use, carbon emissions and perpetuates rural poverty. The lack of effective storage solutions for the preservation of fresh products translates into large volumes of perishable products losses and up to 40% average loss of income for smallholders    One big solution — Cold storage solutions to eliminate post-harvest losses for African smallholder farmers — is out of their reach and we’re solving this.  We offer cooling-as-a-service under a pay-as-you-go model to smallholder cooperatives in Africa and Cote d'Ivoire that combine clean energy access (solar power, hybrid) and digital solutions. We do this by installing cold storage refrigerated containers (10-foot size and above) or standalone cooling systems attachable to existing storehouses which keep produce fresh from 7 weeks for staples and up to 1 year for small-scale fishermen.    Our ambition is to become the leader in providing infrastructure solutions and services for the preservation and marketing of perishable products in the agricultural sector in Sub-Saharan Africa.

Project Title: Turning waste into food (WIF): Integrated Multi-Trophic Farm (IMTF) in a circular economy
Executive Summary: Fish and poultry have the potential to improve the nutrition and income of the population and also contribute to the health of the environment. However, capture fisheries has passed its peak and the costs of the feed for aquaculture and poultry have skyrocketed. The growth and sustainability are dependent upon looking for alternative sustainable ingredients to the commercial feeds. This project will realize the potential of Microalgae and Black Soldier Fly Larvae as feed ingredients.
Innovation Description: The future growth and sustainability of aquaculture and poultry is dependent upon the industry stepping away from its reliance upon animals as major feed ingredients. Microalgae have the highest areal biomass productivities among photosynthetic organisms and microalgal production has a low water and arable-land footprint, making microalgal-based feed environmentally sustainable and climate resilient. Several compounds in algae have confounding effects, providing a source of protein, amino acids, fatty acids, vitamins and minerals. Similarly, Black Soldier Fly Larvae (BSFL) are rich in protein, fats, and oil with added environmental advantage requiring less land and water; lower greenhouse gas emissions; transforming low-value organic by-products into high-quality food or feed. BSFL are also efficient bio-converters that can be mass-reared on low input resources. They are also used in the production of compost that can reduce the rather expensive cost of inorganic fertilizers. Therefore, the project will conduct experiments showcasing the safe and effective benefits that microalgal and BSFL products (fresh, dry, proteins, lipids, fertilizers) have for fish and poultry growth. The project will also train Microalgae/BSFL farmers/entrepreneurs to enable them to incorporate these products into the feeding regimen of their fish and poultry farms. Finally, the ultimate aim is to reach the goal of using microalgal and BSFL products by farmers to reduce the quantity of conventional feed used in producing fish and poultry and, in turn, reduce the cost of production and become environmentally friendly. Ultimately, this should lead producers to acquiring improved economic status, nutritional quality and resilience to climate change.

Project Title: Elevating Safety and Quality in East African Food Markets
Executive Summary: Aflakiosk is an innovative solution, delivering testing services, market linkages and training for farmers, cooperatives, aggregators, processors and other clients especially within the grain value chain. Our testing service allows clients to understand the quality of their grains and enables us to link good quality produce to premium markets. Training services - based on testing diagnostics - enable our clients to take the necessary remedial action to manage and maintain quality over time.
Innovation Description: Rwanda loses 40% of its food supply annually, with grains like maize accounting for 25% of these losses. Poor post-harvest handling, lack of access to affordable quality testing, and insufficient facilities such as dryers and warehouses contribute to these losses. Aflakiosk addresses these issues by providing accessible, cost-effective quality testing and training stakeholders on proper post-harvest practices.  High moisture content in grains has been directly linked to increased aflatoxin levels, which pose significant health risks, including liver cancer and stunting in children. Contaminated grains also prevent farmers and traders from accessing premium markets, where profits are 30% higher. This exclusion perpetuates a cycle of low income and poor reinvestment in improved practices.  Using innovative dry chemistry testing, Aflakiosk identifies contamination risks and educates stakeholders on reducing aflatoxin levels. Its accessible services empower farmers, cooperatives, and processors to improve grain quality, reduce losses, and access better-paying markets. These efforts enhance food security, reduce health risks, and increase incomes for stakeholders, fostering a more resilient food system.  Immediate benefits include reduced grain losses and better-quality products, while sustainable benefits involve improved health outcomes, increased market access, and higher economic returns for farmers and communities. By addressing a critical gap in Rwanda's grain value chain, Aflakiosk is transforming food systems and promoting long-term societal and environmental health.

Project Title: Roots of Resilience
Executive Summary: The Roots of Resilience program transforms Tanzanian agriculture by training youth in regenerative farming practices. Through a Train the Trainer model, the initiative empowers 25 master trainers to integrate indigenous knowledge with modern regenerative agriculture techniques, using a mobile Future-Farm bus. The program restores soil health, promotes food security, and creates economic opportunities while preserving cultural heritage. It integrates hands-on farm training, research, and digital tools to ensure accessibility, job creation, and community empowerment.
Innovation Description: Problem Being Solved: Tanzania faces critical agricultural challenges, including food insecurity, climate change impacts, and soil degradation. Over-reliance on chemical fertilisers and pesticides has compromised soil health, increased climate vulnerability, and created dependency on unstable supply chains. This situation threatens long-term agricultural productivity, public health, and rural economic resilience.  Solution Approach:  The solution is a comprehensive regenerative agriculture education program that: - Trains youth as agricultural transformation leaders - Integrates indigenous knowledge with modern sustainable practices - Reduces chemical (farm input) dependencies - Promotes soil regeneration and biodiversity - Creates economic opportunities in rural communities - Develops resilient, local food systems By training 25 master trainers who will subsequently train hundreds of farmers, the project addresses multiple interconnected challenges: environmental degradation, food insecurity, economic instability, and limited agricultural innovation. The approach empowers communities with knowledge, practical skills, and a sustainable pathway to agricultural transformation.  Scientific/Technical Insights: - Experiential learning methodology - Permaculture and agroforestry principles - Indigenous agricultural knowledge - Health and medicinal value of plants for humans - Digital technology integration - Data-driven monitoring  Benefits: Farmers gain reduced farming input costs, improved soil health, and increased crop diversity and food security. The environment benefits from reduces emissions, soil restoration, biodiversity preservation, and carbon sequestration. Communities experience agriculture all job creation, youth empowerment, improved public health through chemical-free farming and economic resilience.  By creating a holistic, replicable approach, the Roots of Resilience program transforms agricultural education while simultaneously addressing environmental, economic, and social challenges through regenerative farming practices.

Project Title: Farm-In-A-Tank (Pilot Stage)
Executive Summary: AARC is a pioneering agribusiness concern, developing a commercial smallholder aquaculture-value-chain. At this Pilot Stage: we shall establish a 'Smallholder Outgrower Scheme' with 100 farmers, equip them with a Farm-In-A-Tank (FIAT)   a high-yielding fish-tank, provide inputs and extension services. As the sole off-taker, AARC will buy, process and sell the fish.. The goal is to ascertain the economic, social and financial viability of the business model and position the project for scaling.
Innovation Description: Problem Statement: Notably, one-third of the worlds  droughts occur in sub-Saharan Africa. Considering that smallholder farmers contribute over 80% of food supplies, and over 90% of agriculture is rain-fed, the impact of climate change is deeper and longer lasting in Sub-Saharan Africa than any other continent in terms of food production, livelihoods, health and water security   driving more people into multi-dimensional poverty. Currently 60% of the continent s population is experiencing food insecurity with rate of malnutrition at 47% in some regions .  Against this backdrop, AARC identified commercialisation of smallholder aquaculture as the agricultural value-chain with the most potential to accelerate the production of high-protein food at scale, raise incomes for smallholder farmers, create jobs especially for women and youth, while improving their climate adaptability and resilience. Our Solution combines (3) strategic pro-poor interventions that address the issues that deter smallholders from participating in commercial aquaculture: a) Technology Innovation: We have developed a cost-effective, high-yielding, semi-intensive fish-tank (FIAT)- that intensifies smallholder yields from 200Kg/year [using earthen ponds], to commercial level of 2,000 Kg/year. b) Inclusive Business Model: To scale production, we have adopted the Smallholder Outgrower Model- where AARC provides each outgrower (60% women) a FIAT, inputs and extension services- -purchases the fish, processes and sells   providing outgrowers a reliable monthly income. c) Credit Line: AARC provides the FIAT on lease and inputs on credit   hence outgrowers can focus on fattening the fish to market size without worrying about costs  the key deterrent to commercial aquaculture.

Project Title: Empowering Nigerian Soybean Farmers: Training Cooperatives for Sustainable Farming, Value Addition, and Market Access
Executive Summary: Our project aims to train Nigerian soybean farmers' cooperatives on sustainable farming techniques, value addition, and market strategies to boost production and income. With Nigeria producing 1.35 million metric tons of soybeans annually and demand exceeding supply by 20%, the initiative will enhance yields, reduce post-harvest losses, and create value-added products, such as soybean oil and flour. By linking farmers to profitable markets, the project promotes food security, rural development, and economic empowerment.
Innovation Description: Nigeria's soybean industry faces significant challenges, including low yields, post-harvest losses, and limited market access, despite a growing demand for soybean products driven by the food and feed industries. Current production of 1.35 million metric tons annually falls short of domestic demand by 20%, creating missed economic opportunities for farmers and food insecurity for the population. The problem is compounded by inadequate knowledge of modern farming techniques, lack of value addition, and poor market integration. Our solution is to train soybean farmers cooperatives on sustainable farming practices, value addition, and market strategies. The training will introduce innovative techniques, such as soil nutrient management, pest control using environmentally friendly methods, and precision farming technologies. Value addition will focus on transforming raw soybeans into high-demand products, including soybean oil, flour, and animal feed, reducing post-harvest losses and increasing profitability. Farmers will also be equipped with marketing strategies to connect with reliable buyers, cooperatives, and regional trade platforms. The innovation leverages insights from agricultural best practices and value chain development studies, demonstrating that education and technical support significantly enhance yields and income. By applying this model, immediate benefits include increased production, reduced waste, and improved farmer incomes. Long-term benefits include enhanced food security, rural economic growth, reduced reliance on imports, and environmental sustainability through eco-friendly farming practices. Consumers gain access to affordable, nutritious products, while society benefits from strengthened local economies and reduced environmental impact.

Long-term benefits encompass reduced child mortality rates, improved public health, and enhanced economic resilience. Environmentally, our approach results in a lower carbon footprint and promotes sustainable agricultural practices.  This innovative approach not only addresses immediate nutritional needs but also fosters long-term sustainability and community empowerment, making a profound impact on society and the environment.

Project Title: Innovative Liquid bio-fertilizers from Black Soldier Fly Larvae: A Sustainable Solution for Agriculture in Kenya
Executive Summary: We rear Black Soldier Fly (BSF) larvae and transform them into organic liquid fertilizers, addressing the inefficiency and unprofitability of selling larvae as animal feed. This innovation will increase BSF farmers' income tenfold while reducing biofertilizer costs for organic farmers by two-thirds. Enriched with nutrients and chitin, our fertilizers enhance plant resistance, reduce organic waste, and provide a sustainable, locally sourced alternative to imports, supporting environmental and economic sustainability for Kenyan farmers.
Innovation Description: We rear Black Soldier Fly (BSF) larvae commercially, producing over 1 ton of larvae monthly. Currently, we sell the larvae as animal feed protein, but this is unprofitable(and is the case for BSF farms of all sizes) due to a poor feed conversion ratio of 1:20 requiring 20 kg of organic waste to produce just 1 kg of dried larvae, with 70 80% of the mass lost during drying. This inefficiency makes BSF farming financially unsustainable despite its potential.  Recognizing a growing demand among Kenyan farmers for organic liquid biofertilizers most of which are imported we shifted our focus to producing fertilizers directly from BSF larvae. This pivot was driven by the unexpected popularity of frass, a solid organic fertilizer and a byproduct of BSF farming, of which we have sold nearly 20 tonnes.  Transforming BSF larvae into liquid fertilizers will increase our income tenfold compared to selling them as feed. These nutrient-rich fertilizers, containing bioactive compounds like chitin, enhance plant resistance to pests and diseases, offering benefits beyond conventional options. They also reduce biofertilizer costs for organic farmers by two-thirds, providing an affordable, locally produced alternative to imports. Additionally, this approach enables an out-grower model, where small-scale farmers supply larvae, increasing their profitability and promoting sustainable livelihoods.  This innovation addresses two critical challenges: reducing organic waste and improving access to high-quality agricultural inputs. By repurposing BSF larvae into liquid fertilizers, we aim to support Kenyan farmers in boosting productivity, promoting environmental and economic sustainability, and creating a scalable, profitable model for BSF farming.

Project Title: Empowering Mukta Haliyas and Nourishing Lives by upgrading the value chain of Turmeric: The Nutritional Powerhouse
Executive Summary: This project empowers Mukta Haliyas (a marginalized community of freed people in Nepal) in Far-Western region of Nepal by developing a sustainable turmeric value chain. We engage Mukta Haliya farmers in organic turmeric cultivation, while a multidisciplinary team conducts research and develops innovative products, including culinary delights, health supplements, and beauty care items. We establish robust domestic and international markets, ensuring fair returns for farmers and promoting the nutritional power of turmeric globally.
Innovation Description: This project aims to innovate by creating a comprehensive and sustainable value chain for turmeric, specifically focusing on empowering Mukta Haliya communities in the Far-Western Region of Nepal. Recognizing the challenges faced by this marginalized community, including limited economic opportunities and social exclusion, this project aims to provide sustainable livelihoods for Mukta Haliya farmers while contributing to improved nutrition and health outcomes due to increased access to and consumption of turmeric-based products. Project Title: YIBIBOA: Empowering Women Through Waste Management and Improving Food Security
Executive Summary: The project tasks itself with providing women in identified households specifically designed containers for collecting their organic waste and set up a system for collecting filled containers. These waste materials will be converted into organic fertilizer using Black Soldier Fly technology. 10% portion of the fertilizer will then be given to the women along with seeds accompanied with best practice training for their backyard gardens.
Innovation Description: Rural areas often grapple with the consequences of inadequate waste management systems. The absence of regular waste collection services leads to widespread improper waste disposal, resulting in severe environmental degradation. This crisis has far-reaching implications for public health, with a direct link to the prevalence of diseases like malaria and dysentery, which disproportionately affect young Africans. Additionally, this contributes to the emission of tons of Greenhouse Gases (GHG), dealing a negative blow to our planet. Moreover, the economic burden of poor waste management is compounded by limited access to fresh food products and increased cost of production, contributing to escalating malnutrition and food insecurity rates in these communities.  With a structured system, we are able to channel the waste being generated in these communities to a central facility where the black soldier fly is used to transform the waste into organic fertilizer, with the larvae as byproduct, enriched in amino acids that can be used for animal and pet feed. Subsequently, 10% of the fertilizer produced is given out to women to set up backyard vegetable gardens, thus augmenting their household nutrition.  With this technology we are able to produce organic fertilizer that not only improves soil health and combats the effects of nutrient depletion but also reduces the amount of methane and CO2 being released into the environment.

Project Title: Resilient Ecosystems and Sustainable Inclusion for Socioeconomic Transformation (RESIST)
Executive Summary: The RESIST project aims to enhance community resilience in Katakwi District through climate-smart agriculture, sustainable livelihoods, and inclusive socioeconomic initiatives. Over three years, it will promote ecosystem restoration, empower marginalized groups, and strengthen local capacities to adapt to climate change. By fostering collaboration and innovation, RESIST will drive sustainable development, reduce poverty, and build a climate-resilient future for the community.
Innovation Description: The project will introduce an innovative, community-driven approach to address the pressing challenges of climate vulnerability, environmental degradation, and socioeconomic exclusion in Katakwi District. katakwi faces erratic weather patterns, reduced agricultural productivity, and limited opportunities for marginalized groups such as youth, women, and persons with disabilities. These challenges threaten livelihoods, food security, and community resilience. RESIST will integrate climate-smart agriculture, ecosystem restoration, and inclusive economic empowerment. Climate-resilient crop varieties, agroforestry systems, and water conservation techniques are employed to enhance productivity and restore degraded lands. Digital inclusion and vocational training equip marginalized groups with skills for alternative livelihoods. Community groups and schools participate in environmental education, fostering long-term stewardship. This solution is rooted in insights from successful community-based adaptation models and technical evidence supporting agroecological practices. For example, agroforestry systems can improve yields by up to 50% in degraded areas (FAO, 2020), while climate-resilient crops can increase food security for vulnerable populations. Immediate Benefits: Increased incomes for farmers, improved food security, and enhanced knowledge of sustainable practices. Sustainable Benefits: Restored ecosystems, stronger climate resilience, and reduced poverty and inequality across communities. RESIST will ensure a scalable and replicable model for building resilient communities and ecosystems in climate-vulnerable regions.

Project Title: How to Produce Aflatoxin-Free Maize and fortified maize flour to Ugandan consumers
Executive Summary: Uganda loses $38 million yearly due to aflatoxin-contaminated grain, which causes liver cancer and child stunting. Agro Supply will introduce ozone technology to remove aflatoxins and access the export market. Agro Supply will also start milling and producing aflatoxin-free nutritious flour fortified with food values like zinc, protein, and vitamins. This will be introduced to local consumers across East African markets.
Innovation Description: Aflatoxin contamination in grain threatens public health in Uganda. Weak interventions have let Aspergillus flavus fungi thrive in the food supply. Tests in Feb 2023 showed aflatoxin levels in sampled grain exceeded the legal limit by 10-100 times. Aflatoxin B1 is a Group 1 Carcinogen, more toxic than tobacco or asbestos. Factors increasing Ugandans' health risks include: 1. Homogeneous Diets - Maize is a staple, providing 45% of calories, and is highly susceptible to aflatoxin. 2. Hepatitis B - The national rate is 8%, and 25% in the Northeast; co-exposure to aflatoxin raises liver cancer risk by 30 times. 3. Smallholder Production - The Uganda Bureau of Standards lacks resources to enforce food safety among 4.7 million farmers. Farmers dry grain on the ground and store it in makeshift structures, favoring aflatoxin growth. 4. Informal Distribution - 70-80% of Ugandan maize sold locally is uninspected. Food safety interventions reflect class inequity; only two mills are certified aflatoxin-free. Rejected grain is sold to lower-income markets. Aflatoxins cause 155,000 liver cancer cases annually in SSA, with 3,700 in Uganda, and stunt 33% of Ugandan children. Trust issues in the agricultural market, such as counterfeit goods and theft, hinder investment in food safety. Solutions must address the lack of trust. Impact: Economic - Producing aflatoxin-free maize boosts East African trade and farmer profits. Health - Safe staple foods contribute to longer lives.

Project Title: AI powered traceability and food impact management tool for food brands and farming businesses
Executive Summary: AgSpeak is an AI driven SaaS platform designed to empower smallholder farmers and food brands by addressing critical gaps in agricultural supply chains. AgSpeak focuses on enhancing supply chain transparency, sustainability, and consumer engagement, providing a comprehensive suite of tools to create a more inclusive, transparent, and sustainable agri-business ecosystem. This supply chain transparency not only enhances trust among consumers but also help businesses optimize their supply chain and reduce food wastage.
Innovation Description: Agricultural businesses and brands contribute to only 8% of total agricultural production of India. This happens because 30% of farm produce is wasted due inefficiency in information arbitrage of demand-supply in agro-trade. Changing food habits post pandemic, conscious consumers and regulations in international food supply chains are posing a challenge for specialty FMCG brands and export trade businesses to create more visibility and trust amongst their customers. One of the primary goals of this initiative is to enhance market access for smallholder farmers, particularly in rural and underserved regions. AgSpeak s platform will enable farmers to showcase their products to a wider audience, reducing their reliance on middlemen and ensuring they receive fair prices. Additionally, the platform will reduce post-harvest losses by 20% by providing real-time data on storage, transportation, and handling, helping farmers optimize the logistics of their produce. This improved supply chain management will enable them to reach markets faster, minimizing waste and maximizing revenue.  AgSpeak has demonstrated financial viability, with projected revenues of INR 30 lakh in the second year of operations, growing to INR 45 lakh by year three. The platform s adaptable pricing structure and expanding user base make it a sustainable business with the potential for significant growth.  Market timing is also right with new policies being framed around food security that mandates that businesses involved in manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding foods maintain records with key data elements by investing into technologies like blockchain and AI that fulfills the purpose of end to end traceability.

In Africa, food waste could feed 300 million people, yet over 200 million face food insecurity, poor soils, and unclean energy. This crisis undermines farmer incomes, perpetuates poverty, and weakens food security. With our solution, we transform organic waste into valuable products like fertilizers and livestock feed for sustainable farming, biodiesel for clean energy, and biopolymers for sustainable packaging, reducing waste, mitigating emissions, and restoring soil health. This creates a sustainable food system, and improves livelihoods while addressing both environmental and social challenges.

Project Title: Enset Cultivation, Development and Utilization in Ethiopia and Kenya - Determining the Impact of Enset on Food Security
Executive Summary: Due to the impacts of climate change, war, and the COVID-19 pandemic, food insecurity has become a dire issue worldwide, highlighting the need for innovative and diverse agricultural solutions that focus on localization and regional collaboration. Our research collaborative project focuses on developing climate-resilient and genetically diverse crops for marginalized and drought-prone regions in Kenya and Ethiopia needing food alternatives. Ensete ventricosum, commonly known as Enset, is a versatile and drought-tolerant crop that can be harvested year-round, withstanding temperature, altitudinal, and rainfall changes. Despite being used as a sustainable food source for approximately 20 million people in Southern Ethiopia, Enset’s potential is under-researched and it remains an underutilized food source.  Our aims include: 1) determining the regional versatility of Enset through analysis of Kenyan and Ethiopian wild Enset strains; 2) analyze and compare domesticated Enset (currently only grown in Ethiopia) and wild Enset to understand how to scale its utilization as a food source; 3) develop advanced agricultural and scientific technologies to establish Enset as a food security crop.

Project Title: Enset Food Security Initiative
Executive Summary: The Enset Food Security Initiative enhances food security in Ethiopia and Kenya by promoting the cultivation of Enset, a drought-resistant crop. Our project focuses on improving agricultural practices, increasing access to this vital food source, and helping communities adapt to climate change. By empowering local farmers, particularly women, our initiative promotes sustainable agriculture, improves nutrition, and strengthens food systems in communities vulnerable to poverty, food insecurity, and climate-related challenges.
Innovation Description: In many parts of Ethiopia and Kenya, food insecurity is a pressing issue, worsened by climate change, which brings erratic rainfall and droughts. Traditional crops are becoming increasingly vulnerable, putting communities at risk of malnutrition and economic instability. Our Enset Food Security Initiative addresses this by promoting the cultivation of Enset, a drought-resistant crop native to Ethiopia. Enset is rich in carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals, and it thrives in harsh climates and degraded soils, making it a resilient solution to climate extremes.  The innovation behind this initiative is scaling up Enset cultivation and integrating it into local food systems. Combining traditional agricultural knowledge with modern techniques, we help farmers increase yields and improve processing methods, ensuring Enset becomes a sustainable food source. This solution is inspired by local agricultural practices but addresses the challenges communities face in expanding Enset cultivation due to limited resources and knowledge.  Our Enset Food Security Initiative is grounded in four principles: regenerative agriculture, promoting biodiversity, empowering smallholder farmers, and introducing climate-smart crops. These principles are essential to positioning Enset as a sustainable, climate-resilient solution to food insecurity. Despite Africa contributing only four percent of global greenhouse gas emissions, the continent is experiencing climate change faster than anywhere else in the world, which is why our initiative focuses on helping communities adapt to these changes.  Immediate benefits include improved food security, increased income, and greater community resilience. Over time, the initiative will foster sustainable agriculture, promote economic growth, and strengthen local food systems.

Project Title: Alnarps Agroecology Farm: a living lab & model farm for the future of our food systems
Executive Summary: The project seeks to develop a sustainable farm model by integrating market gardening, poultry, agroforestry, in CSA scheme. Serving as a living lab, it fosters innovation, research, and practice, to develop a resilient, replicable model for Scandinavia. As a community hub, it invites consumers to connect with their food, the land, and farmers, building stronger relationships and shared responsibility.
Innovation Description: Globally, conventional food systems face multiple crises simultaneously, not limited to global warming, soil degradation, energy crises, low profitability, changing customer awareness and geo-political instability. Policy makers, scientists and activists are urgently calling for novel food production methods to help address these challenges whilst guaranteeing food security, resilience, accessibility, improving dietary health and mitigating climate change. Alnarp s Agroecology Farm (AAF) employs bio intensive market gardening guided by agroecological principles, merging indigenous subsistence farming with modern horticultural methods to prioritize prolonged soil health and fertility. This approach balances nutrient extraction and recycling while fostering multifunctionality within the farm ecosystem, enhancing resilience and environmental sustainability. To ensure social and financial sustainability, AAF uses a Community-Supported Agriculture (CSA) model, enabling customers to directly engage with local food production by financing upcoming seasons and sharing the harvest. CSA fosters community building, food security, and consumer awareness. Contrasting with conventional farming reliant on fossil fuels and synthetic inputs, AAF s methods address issues like soil depletion, biodiversity loss, and disconnection from the land. With modern farming contributing to environmental and social crises, viable alternatives like local vegetable production and agroforestry are critical. Agroforestry integrates trees and crops, offering benefits like improved biodiversity, carbon sequestration, soil health, and resilience. Combining CSA, market gardening, and agroforestry presents a model for circular economies that enhance food security and ecosystem services while addressing socio-economic and environmental challenges.

Project Title: Nutricare by Alunna to prevent anemia in women of childbearing age
Executive Summary: Nutricare by Alunna is a program to reduce anemia among women of childbearing age in Indonesia, addressing its link to increased stunting risks in future generations. Through innovative products like our antioxidant and iron-rich Date Seed Drinks, we empower women to improve their health and well-being. This initiative aims to create a lasting impact by tackling anemia as a key factor in breaking the cycle of malnutrition and promoting healthier families.
Innovation Description: Anemia is a widespread issue among women of childbearing age in Indonesia, with significant health consequences. Anemic women face reduced productivity, impaired cognitive function, and higher risks during pregnancy. Critically, anemia increases the likelihood of stunting in children, perpetuating a cycle of poor health and malnutrition across generations. This issue is highly relevant, as addressing anemia not only improves women's health but also contributes to the nation s development by ensuring healthier future generations.  Nutricare by Alunna offers an innovative solution through its Date Seed Drinks, a functional beverage rich in antioxidants and iron (Fe). This product addresses anemia by improving hemoglobin levels and combating oxidative stress, which is a contributing factor to the condition. Date seeds, a sustainable and underutilized resource, were chosen based on scientific insights into their high iron and antioxidant content, making them an effective yet affordable ingredient for anemia prevention.  The program is designed to provide immediate benefits to consumers by enhancing their health and quality of life. Women gain access to a practical and enjoyable way to meet their nutritional needs, leading to better productivity and well-being. On a larger scale, Nutricare promotes sustainable practices by utilizing date seeds, reducing waste, and encouraging eco-friendly production. Communities benefit from the reduced prevalence of anemia and its associated economic and social costs, fostering a healthier and more prosperous society. Nutricare combines health innovation with sustainability to address anemia effectively and inclusively.

Project Title: Sustainable Hydroponics for Accessible and Regenerative Environment (SHARE)
Executive Summary: SHARE Hydroponics" is a solar-powered, resource-efficient farming system that addresses food security, water scarcity, and sustainability. It recycles up to 90% of water, eliminates chemical pesticides, and uses solar energy, reducing its carbon footprint. With a modular and scalable design, it produces healthy, safe food for farmers, consumers, and communities. This innovation enhances climate resilience, promotes food inclusivity, and fosters environmentally sustainable agricultural practices, making it a vital solution for modern farming challenges.
Innovation Description: SHARE Hydroponics" is a solar-powered, resource-efficient farming system designed to tackle some of humanity s greatest challenges: food insecurity, water scarcity, and environmental degradation. Traditional agriculture is resource-intensive, consuming large amounts of water, energy, and land while contributing to greenhouse gas emissions and environmental damage. As populations grow and resources dwindle, sustainable farming solutions have become critical. This innovation combines hydroponic farming, which replaces soil with nutrient-enriched water, and solar energy to reduce reliance on non-renewable resources. It addresses water scarcity, particularly in arid regions, by recycling up to 90% of the water it uses. Free from harmful pesticides, it produces safe, non-toxic crops while minimizing environmental contamination. By reducing greenhouse gas emissions, SHARE Hydroponics provides an eco-friendly alternative to traditional farming methods. The system is powered by Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA), a scientific approach that precisely optimizes factors like temperature, light, and nutrient delivery. This ensures higher crop quality, increased yields, and reduced resource consumption. SHARE Hydroponics benefits consumers by providing affordable, safe, and healthy food. Farmers gain reduced input costs and higher yields, while unproductive or poor soil regions become viable for cultivation. Schools and communities access fresh produce and gain education in sustainable farming practices. Environmentally, it enhances climate resilience by conserving water, lowering carbon emissions, and promoting regenerative agriculture. By upcycling agricultural byproducts into useful resources, SHARE Hydroponics offers a holistic solution, strengthening sustainability and food security while addressing the needs of a growing global population.

Project Title: Leveraging Bioengineered Microbial Consortia Incorporating Ciliated Protists for Advancing Sustainable Agriculture Practices.
Executive Summary: An innovative biofertilizer combines bacteria (Bacillus subtilis, Pseudomonas fluorescens), fungi (Talaromyces albobiverticillius HNB9), and protozoan ciliates (Sterkiella cavicola, Euplotes affine, Colpoda inflata) to synergistically enhance nutrient availability, stress tolerance, and pathogen suppression. Leveraging natural microbial interactions, it boosts crop yields by 25%, promotes sustainable agriculture, and offers an eco-friendly alternative to chemical fertilizers, supporting soil health and long-term productivity.
Innovation Description: The innovation introduces a groundbreaking biofertilizer that combines bacteria, fungi, and protozoa to revolutionize sustainable agriculture. It addresses the pressing problem of chemical fertilizer overuse, which depletes soil health, reduces biodiversity, and exacerbates climate change. As the demand for eco-friendly solutions grows, this biofertilizer offers a transformative alternative to ensure food security while protecting the environment.  This solution leverages synergistic interactions between its components. Bacteria like Bacillus subtilis and Pseudomonas fluorescens enhance nutrient availability and boost plant resilience. The fungal strain Talaromyces albobiverticillius HNB9 solubilizes minerals like phosphate, zinc, and silica while producing auxins for root growth. Protozoa, such as Sterkiella cavicola and Colpoda inflata, stimulate microbial activity and nutrient cycling by consuming other microorganisms, unlocking vital nutrients for plant uptake. Together, these components amplify the production of plant growth-promoting compounds like indole-3-acetic acid and biofilms. The formulation demonstrates a two- to three-fold yield increase compared to conventional biofertilizers. Farmers benefit from reduced dependence on synthetic fertilizers, improved soil fertility, and higher crop productivity. Environmental benefits include reduced chemical runoff, enhanced microbial diversity, and healthier ecosystems. This scalable, eco-friendly innovation aligns with global sustainable agriculture goals, ensuring long-term economic and ecological stability for farmers, producers, and communities worldwide.

Project Title: Propagation of perennial grain Kernza (a wheat hybrid) through tissue culture and field trials.
Executive Summary: This project aims to propagate Kernza (a wheat hybrid), a perennial grain, using tissue culture techniques and field trials. By producing virus-free, genetically consistent starter plants, it ensures a reliable supply for research and cultivation. Field trials will validate plant performance in diverse conditions.  Leveraging Dr. Abed Choudhury's expertise (a global expert in grain breeding) , the project incorporates insights from rice and wheat prototypes to address food security and promote sustainable agriculture practices.
Innovation Description: Modern agriculture faces pressing challenges such as soil degradation, water scarcity, and climate change. Traditional annual crops exacerbate these issues through intensive farming practices. Kernza, a perennial grain, offers a sustainable alternative with its deep root system that improves soil health, reduces erosion, enhances water retention, and sequesters carbon. However, Kernza s adoption is constrained by the limited availability of high-quality planting materials and inconsistent cultivation practices. Our project addresses these barriers through tissue culture propagation and field trials. Tissue culture enables year-round production of virus-free, genetically consistent Kernza plants, ensuring a reliable supply for researchers and farmers. Field trials will validate the performance of tissue-cultured plants under diverse environmental conditions, providing critical insights for optimal cultivation practices. Immediate benefits include reliable planting materials for researchers and early adopter farmers. Long-term outcomes include improved soil health, reduced environmental degradation, and expanded opportunities for sustainable agriculture. This innovative approach lays the groundwork for broader adoption of Kernza, contributing to global efforts in combating climate change and enhancing food security. This project can be replicated to other regionally suitable areas globally eg. Bangladesh, India, Africa etc.

Project Title: Reducing post-harvest fresh produce loss using green engineered seaweed ingredients and processes
Executive Summary: Atlantic Sea Solutions has developed an edible coating technology to reduce food loss. Our immediate hurdle is field testing this technology which is limited by the small scale of our precision sprayers. We propose to engineer a scaled-up sprayer and test it in a greenhouse to de-risk our technology, validate value propositions, and obtain metrics for impacts of reducing food loss in real-time fresh produce supply chains to help accelerate our journey to commercialization.
Innovation Description: More than one-third of fresh produce is lost before reaching the consumers. This costs the US economy >20 million tons of food and >$40 billion in just one year - tangibly affecting growers and distributors. More than 90% of this lost food material ends up rotting in landfills contributing to about 8% of the total greenhouse gas emissions exacerbating climate crisis. This problem is compounded after considering food waste at consumer level in addition to food loss. Existing approaches to reduce food loss include cold chains, fumigants, synthetic coatings, sophisticated polymer packaging, and gene modifications among others. The material solutions take a major toll on terrestrial material and energy feedstocks such as forestry and farmlands, minerals, and petroleum reserves. We discovered that the seaweed industry is highly underdeveloped in Connecticut with immense growth potential and that seaweed can be a carbon neutral or carbon negative feedstock. We devised green engineering processes to derive seaweed extracts of commercial interest, of which one forms an invisible and flavorless edible coating that can reduce desiccation and spoilage in fresh produce by more than 50% over control. We also devised a precision spray process that minimizes material use to form coatings that can dry >4x faster than conventional coating. Our technology can reduce post-harvest losses to improve the profitability of produce growers, distributors, and improve value for money for consumers, while incentivizing the underutilized seaweed industry with a large and steady demand, removing the onus of sourcing away from dwindling land resources.

Project Title: Biochar from waste biomass for climate resilience in agriculture and carbon removal for climate change mitigation and biodiversity regeneration.
Executive Summary: We propose production and use of biochar from waste biomass, which mostly burns causing carbon emissions and destruction of biodiversity, for use in agriculture as a soil amendment agent to sustainably rebuild soil ecology. This is aimed at increasing the farm productivity and decrease input costs by developing the capacity of soil to retain moisture and nutrients close to the plant roots, and increasing the soil microbial population for a healthy regenerative soil.
Innovation Description: Come summers, forests in the entire sub-Himalayan region become carbon-spewing-factories due to massive forest fires spread by high-calory pine needles that fall during dry summer months, destroying biodiversity, diminishing CO2 draw down capacity of the forests and ground water recharge. Lack of adequate nutrients and ground water, combined with erratic weather patterns, is negatively impacting agriculture.  Our project aims to give economic value to fallen pine needles and agricultural waste/wood and bamboo chips/coffee husk, which farmers traditionally burn, by converting it into biochar and usable electrical/thermal energy. We are using downdraft gasification   specially designed for these low density materials   to produce biochar for soil amendment and carbon removal.  The project is an innovation in  high quality biochar production from such abundantly available waste biomass, a very difficult material to process. The technology of continuous raw material feeding and biochar removal/collection mechanism is unique for converting this difficult to handle biomass into biochar with ease. This innovation also uses the gases produced in the biochar production process, which otherwise are emitted contributing to non-CO2 gas emissions, for production of clean electrical/thermal energy eliminating the non-CO2 emissions harmful for atmosphere and generating additional revenue for the business.   While this conversion of waste biomass regenerates biodiversity and eco-system, use of biochar not only directly benefits the farmers in developing climate resilient agriculture by rebuilding soil ecology, its nutrient-water retention capacity, decreasing farm input costs, and increasing agriculture productivity, but also uses technology to actively remove and store carbon in the soil.

Project Title: Millets For Growth (M4G): Combating Malnutrition through Nutritious and Climate-Resilient Crops
Executive Summary: Baobab Superfoods proposes to help address Rwanda s triple burden of malnutrition stunting (33%), anemia (37%), and micronutrient deficiencies through millet-based fortified foods. Our solution leverages millet, a climate-resilient crop, to create fortified products enriched with essential nutrients, partnering with farmers for sustainable practices, and educating communities on dietary diversity. This approach improves nutrition, boosts farmer incomes, enhances school meal programs, and promotes climate-smart agriculture, supporting Rwandan Government s goal to reduce stunting to 10% by 2030.
Innovation Description: Problem Rwanda faces a triple burden of malnutrition, as highlighted in the National Family and Nutrition Policy 2024. Stunting (33%), anemia (37%), and micronutrient deficiencies are particularly severe among children under five, adolescent girls, and pregnant women. These challenges are partly attributed to sub-optimal minimum acceptable diet rates, which limit dietary diversity and nutrient intake.                                                                                                    Innovation To reduce stunting rates to 10% by 2030, the Rwandan Government emphasizes the "cultivation, supply, and consumption of nutritious foods". Baobab Superfoods leverages millet, a climate-resilient and nutrient-rich crop, to create and distribute fortified products like flours for porridge and pastries.  Our proposed solution focuses on three domains: 1. Fortify Millet-Based Products with:         (a) Iron + Vitamin C + Vitamin B12: To combat anemia.         (b) Zinc + Vitamin A: To support growth and immunity.         (c) Protein + Lysine: To address wasting and improve muscle development.   2. Establish Farmer Partnerships:     Engage small-scale farmers through fair contracts and training in regenerative practices, such as intercropping millet with legumes      to enhance soil health.  3. Do Consumer Awareness Campaigns:          Educate target groups on product use and dietary diversity through direct awareness campaigns and in partnership with frontline          health workers.                                                                                                              Benefits   Consumers gain access to safe, nutritious foods that combat stunting and anemia.   Farmers benefit from improved incomes through sustainable practices.   Schools enhance meal programs, boosting children's nutrition and academic outcomes.   Communities adopt healthier eating habits, reducing malnutrition.   The environment benefits from millet s low ecological footprint, promoting climate-smart agriculture.

Traceability system initiation for empowering farmers, businesses, and consumers. Project Title: Production and distribution of quality and pest control organic fertilizer for farmlands restoration and increased yields across Pob , Benin
Executive Summary: BIO PLANET TMC Ltd increases access to high-quality granulated organic fertilizer for over 18,000 women and indigenous small-scale farmers across Pob , Benin Republic, West Africa, for farmlands restoration and increased crop yields up to 45%, by recycling over 100 tons of biodegradable waste, annually. We want to be part of the solution to save millions of lives, providing an eco-friendly fertilizer to restore over 100,000 degraded farmlands across West Africa by 2030.
Innovation Description: Over 18,640 inhabitants of Pob  are active farmers, 60% as women. Despite the growing food products' market, 80% of these farmers are facing a significant decline in crop yields due to unsustainable farming practices leading to the degradation of 90% of their over 40,000 hectares of farmlands. The cereal production in Pob  from 2020 to 2023 declined by 52%. From 1 hectare, farmers gained 2.2 tons of yields; but today they are down to 0.9.  Research also showed that Pob  is the source of over 100,000 tons of organic waste deposit annually. Nearly 80% of this waste is dumped into the environment, and 20% is burned directly, causing carbon and methane emissions, which pollute the air and damage climate.   We collect this organic waste, process it using environmentally friendly methods to produce high-quality organic fertilizer for farmland restoration. In this way, we reduce atmospheric pollution by 80%, and cut greenhouse gas emissions by 75% in that region.  Till date in Pob , Benin, we have recycled over 100 tons of biodegradable waste, reducing carbon emissions up to 70 tons; delivered over 34 tons of granulated organic fertilizer, increasing crop yields up to 35%, and 20% in 350 farmers' income; contributed to the restoration and biodiversity enrichment of over 100 hectares of farmlands; generated 44 green jobs for rural people, 75% being for women; and improved air quality for over 50,000 residents, with 500 women benefiting from social inclusion.

Project Title: Backyard Farms: Using Lyophilization to Empower Underserved Regenerative Agriculture Farmers to Feed Food Insecure Population in Food Deserts Across New Mexico.
Executive Summary: Backyard Farms leverages lyophilization an advanced freeze-drying technology to combat food insecurity in New Mexico s food deserts. By extending the shelf life of perishable foods while preserving their nutritional value, this innovative solution mitigates logistical challenges faced by underserved communities, particularly Native American tribes and Hispanic populations. Our initiative integrates cultural traditions and local farming practices to provide nutritious, year-round food options. By partnering with small farmers and community organizations we reduce food waste and create markets.
Innovation Description: Enormous amounts of fresh foods are lost between the farm and the consumers in food deserts. This results in large amounts of food waste and food banks and disaster relief organizations stockpiling dried, canned, or frozen foods. This surplus of shelf-stable junk foods are preserved with lots of sugar, salt, or subject to heat in a canning process that destroys the nutrition of these foods.  New Mexico is the largest rural state and suffers socioeconomic conditions that force some to live in conditions that would shock most Americans. The  Colonias  is a region along the southern border with residence routinely living without electricity or running water and similar conditions exist on the Navajo Reservation. Many have to travel 30-60 minutes to buy groceries when summer heat reaches over a 100F, a family can only get as many cold foods as can fit in a cooler. These problems are universal food desert issues that we found a solution using lyophilization (freeze-drying) technology developed by NASA for space travel to transport foods across food deserts!   We have developed a model that can be scaled and used in any state, country, or nation and any ecozone where food can be grown, and hungry people live. This model empowers small local farmers, and preserves 97% of the nutrition of the fresh foods, removes perishability barriers for storage and transport to reduce food waste and get more healthy food back into the food system without extra acres being tilled, water usage, etc.

Project Title: Improve Climate-Resilient Supply Chains for Indigenous Baby Food to Combat Malnutrition and Empower Female Farmers
Executive Summary: Our project aims to fight infant malnutrition by creating a sustainable supply chain for indigenous crops like millet, sorghum, and baobab, used in Baobaby s affordable baby formulas. We will partner with local. female farmers cooperatives to train them in climate-smart agricultural practices and install solar-powered drying and processing units to reduce post-harvest losses and maintain nutritional quality.
Innovation Description: When our co-founder Ida had her baby, she struggled to feed him because she did not have enough breastmilk. The alternatives were milk-based formulas, but they were too expensive and not distributed in underserved areas, such as urban poor and rural regions. This represents the struggle of millions of African mothers, contributing to one in three African babies being stunted. Baobaby's innovative solution is to provide a more sustainable and accessible alternative to milk-based formulas by developing a circular business model. This model sources indigenous crops from local female farmers, transforms these crops into affordable and nutritious baby formulas, and distributes them back into local communities. This project specifically combines climate-smart agriculture and renewable energy technologies. We will train 150 female farmers in sustainable practices tailored to indigenous crops, enhancing their resilience to climate change. Two solar-powered drying and processing units will be installed to reduce post-harvest losses, improve product quality, and preserve the nutritional value of harvested crops. Immediate Benefits:   Female farmers will experience a 50% to 150% increase in productivity and revenue.   We will purchase their crops at fair market prices, transforming them into affordable, nutritious baby formulas.   These formulas will be distributed to 50 new communities, increasing mothers' access to affordable, nutrient-rich baby food and reducing infant malnutrition. Long-Term Impact: The promotion of climate-smart agriculture will empower women, strengthen their role in ensuring food security, and enhance economic resilience in their communities.

Project Title: "Bridging the Climate Gap: Solar Solutions for Resilient Farming"
Executive Summary: Our project, "Bridging the Climate Gap," empowers smallholder farmers to adapt to climate change by providing affordable PAYGO solar irrigation systems and community agricultural solar hubs. These hubs offer rentable Solar Irrigation energy needs, with payments aligned to crop harvest cycles. By improving access to sustainable energy and water solutions, we enhance agricultural productivity, reduce environmental impact, and build climate resilience in rural farming communities.
Innovation Description: Our innovation, "Bridging the Climate Gap," addresses the critical challenge of climate change adaptation for smallholder farmers by providing sustainable, affordable energy and irrigation solutions. Many farmers lack access to reliable irrigation and energy, resulting in low productivity, vulnerability to erratic weather patterns, and increased dependence on unsustainable practices like fossil fuels and over-extraction of groundwater.  We solve this problem through two key solutions:  PAYGO Solar Irrigation Systems   Affordable, pay-as-you-go solar-powered irrigation tailored to farmers' income cycles, ensuring year-round crop production. Community Agricultural Solar Hubs   Centralized hubs offering Solar solutions for rent, enabling farmers to power tools, equipment, and processing activities. Farmers pay for these services after their harvests, aligning costs with their income flow. This solution is based on insights into smallholder farmers' challenges with upfront costs for renewable energy systems, access to irrigation, and energy storage. Advances in solar technology, battery efficiency, and PAYGO financing models make this approach both feasible and scalable.  Benefits:  Immediate: Farmers access affordable energy and irrigation, increasing yields and incomes. Sustainable: Reduced reliance on fossil fuels, enhanced climate resilience, and improved food security. Social: Empowered communities with better livelihoods and more equitable access to technology. Environmental: Promotion of renewable energy and water conservation, reducing carbon footprints. This project not only improves farmers  productivity but also fosters environmental stewardship and community resilience, creating long-term impacts on society and the planet.

Project Title: Optimization, purification and processing of a precision fermentation derived protein based natural sweetener Brazzein.
Executive Summary: Biofect Innovations is revolutionizing the food industry by harnessing the power of microbial precision fermentation technology to produce sustainable, high-value ingredients; starting with Brazzein, a natural, high-intensity sweetener. In order to be adopted by the larger food & beverage industry, it must first be presented in a widely adaptable format such as a powder where it can be easily adapted to various product formulations such as cereals, beverages, and gummies.
Innovation Description: The evolving landscape in dietary habits has consumers closely focusing on packaging labels and ingredients in food and beverages. As a staple ingredient, sugar is the most commonly scrutinized as consumers seek healthier alternatives to reduce the risk of future health complications. This demand has resulted in manufacturers and distributors to search for new sweetener alternatives like sucralose, aspartame, and erythritol. However, these non-caloric sweeteners are not satisfying consumer demands due to recently uncovered health risks associated with consumption.  Brazzein is a potent, natural, and emerging protein-based alternative sweetener that was originally discovered in the West African fruit of Oubli Pentadiplandra brazzeana). Brazzein is reported to be up to 2000x sweeter than sugar (w/w), providing a superior alternative without compromising on taste and health profile. Attempts have been made to commercialize this ingredient using traditional agricultural techniques but have largely remained unsuccessful due to the demanding climate requirements combined with the difficult purification processes involved resulting in a non-existent global supply. Precision fermentation technology differs from traditional fermentation because microbes are engineered to facilitate the conversion of carbon (i.e., sugar) to a specific product (i.e., protein) instead of alcohol. Leveraging this technology allows for sustainable production of ingredients that uses less water, carbon emissions, and land usage compared to traditional agriculture. The immediate benefits to end users is the availability of a novel ingredient that has the potential to reduce the usage of sugar while still maintaining similar sweetness potentials in the food and beverage products we consume.

Project Title: IRIF: Intelligence, Resilience, and Innovative Farming For Africa
Executive Summary: IRIF, an AI-powered platform, is revolutionizing African agriculture by empowering smallholder farmers to adapt to climate change and thrive. Combining real-time data, personalized recommendations delivered via SMS, and market access, IRIF demonstrably increases yields, conserves precious resources, and boosts farmer incomes. IRIF's innovative "pay-on-harvest" model ensures affordability and widespread accessibility, creating a truly sustainable and equitable food system, starting in Ethiopia and poised to impact millions.
Innovation Description: Climate change is devastating African agriculture, impacting millions of smallholder farmers the foundation of the continent s food security. Erratic rainfall, prolonged droughts, and emerging pests and diseases are causing significant crop losses and reduced incomes, exacerbating poverty and hindering economic advancement, especially among young people. Projections paint a grim picture: agricultural productivity could decline by up to 30% in some regions by 2050, and water stress threatens up to 250 million Africans by 2025. In Ethiopia alone, over 90% of farmers are already affected, battling erratic rainfall and devastating crop losses. These challenges hinder access to nutritious food and sustainable practices, impacting the health of both people and the planet. These challenges are compounded by limited access to modern technologies, climate-smart information, and profitable markets.  IRIF (Intelligence, Resilience, Innovative Farming), our AI-powered platform, is transforming this challenge into an opportunity. By combining real-time data, personalized recommendations, and market access, IRIF empowers farmers to adapt to climate change and build a more equitable and regenerative food system. On-farm sensors, satellite imagery, and AI generate tailored advice, optimizing irrigation, predicting pest outbreaks, and guiding crop selection, ultimately increasing yields and incomes. Direct market connections ensure fair prices and build trust with consumers seeking sustainable, locally-sourced food. Our "pay-on-harvest" model makes IRIF accessible and affordable, ensuring widespread adoption and maximizing our impact on nutrition, sustainability, and accessibility within the food system. IRIF is not just adapting to the future of food; it is the future of food, starting in Ethiopia.
