Project Title: Piloting Sustainable Farming Transformation: Enhancing Resilience and Prosperity in India's Agricultural Communities
Executive Summary: This project establishes three food system transformation clusters in Indian state of West Bengal to revolutionize farming practices through natural methods, reducing chemical reliance and promoting sustainability. Engaging 1,050 farmers initially, it aims to enhance crop yields, farmer incomes, and environmental health, while fostering resilience against climate change. By incorporating multidisciplinary expertise, the initiative strives to create scalable models for sustainable agriculture, positioning it as a replicable blueprint for regional and global adaptation.
Innovation Description: The agriculture sector in the Indian state of West Bengal faces significant challenges due to unsustainable farming practices, declining soil fertility, and inequitable market access. These issues exacerbate food insecurity and economic instability among rural communities. Our project aims to transform this situation by integrating natural farming methods, boosting farmer incomes, and fostering climate resilience through comprehensive landscape-level interventions.  The solution is rooted in scientific principles of agroecology and permaculture, emphasizing the reduction of chemical inputs, the enhancement of soil health, and the establishment of fair market linkages. By adopting a block-based approach, the initiative fosters collaboration among communities and stakeholders, optimizing resource management and promoting sustainable agricultural practices.  Immediate benefits include enhanced access to safe and nutritious food through organic production methods, and increased incomes for farmers through reduced input costs and improved market opportunities. Long-term sustainable benefits manifest as better soil health and biodiversity, alongside enhanced community resilience to climate variability. This holistic approach not only invigorates the local economy but also contributes to a more sustainable and resilient global food system, aligning with multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals.

Project Title: Esomchi Nutrition and Economic Empowerment Program (ENEEP)
Executive Summary: Our project combats malnutrition and hidden hunger in Nigeria by promoting biofortified crops like Orange-Fleshed Sweet Potato (OFSP), vitamin A cassava, maize, and iron pearl millet. We produce affordable, nutritious food products for all ages while empowering smallholder farmers, women, and youths through input distribution, climate-smart farming, household farming, food processing, and value addition training. This initiative enhances food security, nutrition, and sustainable livelihoods in local communities, fostering resilience and improved well-being.
Innovation Description: Nigeria faces a severe malnutrition crisis, with 32% of children under five stunted and 2 million suffering from severe acute malnutrition (UNICEF, 2023). The Northern region is most affected, plagued by food scarcity, climate-induced challenges, and poverty. Our Project addresses this urgent crisis by promoting biofortified crops. We produce affordable, nutritious food products for all ages while empowering smallholder farmers, women, and youths through input distribution, climate-smart farming, household farming, food processing, and value addition training. In 2023, we partnered with USAID s Rural Resilience Activity to establish a bakery and processing company in Gombe, producing health-promoting food products. Over 410 farmers across Gombe, Adamawa, and Yobe states have been mobilized to grow biofortified crops. But with the increase rate of malnutrition and rising demand for our products and we aim to expand our initiative across all Northern states in Nigeria which have an estimated population of over 100 million people. By providing the following solutions:   Training additional 3000+ farmers especially women and youth across the Northern region also supporting them with farm inputs.   Increase the number of aggregators and sales agents by 200%.    Train the women farmers on climate-smart agriculture techniques, focusing on the use of biodegradable waste such as household sewage and food waste to generate natural manure and also on household and vertical farming.  Immediate benefits include greater access to nutritious foods, increase job creation and increased incomes for farmers. Long-term, we aim to transform food systems, enhance health outcomes, and build sustainable, empowered communities.

Project Title: Seed-credit project.
Executive Summary: We support smallholder access quality seeds for planting on credit and flexibly pay back after harvest in form of produce. We also support farmer with free trainings on climate smart farming practices, we train farmers also in making green organic manure from agriculture waste.
Innovation Description: Over 65% of the world's arable land is located in Africa and smallholder farmers who contribute over 80% to food production in Africa suffer low yields due to poor quality seeds planted and poor farming practices. The little they harvest being poor quality is bought at low prices since it cannot compete on international standards. This in turn worsens food insecurity, poverty and climate change. Everlend agritech is a B2B digital platform that supports smallholder farmers access quality climate resilient seeds for planting on credit and they flexibly pay in form of produce after harvesting. The platform also acts as an online farmers marketplace hence eliminating middlemen. We have so far served over 2000 farmers who attest to a 65% increased in yields and a 40% increase in household income. We also offer farmers free trainings on best climate smart farming practices like afforestation, cover crop planting, mulching, green manuring and we have so far trained over 5000 farmers reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 12%. We also train farmers in making green organic manure from agriculture waste hence reducing waste pollution while saving farmers money that would have been spent on procurement of manure.

Project Title: Agrocist
Executive Summary: It has been estimated that by the year 2050, antimicrobial resistance will be causing 10 million deaths annually worldwide and this will cost the world 100 trillion dollars. In Nigeria, the high levels of antimicrobial residues in livestock meat/ milk point to antimicrobial abuse in livestock farming as the principal driver of resistance. Agrocist uses technology to  provide farmers access to the needed advisory services to engage in sustainable farming practices and prevent antimicrobial abuse.
Innovation Description: In Sub-saharan Africa, there is a poor access to veterinary extension agents leaving a huge gap in the ways livestock farmers access advisory services for their farm animals. Due to this, most farmers engage in many  poor animal husbandary practices, indiscriminate use of antibiotics, chemicals etc which further result into poor productivity, high mortality and disease outbreaks( 40% loss annually acording to FAO), low profit returns and sales of unhealthy meat/milk products.  we believe that when farmers are equipped with the needed advisory services, these problems can be prevented which is why we are building Agrocist.  Agrocist is a cloud based platform that increases access to veterinary advisory support for livestock farmers ( with initial focus on fish, poultry and pig farmers ). we are building AI agents powered by machine learning to deliver extension services to farmers via phone call, whatsapp, sms and app for easy accessibility, therefore removing the existing barrier. All that a farmer needs is just his/her mobile phone and with or without internet connectivity can  easily access advisory services either by phone call, whatsapp chat or via mobile app

Project Title: Turning legume waste into gold
Executive Summary: FABUMIN transforms aquafaba, a legume processing byproduct, into a versatile egg powder substitute with potential to become a key raw-material in the food industry. Our innovative drying technology creates a sustainable alternative to eggs, which have one of the largest environmental footprints among food ingredients. One-ton of FABUMIN replaces 130,000 eggs, offering identical functionality without compromising taste or texture. This circular economy approach upcycles food waste, reduces water usage, and promotes healthier, sustainable global-food systems.
Innovation Description: The legume industry faces a significant challenge with the daily generation of substantial wastewater, known as aquafaba. This by-product not only burdens sewage systems but also results in the waste of valuable freshwater resources. Concurrently, the egg industry grapples with a multitude of environmental, health, and economic issues that underscore the urgent need for sustainable alternatives. Egg production carries a hefty environmental footprint, consuming considerable water and land while contributing to carbon emissions. A single egg requires 8 liters of water and 20 square meters of land to produce, releasing 170 grams of greenhouse gases. Moreover, the industry contends with food safety concerns, including the risk of salmonella contamination and the growing threat of antibiotic-resistant bacteria due to widespread antibiotic use in poultry farming. Egg allergies, affecting about 20% of food allergy sufferers, further complicate matters, as does price volatility, which hinders effective production planning. Aquafaba, discovered in 2014, has emerged as a promising solution to these challenges. This egg alternative effectively binds, emulsifies, and whips in food production, often outperforming eggs themselves. However, its liquid form and short shelf life have posed logistical challenges for widespread industrial adoption. To address these issues, innovative techniques have been developed to dry legume industry side streams, transforming aquafaba into a new egg replacement ingredient for the food industry. This approach not only provides a sustainable alternative to eggs but also offers a solution to the wastewater problem in legume processing. Project Title: Empowering Regenerative Agriculture: Connecting Farmers and Consumers in Central Kenya
Executive Summary: farmbetter s innovative 3-in-1 digital platform connects farmers, extensionists, and organizations to promote sustainable agriculture. We propose scaling our current pilot marketplace in Central Kenya and collaborating with social media company Wowzi for a consumer campaign to increase demand for organic produce. This project will support farmers to achieve Kenyan Participatory Guarantee System organic certification (KilimoHai), link them to buyers, and drive demand for organic products, fostering sustainable practices, improving farmer livelihoods, and promoting healthier diets.
Innovation Description: Farmbetter s innovative 3-in-1 digital platform is transforming sustainable agriculture by integrating a WhatsApp chatbot for farmers, a mobile app for extension agents, and a dashboard for farmer-facing organizations. This integrated system addresses fragmentation in agricultural tools, enhancing collaboration and efficiency across the sector. The project focuses on bridging the gap in access to safe, nutritious, and organic produce while promoting regenerative farming. In Kenya, the demand for organic produce outpaces supply due to challenges smallholders face in certification and market access. This results in lower farmer incomes and limited availability of healthy food for consumers. Retailers often struggle to source consistent, high-quality, organic-certified produce. We aim to address these challenges by scaling current efforts with farmers in Ciumenene to achieve Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) KilimoHai certification. This certification builds trust in organic farming and connects certified farmers with reliable markets through our expanded marketplace. This connection will boost demand and secure better prices for farmers. The project will also partner with Wowzi to launch social media campaigns, increasing consumer awareness about the benefits of organic produce. These campaigns will promote healthy diets and sustainable farming practices, driving demand. Combining agricultural science, technology, and consumer behavior insights, this initiative benefits both producers and consumers. Farmers gain access to premium markets and higher incomes, while consumers access safer, more nutritious food. Additionally, the project promotes climate-smart, regenerative practices, improving soil health and climate resilience. This initiative will contribute to a sustainable transformation of Kenya s agricultural system by empowering farmers and educating consumers.

Project Title: EARLY CROP PESTS AND DISEASES DETECTION AI-TECHNOLOGY
Executive Summary: Farmer Lifeline uses AI-powered, solar-driven agricultural robots to detect crop pests and diseases early, providing farmers with actionable recommendations via text messages. By increasing yields, reducing losses, and enhancing climate resilience, the technology aims to impact 1 million small-scale farmers by 2030, driving food security and sustainable agriculture.Currently, each robot boast the capability to detect over 12,000+ crop pests and pathogens species within the initial 5 seconds of infestation with an accuracy of 97.5%.
Innovation Description: (1)Globally, delayed detection of crop pests and diseases destroys up to 47% of farm yields each farming season.In Africa alone, pests and diseases destroy farm yields enough to feed 1.2 billion people. (2)In addressing the crop pests and diseases, farmers resort to excessive use of chemicals and fertilizers, emitting 9.8bn tons of GHGs which is 24% of global emissions.  FarmerLifeline developed proprietary solar-powered autonomous agricultural AI-robots (patent No: KE/UM/2023/2015) that are permanently installed in the farmers' fields, equipped with AI-camera scanners that continuously scan crops in the farm, and utilizes Machine Learning and AI algorithms to detect any crop pests or pathogens. Farmers are then promptly notified via text messages in their local language with recommendations of carbon-negative fertilizers and environmentally-friendly pesticides. These recommendations reduce the use of harmful, emission-intensive chemicals and contribute to the reduction of overall greenhouse gas emissions in the agricultural sector. FarmerLifeline has positively impacted over 53,970 small-scale farmers in Kenya.Additionally, over 37,807 acres are now under AI-driven pest and disease surveillance.The devices have detected over 1.7million instances of pests and diseases and provided climate-friendly solution recommendations.  Farmers using FarmerLifeline s devices have saved more than $1.27million in potential crop losses, while increasing yields by $1.39million.Through the adoption of emissions-free inputs recommended by our devices, farmers have collectively reduced CO2 emissions by over 111,000 metric-tons, equivalent to emissions from 13,700 passenger vehicles.  The company was honored with the UN-FAO Achievement Scroll and the Kenya's Presidential Innovation Award by Kenya's president H.E William Ruto. Project Title: "Empowering Youth and Communities through Sustainable Poultry Farming in Burkina Faso"
Executive Summary: We empower vulnerable youth in Burkina Faso with solar egg incubators, fertilized eggs, training, and starter kits to create sustainable micro-enterprises in poultry farming. Our initiative reduces chick production costs by 30%, enhances food security by improving access to affordable protein, and addresses unemployment and climate challenges. By fostering resilience, boosting incomes, and promoting environmental sustainability, the project transforms lives and creates a scalable model for economic empowerment in communities affected by poverty and instability.
Innovation Description: Faso Elevage offers an innovative solution to youth unemployment, high poultry production costs, and food insecurity in Burkina Faso. Our approach combines solar-powered egg incubators with an inclusive model targeting vulnerable and at-risk youth, particularly those displaced by terrorism in the Sahel region.  Traditional poultry farming relies on costly, energy-intensive incubation methods, limiting access to affordable chicks and protein-rich food. Faso Elevage will disrupt this cycle by equipping 50 displaced and vulnerable youth with solar incubators and access to fertilized eggs, enabling them to become independent distributors of affordable chicks nationwide. These solar incubators cut carbon emissions by 70%, reduce reliance on expensive energy sources, and make poultry farming accessible and sustainable.  We train youth in sustainable poultry practices and provide starter kits, empowering them to launch micro-enterprises and meet the growing local demand for chicks. Immediate benefits include increased incomes for youth entrepreneurs, a 30% reduction in chick prices, and improved household access to affordable protein.  In the long term, the project enhances food security, promotes environmental sustainability through reduced carbon footprints, and offers a scalable model for economic empowerment. Communities experience reduced poverty and greater resilience, while farmers and consumers gain affordable, essential resources. Faso Elevage addresses critical societal challenges with innovation, inclusivity, and sustainability, transforming lives and fostering development in a region deeply affected by poverty and instability.

Project Title: Food Rescue Network: Bridging Waste and Nourishment in Communities
Executive Summary: Feed Louisville rescues surplus food destined for waste and transforms it into hot, nutrient-dense meals for food-insecure individuals and families. By collaborating with local farmers, restaurants, and food producers, we tackle both food insecurity and food waste. Our innovation bridges the gap between surplus food and those in need, creating a sustainable system that feeds thousands while reducing environmental harm.  Our goal with this project is to further expand our work regionally and nationally.
Innovation Description: The dual crises of food waste and food insecurity are pressing global issues. In the United States, up to 40% of food is wasted annually, contributing to greenhouse gas emissions, while millions face hunger daily. Louisville, KY, mirrors this national problem, with food insecurity rates exceeding 15%. Simultaneously, food producers and retailers discard vast quantities of perfectly edible food due to surplus or aesthetic imperfections.  Feed Louisville provides an innovative, community-centered solution by rescuing surplus food and repurposing it into nutritious, ready-to-eat meals. Collaborating with local farmers, restaurants, caterers, and food distributors, we intercept edible food before it becomes waste. Using our mobile kitchens and community kitchens, we create and distribute meals directly to vulnerable populations, including the homeless and food-insecure families.  This approach solves multiple problems: it reduces food waste, addresses hunger, and fosters community resilience. By diverting food from landfills, Feed Louisville lowers methane emissions and promotes environmental sustainability. For local food producers, it offers a sustainable alternative to food disposal, turning surplus into a tool for social good. For recipients, it provides dignity and nourishment, offering a lifeline to those most in need.  Our model is scalable and replicable, providing a sustainable framework for tackling food insecurity and waste in other communities, bridging the gap between food surplus and food scarcity while advancing environmental stewardship.

One small act of good is a catalyst for change and has far-reaching effects. A neighbor, now nourished, may be a better neighbor to another, a better partner. A better parent. Everyone is deserving of the nourishment we all need to succeed. Our Food Bank is just one way to help support those who do not have the same opportunities to succeed that many of us in urban areas or affluent families are afforded.

Project Title: Feeding Communities Together - Sustainable Food Systems, Engaging the most Marginalized Communities
Executive Summary: Foodbank Botswana Trust plans to address the critical issue of food waste and food loss while providing essential nourishment to individuals and families in need. Our organization plans to leverage the power of WhatsApp, a widely accessible and user-friendly messaging app, to connect retail operators, distributors, farmers, individuals, and beneficiaries, facilitating seamless food pickups and distributions. With our comprehensive system, we aim to maximize the efficiency of food utilization and foster a culture of sharing.
Innovation Description: To address the critical issue of food waste and loss while providing essential nourishment to individuals and families in need.  This will be achieved by connecting surplus food providers with households and organizations. Redistribution of surplus food to vulnerable communities will improve both household food security and nutrition status. Sustainability is going to be promoted by reducing the environmental impact associated with food waste. Local community centers, charitable organizations, and individuals in need will be required to register for the project for them to receive food packages. The beneficiaries will have enhanced physical and economic access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food that meets their dietary needs because they will be utilizing an easy-to-use social media application (WhatsApp), to access and receive free nutritious food packages.  According to FAO, approximately one-third of all food produced for human consumption is lost or wasted each year. Meanwhile, millions of people suffer from hunger and malnutrition. FBBT bridges this gap by redirecting surplus food to those who need it most, utilizing the power of WhatsApp to streamline the process. Project Title: Ownership Innovation: Strengthening Seeding The Future s Innovation Areas with Perpetual Purpose Trusts for Scaled Impact
Executive Summary: This project empowers mission-driven food and farm businesses to adopt Perpetual Purpose Trusts (PPTs), a groundbreaking ownership model ensuring long-term alignment with regenerative practices, nutritious food production, and conscious consumer choice. Through targeted training, resources, and assessments, we equip consultants and businesses to prioritize mission over profit, fostering a sustainable and innovative food system.
Innovation Description: Mission-driven food and farm businesses are essential to advancing innovation in IFT s focus areas. However, traditional ownership structures prioritize shareholder returns over everything else, dramatically limiting scalability of regenerative outcomes. We need alternative ownership structures that prioritize mission over shareholder returns.          Perpetual Purpose Trusts (PPTs) offer an innovative solution. By replacing human owners with a trust governed by a stakeholder committee, PPTs legally ensure financial resources advance mission-driven goals over profit extraction. This structure secures the long-term viability of businesses advancing regenerative practices, producing naturally nutritious products, and expanding conscious consumer choice.   Despite their potential, consultants and entrepreneurs lack awareness and expertise to guide the adoption of PPTs. This project will address this gap by:   1-Building awareness through established consultant networks.   2-Providing skill-building in structural, legal, and financial aspects unique to PPTs.   3-Offering readiness assessments for businesses interested in adopting this model.    This strategy will prepare more farmers, entrepreneurs, and consultants aligned with IFT s three focus areas to understand PPTs and implement this structure, ensuring their missions thrive in perpetuity.   Project lead, Food Finance Institute (FFI), has supported food and farm entrepreneurs by training over 460 consultants and 1500 entrepreneurs. In 2025-2026, FFI will train 100+ new consultants, host a regional conference, and provide extensive learning resources. FFI will collaborate with Purpose Trust Partners for PPT expertise and content creation. By leveraging these assets, this project will create a scalable pathway to empower food and farm businesses to continue innovating in IFT s focus areas while ensuring their long-term viability.

Project Title: Farm2Veteran Meal Program & Agribusiness Empowerment Initiative
Executive Summary: Our solution addresses food insecurity and nutritional deficits among veterans in food deserts by providing nutritious, farm-fresh meals from our 60-acre farm, which employs sustainable practices. We donate 100% of food to veterans and purchase additional produce from local BIPOC and veteran-owned farms. Additionally, we empower communities through education on food systems, nutrition, sustainable farming, and agricultural careers, fostering long-term food security and economic mobility.
Innovation Description: Farm2Veteran's Meal Program, Workforce Development, and Counseling Services Initiatives aims to increase veterans access to nutritious food, create viable career pathways for veterans, and address the mental and physical health issues that create barriers for acquiring stable employment in the veteran population. Veterans face a critical lack of access to nutritious food, being nearly twice as likely as the general population to experience food insecurity. Veterans encounter distinct workforce development challenges due to their unique experiences, skills, and needs. They face higher unemployment and underemployment rates compared to the general population, often struggling to translate military skills into civilian job qualifications. This disconnect can hinder their job search and career transition. Additionally, service-related disabilities and mental health issues like PTSD can impact job performance and well- being.  Our solution aims to address the specific food insecurity and nutritional deficit challenges faced by Veterans living amidst food deserts in marginalized communities across the country. Project Title: Beyond the Bean: Promoting Sustainability and Food Security in Coffee Farming
Executive Summary: This project aims to enhance food security and promotes sustainable agriculture in coffee-growing communities. By producing biochar and cultivating nutrient-rich beans and corn, the project improves soil fertility, boosts agricultural productivity, and enhances local diets. This integrated approach fosters regenerative agriculture and ensures access to safe and nutritious food.
Innovation Description: This project focuses: 1. Rotating Community Biochar: Coffee plant residues and pulp generated during coffee processing will be transformed into biochar, a valuable soil amendment. Biochar improves soil quality, enhances water retention, and contributes to carbon capture. The implementation of rotating community biochar systems will ensure equitable and efficient access to this technology for multiple coffee-growing communities. This approach maximizes the benefits of biochar while promoting collaboration and resource sharing.    2. Food Security with Bean and Corn Seeds: The project will promote the cultivation of local bean and corn varieties with high nitrogen fixation capacity. These crops improve soil fertility, reduce the need for chemical fertilizers, and ensure the sustainable production of staple foods, enhancing local diets and nutrition. Studies by Cenicaf  highlight the benefits of these crops in increasing agricultural productivity and promoting sustainable farming practices. Innovation and Benefits Integrating biochar with bean and corn cultivation creates a circular model of sustainable agriculture. This innovative approach transforms coffee waste into valuable resources, enriching the soil and enhancing productivity. By combining technical knowledge in carbon management, crop rotation, and climate-smart agriculture, the project promotes a holistic and sustainable approach to coffee farming. Sustainable Impact In the short term, farmers will benefit from more fertile soils, increased yields, and equitable access to innovative technologies. In the long term, the project will strengthen climate resilience, enhance food security, and promote environmental sustainability. This integrated approach will reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve livelihoods, and enhance the overall quality of life in coffee-growing regions.

Project Title: Ocean Growing of Asparagopsis in South Korea
Executive Summary: We seek to complete a pilot project to conduct ocean-growing of Asparagopsis in South Korea.   Asparagopsis seaweed reduces methane emissions and increases livestock productivity. This makes beef and dairy farming more economical and environmentally sustainable. Asparagopsis grows naturally in many locations including South Korea. To begin scaling production to feed cattle and reduce methane emissions, Asparagopsis will need to be grown commercially in locations with good conditions such as South Korea.
Innovation Description: One of the biggest climate change issues is the methane emissions from agriculture. Livestock, produce about 12% of total global greenhouse gases, with a large amount of those being from enteric emissions due to microbes that make methane in the cows first stomach, the rumen.  Asparagopsis, a type of red seaweed found around the world, contains bio-actives that disrupt this methane production. FutureFeed has created a solution where a small amount of Asparagopsis (less than 1% of total feed) is added to ruminant livestock diets. Scientific studies have shown this can reduce methane emissions by greater than 80% in certain settings.  By stopping methane production, the energy saved is used more efficiently by the animal, improving feed conversion efficiency (FCE) by up to 7% as per recent published scientific studies. This means animals grow better on the same amount of food.  Asparagopsis is safe for animals, with no negative effects on their digestion. Meat and dairy products from these animals are also safe for humans, with no changes in quality or taste.  In addition, the commercial production of Asparagopsis will enable a seaweed species to be farmed for a purpose, enabling marine and aquaculture industries. This will drive employment and development of coastal communities to grow and produce this climate-changing feed additive.

Project Title: G-Green: Enhancing Biodynamic Vegetable Farming through Cooperatives in Northern Nigeria
Executive Summary: Our project will establish biodynamic vegetable farming for carrots, cabbages, and potatoes in Northern Nigeria, utilizing a cooperative model to empower local farmers. The cooperative will enhance resource-sharing, provide access to training, equipment, and markets, and improve productivity through collective decision-making. By integrating sustainable farming practices, the initiative will boost soil health, increase yields, and promote economic resilience, benefiting both the environment and the community.
Innovation Description: The ongoing farmers-herders conflict in northern Nigeria has significantly disrupted agricultural productivity, food security, and community cohesion. This conflict arises from competition particularly over arable land and grazing areas, exacerbated by climate change and unsustainable farming practices. Traditional farming systems often deplete soil nutrients, further aggravating land scarcity and community tensions. Our project introduces biodynamic vegetable farming as an innovative solution to these challenges. Biodynamic farming integrates organic methods with ecological and spiritual principles, emphasizing soil regeneration, water conservation, and diversified cropping. By adopting this approach, farmers can enhance soil fertility and maximize land use efficiency, reducing the pressure for expansion into grazing territories.  This solution is relevant because it offers a practical pathway to sustainable agriculture while addressing underlying resource-based conflicts. Training programs and workshops will equip farmers with the knowledge and tools to transition to biodynamic methods. Farmers will also learn to collaborate with herders on land-sharing arrangements, fostering peaceful coexistence and mutual benefit. Immediate benefits include improved crop yields, reduced dependency on chemical inputs, and strengthened community resilience. Over time, the initiative will promote environmental regeneration, restore degraded lands, and create stable livelihoods, reducing conflict triggers. For consumers and society, the availability of chemical-free, nutrient-rich vegetables enhances public health, while the environmental benefits contribute to climate change mitigation.

Project Title: Scaregrow: Transforming Farming with AI and IoT for Climate Resilience and Food Security
Executive Summary: At Green Eden Farms, we develop technology to empower smallholder farmers with climate-smart solutions. Our flagship product, Scaregrow, is an AI-powered farm management platform using IoT sensors to deliver real-time insights on soil health, weather, and crop conditions. Scaregrow helps farmers make data-driven decisions, reduce resource waste, and improve climate resilience. Tested in Nigeria with support from the African Development Bank (AFD), it has impacted over 100 farmers and seeks to scale for greater reach.
Innovation Description: Agricultural productivity in sub-Saharan Africa is heavily impacted by erratic weather, water scarcity, degraded soils, and inefficient farming practices. Smallholder farmers, who contribute over 80% of agricultural production in the region, face significant challenges that result in annual losses exceeding $10 billion, according to the FAO. These losses are driven by pest outbreaks, poor resource utilization, and climate variability. Compounding the problem is the limited access to agronomic and weather data, which leaves farmers vulnerable and food systems unstable.  At Green Eden Farms, we have developed Scaregrow, an AI-powered farm management system designed to address these critical issues. Scaregrow integrates IoT sensors with AI-driven analytics to provide real-time insights on soil health, moisture levels, weather patterns, and crop conditions. Farmers can access this data through a user-friendly mobile application, empowering them with actionable advice on irrigation scheduling, pest control, and resource optimization. This solution is tailored specifically for Nigerian farmers, building on insights from global agricultural innovations like Microsoft s FarmBeats and CGIAR s Big Data Platform. Its solar-powered sensors ensure accessibility in off-grid regions, overcoming energy limitations.  Scaregrow has demonstrated immediate benefits for farmers, including increased crop yields, reduced water usage, and significant cost savings. By optimizing farming practices, it also reduces greenhouse gas emissions and builds resilience against climate change. Supported by the African Development Bank, Scaregrow has already positively impacted over 100+ farmers in Nigeria. With a clear pathway to scale, it has the potential to transform agricultural systems and empower millions of farmers across Africa..

Project Title: Gawad Kalinga s Food Productivity Hubs: Building Sustainable, Food-Secure, and Healthy Filipino Communities
Executive Summary: Gawad Kalinga s Food Productivity Hubs are regional hubs that centralize and harmonize multiple interventions for food security, health, and sustainability, all of which contribute to achieving zero poverty, zero hunger, and net zero carbon in Filipino communities in a three to five year timeframe. The productivity hubs are strategically located in regions with high incidence of poverty and hunger, and are primarily led by community members, mission workers, and young leaders from the region.
Innovation Description: Half of the Filipino population is food-poor, and the nation s food producers, farmers and fisherfolk, are the hungriest. In a country where hunger and food insecurity are pervasive, there is an urgent need to empower communities to be food productive, collectively working towards a community-based solution promoting sustainable food production practices and improving community health.  GK s food productivity hubs harmonize multiple initiatives targeting food security, health, and livelihood.  The hub begins with an economic model called BayanAnihan, translated as  community harvest , where farmers are organized to plant a crop whose production is directly invested in by the market buyer, and where the farmers share in equity and profit. Alongside this, GK establishes a community food farm program, where young farm organizers from GK s agricultural school, SEED Philippines, teach mothers and children to plant organic vegetables for consumption or sale. Vegetables harvested from the farms are cooked into nutritious meals for a central community kitchen, which provides nutrition supplementation to children and pregnant mothers. Finally, youth from the community are sent to study agri-entrepreneurship at SEED Philippines to be able to sustain the gains of the community. All of these initiatives work in harmony to achieve sustainable, food-secure, and healthy Filipino communities.  The productivity hubs that GK has established in two Philippine provinces so far have proved its capacity to transform the lives of Filipino families, who now earn a better living, produce their own food, and live healthier lives.

Project Title: NEGLECTED AND UNDER-UTILIZED SPECIES  CULINARY INNOVATION THROUGH THE GFM KITCHEN (NUS-CI)
Executive Summary: The Kitchen by Ghana Food Movement (GFM)  is a food education hub equipped with a Training Kitchen, Food Innovation Lab and Urban Demo Farm to train and empower actors in the food sector. Through the NUS-CI program, the kitchen by GFM aims to: Enhance the biodiversity of 1000 cocoa farmers  through the cultivation of NUS  by 2027 and Improve the Nutrition of 200,000 School children through the inclusion of NUS ingredients in school diet.
Innovation Description: Enhancing food security and climate resilience in Ghana requires developing the Neglected and Underutilized Species (NUS) value chain. NUS crops, such as cocoyam, plantain, tiger nuts, taro, jute mallow, are nutrient-rich, drought-tolerant, and pest-resistant, but their potential is still unrealized due to a lack of awareness, insufficient investment, and poor integration into agricultural policies. With 22.6% of Ghanaian households experiencing food insecurity (World Food Programme, 2022), promoting NUS crops through improved cultivation and culinary innovation will diversify diets, and improve rural livelihoods. The NUS-CI program stands out as it bridges the gap between farmers and offtakers, facilitating to connect increased supply of NUS ingredients with schools and households and influencing growing consumption of NUS ingredients. The main objective is more nutritious meals with local ingredients on the plates of school children and increased incomes for farmers. To achieve this, we use a multifaceted approach of technical skills training for 1000 cocoa farmers in sustainable cultivation of NUS ingredients, culinary skills training of Matrons of schools in NUS ingredients recipe development in areas such as developing meat substitutes or plant-based milk and creating consumer awareness on NUS ingredients and its health benefits. In our pilot program, the Kitchen by GFM trained over 150 NUS farmers to integrate NUS crops in their cocoa farms in 2 communities in the Eastern Region of Ghana (Adawso and Bawjiase).

Project Title: IMMERSE: Integrated Multisectoral Model for Enhancing Resilience in Shock-prone Environments
Executive Summary: This project seeks to improve the availability, affordability, and desirability of nutritious, sustainable foods during climate-related shocks by integrating private-sector value chain actors into sub-national shock early-warning and response systems. The initiative leverages innovative AI technology and multi-sectoral coordination, building on ongoing work to improve shock response in collaboration with county governments and value chain partners. The project will create a scalable model for enhancing nutrition and climate resilience in vulnerable communities.
Innovation Description: The State of the Climate in Africa 2022 report shows that over 110 million people in Africa were directly affected by weather, climate, and water-related hazards in 2022, resulting in more than $8.5 billion in economic damages. Climate-related shocks are increasing in both magnitude and frequency year-on-year (Richardson, K et al., 2022). The immediate and medium-term impacts of climate shocks disproportionately affect the most vulnerable and marginalised communities. In Kenya, the growing frequency and magnitude of climate-related shocks puts local administrators under increased pressure to maintain nutrition security and climate resilience. Bringing the private sector into these systems will help governments relieve this pressure, and constitutes a clear win-win for food system resilience: this approach ensures that social protection systems can deliver timely support to shock-affected communities, and also supports local food enterprises to stay profitable and adapt to evolving market conditions during shocks. GAIN s ongoing work to engage private sector actors in sub-national early warning systems in Kenya has generated compelling evidence that engaging the private sector in these systems is feasible, scalable, and that it can make food systems more resilient to shocks. In this project, we aim to capitalise on our existing successes to reinforce and scale a public-private partnership model for shock-responsive social protection, which integrates artificial intelligence (AI) technology, consumer insights, and private-sector mobilization.

Project Title: Empowering Communities for Sustainable, Equitable, Ecological, and Diverse Food Systems through Seed Sovereignty (ECOSEEDS Project)
Executive Summary: The ECOSEEDS Project intends to transform the landscape of agroecology and regenerative  systems by restoring the tradition of farmers saving their own seeds. The dominant  agro-industrial model has led to the loss of traditional agricultural practices and local seed  varieties. Seed sovereignty as an innovative approach and seeks to promote a sustainable,  equitable, and diverse seed system that empowers farmers, conserves biodiversity, and  fosters resilient and nutritious food systems. We have two main strategies, Participatory Seed  Governance (PSG) and Farmer-Consumer Hubs.    The ECOSEED Project revitalizes traditional knowledge and farming practices by granting  seeds back to the farmers to save, use, exchange, and propagate. This approach is unique  and disruptive to the prevailing industrialized agriculture model that resulted in monocultures  and the erosion of biodiversity. Through the seed-saving communities, seed production  centers, seed entrepreneurship, and farmer-consumer hubs, the ECOSEEDS project will  foster knowledge-sharing and empower communities to become stewards of their agricultural  heritage. By increasing access to diverse locally adapted seed varieties, communities will  have a reliable source of nutritionally rich crops, reducing vulnerability to food shortages and  malnutrition. No seeds, no farmer, no food, no future.

Project Title: Seeding Community Power for Sustainable, Equitable, and Diverse Food Systems and Policies (Seeding Power)
Executive Summary: Seeding Power leverages local partnerships between government units, smallholder farmers and academia to promote seed sovereignty as an innovative approach to address food insecurity and the impacts of climate change. Seed sovereignty promotes sustainable, equitable seed systems that strengthens Filipino smallholder farmers, conserves biodiversity, and advances resilient, nutritious food systems. Seeding Power establishes new seed saving communities (SSCs), creates seed policies that transform the seed system, and ensures resilient seed libraries.
Innovation Description: Problem: The Philippines is the most climate vulnerable country in the world, experiencing up to 20 typhoons per year, numerous floodings and droughts and additional impacts of slow on-set climate change. These impacts place the Philippines in a critical agricultural biodiversity and climate crisis that threatens food security and economic growth of small-scale farmers. Further catalyzing these threats, corporate control of seeds and current policies challenge the livelihood of farmers.  Solution/Innovation: To combat climate change and strengthen farmers, Seeding Power s model develops a resilient seed system supported by a network of seed libraries and local seed policies that promote long-term agricultural sustainability. Furthermore, Seeding Power focuses on its innovative approach of seed sovereignty and the traditional practice of saving open-pollinated varieties (OPVs). GSS utilizes local insight, seed sovereignty and OPVs as a solution because it provides a multifaceted approach to climate changes, systemic barriers and food insecurity.   Benefits: OPVs and seed sovereignty provide wide-ranging benefits, impacting those most vulnerable: ● Economic wellbeing of farmers. OPVs increase yields for small-holder farmers and help plants withstand climate disasters. Additionally, local seed policies encourage farmers to save and replant their own OPVs, making them less dependent on commercial seeds.  ● Enhanced food security for communities. OPVs help reduce climate-related disruptions in the supply chain and create opportunities for more diverse, locally accessed nutritious food. ● Environment. The wider genetic diversity of OPVs result in increased biodiversity and plants that are adapted to their specific growing conditions and naturally resistant to pests and diseases.

Project Title: Transforming Institutional Food Systems Through Scalable Meatless Monday China Initiatives
Executive Summary: The Meatless Monday China Institutional Dining Transformation Initiative engages institutions to reduce meat consumption through interactive workshops, chef training, and behavioral nudges. By fostering plant-based dietary shifts, the project promotes sustainable, nutritious, and affordable food systems. This scalable model will drive meaningful reductions in meat consumption, empower institutions to adopt sustainable practices, and establish a framework for broader implementation, aligning with IFT s mission of advancing innovative food systems.
Innovation Description: Rapidly increasing meat consumption in China has led to significant challenges. In 2020, urban residents consumed 58.3% more meat than recommended by dietary guidelines, contributing to chronic health issues 88.5% of deaths in China are linked to chronic diseases. Additionally, China s vast geography and diverse culinary traditions make it difficult for a single dietary guideline to be universally effective. Tailored, region-specific approaches are needed to drive meaningful dietary change.  Historically, efforts to educate consumers on food literacy have focused primarily on raising awareness. However, to shift consumption patterns, individuals require actionable guidance and practical tools to integrate sustainable practices into daily life.  The Meatless Monday China Institutional Dining Transformation Initiative offers a solution by addressing these gaps. Through interactive workshops, chef training, and behavioral nudges, the initiative empowers institutions to implement plant-based dietary practices tailored to local preferences. Workshops combine gamified activities and hands-on meal design to make dietary recommendations tangible and accessible, while chef training equips culinary teams to create appealing, regionally appropriate plant-based menus. Behavioral nudges like Meatless Monday offer simple, actionable steps for gradual yet impactful change.  This approach not only reduces meat consumption but also promotes healthier diets, lowers the environmental footprint, and aligns with local dietary traditions. By bridging the gap between awareness and action, the initiative provides a scalable and sustainable model to address the interconnected challenges of health, culture, and environmental sustainability.

Project Title: Promotion of Biofortified Grains to Reduce Malnutrition and Improve Food System
Executive Summary: The project promotes bio-fortified grains, Iron Pearl Millet (IPM) and Zinc Wheat (ZW), as a sustainable solution to combat malnutrition and enhance food systems in Uttar Pradesh. By engaging 100 farmers in nutrition-smart, climate-resilient practices, it aims to improve grain production and livelihoods. Additionally, 200 school children will benefit from bio-fortified meals, fostering better health outcomes and demonstrating scalable, impactful solutions for nutrition security and sustainable agriculture.
Innovation Description: The innovation centers on the promotion of bio-fortified grains, Iron Pearl Millet (IPM) and Zinc Wheat (ZW), to address hidden hunger caused by micronutrient deficiencies, particularly iron and zinc. This problem is critical in India, where anemia and stunted growth impact millions, especially women and children. Malnutrition weakens immunity, hampers cognitive development, and perpetuates poverty.  Bio-fortified grains offer a sustainable and innovative solution by enriching staple crops with essential micronutrients. The project introduces nutrition-smart and climate-resilient agronomic practices to improve grain production, engaging 100 farmers, SHGs, and FPCs in Uttar Pradesh. Scientific advancements in biofortification, combined with improved farming techniques, ensure these grains thrive even in challenging climatic conditions.  The benefits are multifaceted and immediate. For farmers, bio-fortified grains enhance yields, improve soil health, and increase market value, ensuring sustainable livelihoods. Schools and communities benefit from healthier, well-nourished children, improving cognitive development and school attendance. Governments and producers gain from reduced healthcare costs and a more resilient food system. Societal gains include better public health and economic stability.  Environmentally, bio-fortified grains reduce the need for synthetic supplements and fertilizers, promoting eco-friendly farming. The project also aligns with climate-resilient goals, ensuring sustainable food security amidst changing climatic patterns.  By addressing malnutrition and empowering farmers with innovative practices, the initiative delivers lasting health, economic, and environmental benefits to communities and society at large.

Project Title: Reducing Stunting through Community Empowerment in Southwest Papua, Championing the Exploration and Education of Endemic Food Sources
Executive Summary: This project addresses stunting in Southwest Papua (30%+ rates) by educating communities on the nutritional value of endemic plants like moringa and purslane. Through sustainable processing tools, a Food Lab prototype, and community activation, it improves diets, food security, and livelihoods. By promoting biodiversity, strengthening local food systems, and fostering sustainable practices, this initiative provides a scalable solution to malnutrition, reducing stunting while enhancing health and resilience in vulnerable communities.
Innovation Description: Southwest Papua faces stunting rates exceeding 30%, significantly higher than Indonesia s national average, driven by limited access to affordable, nutritious food and the underutilization of local nutrient-rich plants such as purslane (Portulaca oleracea) and moringa (Moringa oleifera). Communities lack the knowledge and tools to incorporate these plants into their diets, while reliance on nonlocal staples like rice worsens malnutrition and food insecurity, displacing traditional, nutrient-dense diets.  This initiative empowers local communities through education, capacity-building, and the establishment of a prototype Food Lab. It identifies and trains key stakeholders mothers, youth, and educators on the nutritional value, processing techniques, and culinary uses of underutilized wild plants. By leveraging insights from nutritional science, the program positions these endemic plants as affordable, sustainable superfoods.  The program delivers immediate benefits, including improved dietary diversity and reduced stunting rates, alongside enhanced community knowledge and self-reliance in using local food resources. In the long term, it preserves biodiversity through sustainable use of native plants, strengthens local food systems to reduce dependence on external food, and supports small-scale farmers by integrating wild plants into value-added products.  By addressing immediate nutritional needs and fostering long-term resilience, this initiative aligns with sustainable food system goals. Utilizing local resources, promoting community engagement, and advocating sustainable practices, it creates a scalable model to combat malnutrition in similar regions globally. This holistic approach ensures health, food security, and economic opportunities for vulnerable communities.

Project Title: ASALs Smart Nursery
Executive Summary: The ASAL Tree Planting Initiative promotes food security through agroforestry by planting indigenous trees and integrating sustainable farming practices in arid and semi-arid regions. By using greenhouses and technology to boost tree survival rates, the project creates jobs, enhances biodiversity, and supports local communities with shade, soil improvement, and resources for crops and livestock.

In these regions, harsh climatic conditions, limited water, and pest infestations hinder tree growth, threatening food security and environmental stability. Our innovative approach involves using solar energy to power water-saving irrigation systems, temperature and humidity sensors, and greenhouse operations. These technologies create optimal growing conditions for seedlings, reduce water wastage, and protect young trees from extreme weather and pests. By enhancing tree survival rates, the initiative ensures the establishment of robust agroforestry systems. This solution is rooted in scientific understanding of plant growth requirements and the adaptation of renewable energy for sustainable agriculture. Solar energy is both affordable and accessible, making it ideal for resource-constrained regions. The benefits are significant and far-reaching. Farmers and communities gain resilient agroforestry systems that improve soil fertility, increase crop yields, and provide shade and fodder for livestock. Schools and local groups benefit from training opportunities and environmental education. Society at large experiences improved food security, economic opportunities, and reduced carbon emissions. The environment benefits from enhanced biodiversity and restoration of degraded ecosystems. By increasing tree survival rates through solar-powered technology, this innovation creates a sustainable, scalable solution to agroforestry challenges in ASAL, promoting resilience and long-term prosperity.

Project Title: Scaling Sustainable Cool Chain Solutions in Kenya
Executive Summary: In this project we plan to scale up existing activity in Kenya from one delivery truck to a small delivery line of four trucks. This activity has been supported by the IFC and conducted in collaboration with a local distributor, Farm to Feed. We also plan to integrate one solar cooling container to be stationed in rural environment, demonstrating horizontal and vertical scalability of our sustainable cool chain solutions for developing countries.
Innovation Description: The cold chain industry is crucial for delivering fresh, nutritious food, yet it faces two major challenges: Food Losses: In developing countries, up to 50% of fresh produce spoils due to inadequate cold chain infrastructure. This not only limits access to affordable, healthy food but also impacts farmers' livelihoods. GHG Emissions: Cold chains account for 3-4% of global greenhouse gas emissions, primarily due to their reliance on fossil-based energy. Additionally, food spoilage contributes 8-10% of global emissions through methane release and wasted resources.   GreenTech s innovative solar cooling solutions are designed to provide reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable cooling options. These include community cooling hubs, portable cooling units, and transport refrigeration solutions. Our solutions are specifically tailored to serve rural and remote areas with limited electricity and infrastructure, helping extend the shelf life of fresh produce, reduce food waste, and improve access to healthy, nutritious food for consumers. At the same time, our approach significantly reduces the environmental impact of both food losses and cooling operations.   This strategy benefits farmers by lowering post-harvest losses, strengthens communities through increased food availability, and supports consumers with more affordable, nutritious produce. Environmentally, it reduces emissions from refrigeration and food waste, while enhancing resilience against climate change. This innovation not only provides immediate savings by reducing spoilage and energy consumption but also contributes to building long-term, sustainable food systems that support livelihoods, promote healthy diets, and protect the planet.

Project Title: The Green Menu Movement: Plant-forward Menus for Global Health and Sustainability
Executive Summary: Greener by Default (GBD) plans to expand our Plant-forward Menu Program across the globe, improving healthy diets and outcomes for individuals and communities, increasing access to nutritious, healthy food options for consumer choice, and promoting sustainable practices that reduce institutions  carbon footprints and benefit the environment.

Plant-forward diets are a critical part of the solution to ensuring the wellbeing of people and the planet, but transforming the way people eat is a big lift. The recent slump in US plant-based meat sales shows that simply adding options is not enough to shift consumer behavior.  Choice architecture - organizing the decision-making environment to lower the barriers to making sustainable choices - is one of the most effective ways to create widespread behavioral change. Making plant-based foods the easiest and most appealing option for all diners, not just vegetarians, drives down demand for industrial meat production and normalizes plant-based eating, while offering options to meet everyone s needs.  By promoting nutritious, plant-forward menus at trusted, wide-reaching institutions, Greener by Default drives transformative food systems change, advancing powerful health and environmental outcomes at scale. Through this work, we are generating a meaningful impact that will have a multiplier effect, promoting healthy diets, sustainable practices, and an empowered consumer base throughout the world.

Executive Summary: Grenoh Food Lab is a biotech company focused on producing sustainable, affordable cocoa substitutes and biofertilizers using microbial fermentation technology. By utilizing oil palm leaves and halal-certified microorganisms, we reduce environmental impact using 90% less water and 80% less electricity than traditional cocoa farming. Our innovative products are eco-friendly, cost-effective, and scalable, offering a unique solution for the food and agriculture industries while promoting sustainability and ethical practices.
Innovation Description: Grenoh Food Lab s innovation lies in producing a sustainable cocoa substitute and biofertilizer using microbial fermentation technology. The primary problem it addresses is the environmental and ethical challenges of traditional cocoa farming, including deforestation, excessive water and energy use, and unsustainable agricultural practices. Additionally, there is increasing demand for affordable, halal-certified food products. By using oil palm leaves an underutilized and abundant resource and halal-certified microorganisms, Grenoh reduces the reliance on traditional cocoa farming, which consumes significant land, water, and electricity. The fermentation process produces a high-quality cocoa substitute in just 7 days, requiring 90% less water and 80% less electricity compared to conventional methods. The process also yields biofertilizer as a byproduct, offering a natural, eco-friendly alternative to chemical fertilizers. This innovation is grounded in microbial fermentation science, which efficiently converts organic materials like palm leaves into valuable products. The technical insight stems from optimizing fermentation techniques to produce a cost-effective and scalable solution, while maintaining the desired flavor and functionality of traditional cocoa. Project Title: Advancing Agroecology and Soil Health for Resilient Farming Communities in South Asia
Executive Summary: Through our Farmer-Centered Soil Biology Action-Research Initiative, we will implement mutual learning, testing, and scaling of agroecological principles and practices for regenerating soil fertility with our South Asian member organizations in Nepal and India. These principles will be studied in comparison to conventional agricultural techniques. The lead NGOs involved are: 1) BBP Pariwar and 2) Rural Women s Upliftment Association (RWUA) in Nepal, and 3) Preservation and Proliferation of Rural Resources and Nature (PRAN) in India.
Innovation Description: With our regional and global staff and member NGOs, we will facilitate cross-country coordination to strengthen 20  champion farmers  in three villages in each of the South Asian countries.  We will achieve this through intensive exchange visits, training, and experimentation, impacting approximately 10,000 farmers during a pilot phase. These farmers will serve as key actors for spreading effective, context-specific practices through farmer-to-farmer networks. The research will involve the contextual assessment of different proven natural farming principles and practices in different parts of Nepal and India. The program will focus on regenerating soil biology, fertility, and carbon sequestration using low-cost, low-input techniques such as low, and no-tillage, and increased crop and tree diversity. These practices are easily adaptable and scalable, offering a sustainable alternative to chemical fertilizers, which are harmful to soil and water health and increasingly expensive. Our approach emphasizes farmer-led research, where farmers test, adapt, and spread regenerative practices within their local ecosystems. This process integrates traditional knowledge with proven techniques, ensuring that practices are both effective and widely accepted.  By strengthening farmers' capacity for experimentation, innovation, and decision-making, the program builds local social change processes based on farmers' needs and goals. The project aims to accelerate agroecology learning, foster south-south collaboration, and scale regenerative practices in participating countries. Ultimately, this approach empowers farmers to drive their own sustainable agricultural transformation, replacing external inputs with local, contextually appropriate solutions.

Project Title: "Bee the Change: Ghana s Cashew & Honey Impact Project"
Executive Summary: Our project empowers smallholder cashew growers and women beekeepers in Ghana by improving pollination through bee feed supplements, increasing cashew yields and honey production. Through locally produced nutritious cashews and honey, this sustainable solution increases farmers' income, improves access to a healthy diet, promotes better food diversity, nutritional security for local communities, and creates jobs for rural women. By strengthening bee colonies, we promote climate-resilient farming.
Innovation Description: Our innovation addresses a critical challenge in global food security: the decline in bee populations due to environmental stressors such as climate change, pesticide exposure, and habitat loss, which reduces crop yields and threatens smallholder farmers' livelihoods.  We offer a comprehensive pollination solution, combining our bee feed supplement with professional agricultural and beekeeping consultancy. The supplement strengthens bees colonies, making them more resilient to stress and effective in pollination. This results in higher crop yields, better quality produce, and increased farmer income. Our technical support and training programs ensure farmers can integrate pollination strategies effectively, maximizing impact.  The scientific insight behind our solution is that stronger bee colonies lead to better pollination performance. Trials in apples, onion seeds, and coffee have shown yield improvement up to 40%  The immediate benefits include higher yields for smallholder farmers, increased honey production, and improved biodiversity. In the long term, the project supports food security, nutrition improvement, job creation for women beekeepers, and sustainable farming practices. We also see potential for impact beyond farms, including schools and community centers, by promoting pollination education programs and establishing small-scale beekeeping initiatives. These efforts can enhance local food diversity, improve nutrition through daily balanced diets, and empower communities to integrate sustainable, climate-resilient agricultural practices.  In Ghana, our focus on cashew farmers and women-led beekeeping addresses both economic and nutritional needs, helping vulnerable communities build climate-resilient livelihoods while enhancing access to healthy, local food sources.

Project Title: Tiny feed ,big impact
Executive Summary: Harcourt Farm empowers farmers by converting organic waste into valuable resources using black soldier flies. This process produces high-quality, affordable animal protein and frass fertilizer, enhancing livestock health and crop yields. By promoting sustainable practices, Harcourt Farm ensures food security, reduces hunger, and supports One Health for crops, animals, humans, and the environment. Their innovative approach fosters a balanced ecosystem and contributes to the prosperity of communities.
Innovation Description: Problem Statement: In Kenya, the reliance on imported protein sources for animal feeds has led to high costs and compromised quality. This situation negatively impacts the affordability and nutritional value of animal feeds, posing a challenge for farmers. Additionally, the extensive use of inorganic fertilizers has degraded soil health, resulting in poor crop yields and financial losses for farmers. When farmers cannot produce quality feed, there is no food security and nutrition, leading to hunger. The lack of proper waste disposal systems further exacerbates the issue, as organic waste accumulates in landfills, producing methane gas and contributing to greenhouse gas emissions.   Solution Statement: Harcourt Agri Eco Farm Limited addresses these challenges by utilizing black soldier flies to convert organic waste into valuable resources. By producing high-quality, affordable animal protein, Harcourt ensures that animal feeds are both nutritious and cost-effective. The farm also generates frass fertilizer, which repairs and enriches the soil, leading to improved crop yields and increased profitability for farmers ensuring farmers are producing quality and healthy food. Furthermore, Harcourt's waste collection and conversion process reduces the environmental impact of organic waste, mitigating methane emissions and promoting a sustainable ecosystem. Through these innovative practices, Harcourt Agri Eco Farm Limited supports the health and prosperity of both farmers and the environment and ensures food nutrition and security.

Project Title: Regenerative Food Systems For Planetary Health: Scaling Insect Farming To Sustain The Manombo Rainforest Of Madagascar
Executive Summary: HIH collaborates with rainforest communities to reverse deforestation and enhance livelihoods through scalable, community-driven solutions. Our Black Soldier Fly (BSF) farming project, supported by rigorous research and community-based pilots, addresses food security, regenerative agriculture, and reforestation. Insect frass fertilizer improves crop yields and seedling survival, while behavioral studies highlight the growing acceptance of insect-based foods. Field trials validate BSF farming s feasibility, empowering smallholder farmers and contributing to sustainability, biodiversity conservation, and a climate-resilient future.
Innovation Description: Rainforests, vital for planetary health, face destruction due to unsustainable farming and economic pressures on local communities. These communities, disproportionately affected by climate change, often lack access to sustainable agricultural resources and funding. Health In Harmony addresses this by integrating innovative, community-driven solutions. Black Soldier Fly (BSF) frass as an organic fertilizer has shown the ability to enhance vegetable yields and seedling survival rates for agriculture and reforestation efforts compared to traditional cattle manure. Minimal doses of BSF frass improve crop productivity, reduce dependence on cattle manure and chemical fertilizers, while promoting ecological restoration. By providing high-quality health care, communities no longer needed to extract resources from the forest to pay for it. Instead, they became partners in forest conservation by establishing a non-cash payment system with seeds and seedlings, as showcased by Jones et al., 2020. Food systems became responsible for turning communities that relied on slash-and-burn agriculture and bush meat into active partners in protecting and recovering tropical forests, promoting food security, and reducing spillover risks, as shown by Huntington et al., 2024. Recently, WHO and IUCN also spotlighted HIH's successes in using agriculture to connect human health and biodiversity conservation in Madagascar (WHO-IUCN, 2024).  By investing in locally relevant, scalable solutions like frass-based fertilizers and reforestation initiatives, Health In Harmony collaborates with communities to protect their rainforests while improving food security. This holistic approach, rooted in Indigenous knowledge and data-driven insights, ensures immediate benefits like increased agricultural productivity and long-term impact through climate resilience and biodiversity conservation.

Project Title: One Egg Closer
Executive Summary: In Rwanda 33% of children are stunted, most of them are from rural areas, and with families below the poverty level We aim to bring fresh eggs, egg nutrition education, and cooking demos closer to them at affordable prices, in addition, we aim to produce whole egg powder to increase the variety of feeding the egg. Innovation Description: Our innovation addresses the critical issue of child stunting in Rwanda, where 33% of children are affected (RDHS 2020), primarily in rural and low-income areas. Poor access to affordable, nutrient-rich foods like eggs exacerbates this problem. We aim to bring fresh, affordable eggs closer to remote and vulnerable families, particularly those with at-risk children to improve their nutrition. By establishing local egg kiosks and delivering them directly to these communities, we ensure accessibility and promote consistent egg consumption. Additionally, we plan to introduce whole egg powder, providing a shelf-stable, versatile option to diversify egg consumption for households, schools, and community programs. Our approach combines affordable pricing, nutrition education, and cooking demonstrations to empower families with knowledge and tools to improve dietary habits. This innovation improves the high nutritional value of eggs, addressing protein and micronutrient deficiencies that contribute to stunting. Immediate benefits include improved child nutrition, better dietary practices, and enhanced food security in vulnerable communities. In the long term, this initiative supports healthier generations, reduces stunting rates, and empowers local economies through job creation. The environment also benefits from reduced food waste due to whole egg powder production, ensuring the nutritional value of eggs reaches more people. By bridging the gap between egg producers and underserved families, we create a sustainable model to fight malnutrition and promote health equity in Rwanda's 2 most districts with high rates of malnutrition which are Nyabihu and Burera districts.

Project Title: Home Chocolat Mass-Production Readiness
Executive Summary: Home Chocolat empowers consumers to create personalized, high-quality chocolate at home with regenerative cacao kits, innovative tools, and engaging content. This award will enable us to finalize The Chocolatier appliance for mass production and develop compelling marketing materials to secure funding for its launch. By combining sustainability, creativity, and convenience, this project will transform at-home chocolate-making into a customizable, healthier, eco-conscious experience, fostering a deeper connection to food and empowering mindful consumption.
Innovation Description: Home Chocolat addresses the lack of personalization, transparency, and sustainability in traditional chocolate production. Conventional chocolate is mass-produced, often containing additives and processed ingredients, while its supply chain faces significant ethical and environmental challenges, including deforestation, child labor, and lack of transparency in indirect sourcing. This system disconnects consumers from the chocolate-making process, limiting their awareness and engagement.  Our innovation, the patented CocoaBlox kits, and The Chocolatier appliance, empower consumers to create high-quality chocolate tailored to their preferences using regenerative cacao and clean ingredients. Each CocoaBlox is a single ingredient processed in cocoa butter, designed for easy melting and mixing. Paired with The Chocolatier appliance, this system simplifies the traditionally complex process, providing a seamless, professional-grade chocolate-making experience at home.  This solution is based on the insight that breaking chocolate-making into manageable, high-quality natural components can empower consumers while addressing sustainability. By shifting the final stages of production to the consumer s home, we reduce the environmental impact of large-scale processing and transportation, while engaging the consumers.  Immediate benefits include healthier, customizable chocolate, with consumers controlling ingredients to meet dietary needs. Schools and communities gain educational opportunities in sustainability and chocolate-making, while farmers benefit from the promotion of regenerative cacao, encouraging eco-friendly practices.  In the long term, Home Chocolat fosters sustainable consumption, reduces environmental impact, and connects consumers to the artistry of their food, transforming chocolate into a conscious, creative, and sustainable experience.

Project Title: AQUAPONICS ACCELERATED: A model to transform global systems for nutritious food security and sustainable livelihoods in marginalised communities in South Africa and beyond
Executive Summary: INMED Aquaponics Social Enterprise is a hub-and-spokes network of physical and virtual sites which mentor farmers from established INMED Aquaponics  systems and learning centers in schools and universities. This initiative is supported by a production, consolidation, and training hub, along with satellite farmers, and offers real-time support through web- and app-based platforms. Building on INMED's expertise in climate-smart aquaponics, the initiative empowers vulnerable communities including individuals with disabilities, women, and youth, helping them achieve food security.
Innovation Description: Although often argued to be the least contributor of greenhouse gas emissions, the Southern Africa region is one of the most affected regions by climate calamities which causes serious drawbacks in these thriving economies including unpredictable rainfall patterns, prolonged droughts, and declining soil fertility threatening food security. These challenges make traditional farming methods less viable, especially in regions where water is scarce and arable land is limited. In response to these growing pressures, aquaponics offers a sustainable solution that could revolutionise food production in these vulnerable areas. Aquaponics combines fish farming with soil-less plant cultivation in a closed-loop system, where fish-waste provides nutrients for plants, and plants naturally filter and purify the water for the fish. This method uses up to 90% less water than traditional farming, making it especially relevant for water-scarce regions. It also doesn t rely on soil, enabling farming in areas with degraded land. This innovation solves the twin problems of water scarcity and food insecurity by creating a highly efficient, eco-friendly farming system. The scientific principle behind aquaponics is based on the natural symbiosis of ecosystems, where organisms support each other's growth. The technical insight lies in applying this balance to a controlled, productive environment. For farmers, aquaponics provides an opportunity to grow food year-round with fewer resources. Consumers benefit from fresh, locally sourced produce and fish, while schools and communities use aquaponics as a tool for education and empowerment. Overall, aquaponics contributes to long-term sustainability, resilience, and food security in the face of climate change.
