Project Title: Savanna Flours: From Nature to Nourishment
Executive Summary: This project transforms Mozambique s underutilized native resources, canhu nuts and wild green bananas, into sustainable, gluten-free flours with high nutritional value. By addressing food security, generating income for rural women, and promoting environmental conservation through sustainable practices, it fosters economic empowerment while aligning with multiple Sustainable Development Goals. Through scalable production, strategic market integration, and active community engagement, it offers a replicable, impactful model for inclusive, sustainable development and improved livelihoods across Mozambique and beyond
Innovation Description: Mozambique faces a multifaceted challenge encompassing food insecurity, economic reliance on imported wheat flour, and environmental degradation. Despite the abundance of canhu nuts and wild green bananas, over 95% of these resources are discarded, representing a significant loss of nutritional and economic potential. This untapped opportunity exacerbates the country's vulnerability to food shortages and perpetuates dependency on expensive imports.  This project offers an innovative solution by transforming these underutilized native resources into high-value, gluten-free alternative flours. Canhu nut flour is rich in proteins, healthy fats, and fiber, while wild green banana flour provides resistant starch, a key component for digestive health. Together, these flours enhance dietary diversity, providing affordable and nutrient-rich food options that address local dietary deficiencies and reduce Mozambique s reliance on imported wheat flour.  The initiative also integrates sustainable harvesting and scalable production methods to ensure environmental conservation and climate resilience. Training local communities in resource management and establishing cooperatives fosters equitable participation in the value chain, creating stable income opportunities, particularly for women and youth. By reducing food waste and conserving biodiversity, the project promotes a circular economy while contributing to the country s Sustainable Development Goals.  In addition to its local impact, this project lays the foundation for broader socioeconomic benefits. Through community engagement, market integration, and replicable practices, it not only addresses Mozambique s immediate challenges but also positions the country as a model for sustainable development, ensuring long-term environmental, economic, and social resilience.

It delivers site & crop-specific farm analytics to the farmers mostly using digital channels to improve their agronomy. The engine also tracks the farmers  activity and facilitates targeted lead generation, and direct farmer-linkage for our B2B partners, increasing profitability for all, which eventually ensures food security. Reduced carbon emissions and lower soil degradations are the by-products of our solution. Project Title: Innovation in kombucha production: microbiological strategies and optimization of productive variables for a quality drink
Executive Summary: One of the ferments that has achieved the most popularity in recent decades is kombucha, a non-alcoholic fermented drink that is obtained from a sugary tea infusion fermented by a culture of yeasts and bacteria. In its production process, certain factors such as time, substrate, oxygen, and composition of the microbial inoculum influence the final characteristics of the drink. Currently, kombucha is consumed throughout the world. In our country, the number of producers grows day by day, with more than 20 ventures. The first study of commercial Argentine kombucha production was carried out by CRELTEC, showing great physicochemical, microbiological and sensory variability. Taking into account the characteristics of this drink in terms of its microbial diversity and the variables that influence its production, obtaining a stable and balanced kombucha in terms of acidity with low alcohol content, and sensorially attractive is a challenge. The general objective of this project is to deepen the study of different aspects of kombucha science as well as strengthen the link between the scientific sector and kombucha producers in Argentina. Experimental kombuchas will be developed with microorganisms isolated from Argentine kombuchas seeking to minimize the concentration of ethanol; and the contribution of these microorganisms to the physicochemical and sensory characteristics of kombucha will be studied. In addition, a production method will be developed with a commercial inoculum that allows reducing the alcohol content of kombuchas. On the other hand, the stability of kombuchas in consecutive fermentations will be studied and different methods of conservation of the starter inocula will be evaluated. To this end, experimental fermentations, microbiological, physical-chemical, and sensory analyzes will be carried out. The results obtained will allow the production of kombuchas with low alcohol content, as well as delve into the study of microorganisms, fermentation variables, conservation of inocula and stability of this fermented drink.

Our solution identifies and mitigates key risks, such as extreme rainfall events, prolonged dry spells, and erratic temperature patterns. These insights, delivered through digital platforms, empower farmers with real-time guidance on planting schedules, water management, and pest control strategies. The benefits are immediate and far-reaching. Farmers gain resilience to climate variability, improve yields, and reduce losses. Over time, this fosters sustainable agricultural practices, strengthens food security, and safeguards livelihoods. Additionally, by reducing food production's environmental footprint, Ignitia contributes to planetary health. Grounded in advanced data analytics and validated by on-ground impact, our innovation translates complex climate data into accessible, actionable advice. This empowers millions of smallholder farmers to thrive amidst climate uncertainties, transforming vulnerable communities into resilient contributors to the global food system.

Executive Summary: The AXES program facilitates market access for Colombian agrifood MSMEs producing sustainable, nutritious, and affordable innovations. AXES addresses structural barriers and promotes deforestation-free supply chains, enhances rural incomes, and builds climate-smart capacities. Through tailored coaching, ecosystem collaboration, and capacity-building, the project ensures 30 MSMEs in scaling their impact, improving livelihoods for rural communities, youth, and women, while fostering resilience and contributing to sustainable food systems.
Innovation Description: Colombian agri food MSMEs face challenges that interfere with their growth and integration into sustainable food systems. While MSMEs represent 99.6% of firms in the country, they contribute only 5% of export value [1]. Compliance with international regulations poses additional barriers, particularly for MSMEs lacking technical capacity to adopt traceability and deforestation-free practices [2]. Moreover, financial access remains limited, with only 10% of MSMEs able to secure formal credit, restricting investment in infrastructure, innovation, and sustainable production [1]. Knowledge gaps exacerbate these issues, as most MSMEs lack expertise in regenerative agriculture further limiting their competitiveness [3]. Additionally, Colombia loses 174,000 hectares of forest annually, largely driven by unsustainable agricultural expansion [4]. Fragmented supply chains and weak market linkages isolate MSMEs, increasing transaction costs and reducing their ability to meet consumer and international market demands [2]. Addressing these challenges is critical to fostering resilient, competitive, and sustainable food systems in the country. The AXES program facilitates market access for agrofood MSMEs, promoting sustainable, nutritious, and affordable innovations. The program specifically supports 30 MSMEs by addressing structural barriers through activities such as capacity-building workshops, personalized coaching, and ecosystem activations. These interventions focus on deforestation-free, climate-smart practices, regenerative agriculture, and traceability systems that comply with EUDR (European Union Deforestation Regulation) standards and meet global market demands. The program emphasizes creating sustainable value chains, fostering investments, and enhancing MSME competitiveness. Immediate outcomes include generating 240 new jobs and boosting rural incomes, while long-term impacts focus on building resilient food systems and ensuring equitable opportunities.

Project Title: NourishNative - Reviving Traditional Diets for a Sustainable Future
Executive Summary: NourishNative is a community-driven initiative by Indigikitchen aimed at promoting healthier diets, environmental sustainability, and informed consumer choices. Innovation Description: The modern food system has led to a disconnect between people and their ancestral food traditions, contributing to poor health outcomes, environmental degradation, and unsustainable consumer choices. In many Indigenous communities, the consumption of traditional, nutrient-dense foods has declined, replaced by processed, unhealthy diets that contribute to chronic health issues like obesity, diabetes, and heart disease. At the same time, industrial agriculture and food systems are depleting natural resources, fostering biodiversity loss, and increasing carbon footprints. Consumers, in general, lack of education on traditional food practices and their sustainable benefits which further exacerbates issues related to diet and sustainability.  1. These foods are often nutrient-rich, locally sourced, and environmentally sustainable.  2. Promoting Sustainable Agriculture Practices NourishNative will partner with Indigenous farmers and food producers who practice sustainable, regenerative farming methods. These partnerships help build local food systems, reduce the carbon footprint associated with transporting food, and promote biodiversity. By supporting Indigenous farming techniques, the project ensures the preservation of natural resources and the continuation of time-tested ecological practices.  3. Raising Consumer Awareness: By showing the link between traditional diets and sustainable ecosystems, the project will encourage consumers to make informed decisions that benefit both their health and the planet.  4. Project Title: Promoting a Home-Centered Circular Food System to Ensure Affordability, Accessibility, and Sustainability of Animal Feeds in Rwanda.
Executive Summary: Indintambwe Feeds is a Rwandan-based social enterprise revolutionizing livestock farming by commercializing black soldier fly larvae over the last 4 years and offering seven insect-based feeds to 14,500 smallholder farmers. Now, we plan to train farmers to grow black soldier fly larvae themselves, ensuring a consistent maggot supply for our feed production. Our cost-effective, nutrient-rich solution is 30% cheaper and 50% more nutritious than conventional feeds, boosting productivity and incomes of livestock farmers.
Innovation Description: In Rwanda, agriculture is the backbone of the economy, employing over 70% of the population. However, livestock farming critical for food security and rural livelihoods is underperforming due to the lack of access to affordable, high-quality animal feeds. Over 8 million livestock farmers depend on feed for their animals, yet 6 million remain underserved due to high costs, inconsistent supply, and poor feed quality. This gap contributes to low livestock productivity, reduced farmer income, and persistent rural poverty.   Currently, the animal feed market is dominated by imported feeds, which are costly and often inaccessible for smallholder farmers. Moreover, local feed production primarily relies on traditional ingredients like maize and soybeans, which are not only expensive but also contribute to competition with human food consumption. This results in a market where small-scale livestock farmers are unable to achieve optimal yields or profitability, limiting their ability to invest in better farming practices. Indintambwe Feeds Ltd is addressing the twin challenges of inaccessibility and high costs of quality animal feeds for small-scale farmers, by leveraging black soldier fly larvae to produce insect-based feeds that are 30% cheaper and 50% more nutritious than traditional options.   By leveraging insect-based feed technology, we provide an innovative solution that is:  Affordable and accessible: Our feeds are 30% cheaper than traditional options.  Nutrient-rich: 50% more nutritious feed products, improving livestock growth and productivity.  Sustainable: Utilizing locally sourced black soldier fly larvae, we reduce reliance on conventional feed ingredients, alleviating environmental pressure and ensuring a consistent supply.

Project Title: Development of Community-Supported Agriculture Based on Multi-stakeholder Cooperative with Millennial Farmer as an Actor
Executive Summary: The development of Community-Supported Agriculture (CSA) through multi-stakeholder cooperatives integrates millennial farmers as key actors. This model fosters collaboration among producers, consumers, and other stakeholders, ensuring shared responsibilities and benefits. Millennials bring innovation, digital proficiency, and sustainability focus, revitalizing agricultural practices. By connecting directly with communities, CSA enhances food security, supports local economies, and promotes eco-friendly farming. Multi-stakeholder governance ensures inclusivity, making the model resilient and adaptable to evolving societal and environmental needs.
Innovation Description: Traditional agricultural models face declining engagement from younger generations, leading to aging farmer populations and a lack of innovation in farming practices. Community-Supported Agriculture (CSA) often struggles with scalability, limited stakeholder engagement, and fragmented supply chains. Consumers demand transparency, sustainability, and locally-sourced produce, yet current systems lack effective collaboration between farmers, consumers, and supporting entities. Millennial farmers, equipped with digital skills and a sustainability mindset, are underutilized due to limited access to resources and networks. Without a comprehensive approach to integrate diverse stakeholders, agriculture risks losing its capacity to address food security, economic resilience, and environmental sustainability challenges effectively.    A multi-stakeholder cooperative-based CSA offers a transformative solution, uniting farmers, consumers, and enablers in a shared governance model. Millennial farmers take center stage, leveraging their digital expertise to modernize operations and improve transparency. The cooperative framework ensures equitable decision-making, resource sharing, and financial sustainability. Digital platforms enable direct consumer engagement, strengthening trust and demand for locally-sourced, sustainable products. By integrating diverse stakeholders, the model enhances scalability and resilience, addressing supply chain gaps and promoting eco-friendly practices. This approach revitalizes agriculture, empowers younger generations, and aligns with contemporary demands for sustainability, collaboration, and community-driven solutions, ensuring long-term agricultural and societal benefits.

Project Title: My F&V: Navigate Your Way to Healthy Food Environments
Executive Summary: My F&V is a system designed to enhance access to diverse quality fruits&vegetables (F&V) while supporting local value chain actors. It helps users navigate food environments, track and locate F&V sources, especially mobile vendors. The system records supply-demand flow to optimize value chain efficiency. With personalized consumption goals, healthy diet information, and a reward system, it motivates healthier habits among adolescents and encourages vendors to sell quality produce, ensuring sustained F&V availability and economic benefits.
Innovation Description: F&V are components of a healthy diet and contribute to overall health. However, their consumption remains low among any population group in the Philippines. Our recent project and study confirmed poor dietary diversity due to low F&V intake among consumers, particularly adolescents. High F&V prices, supply chain issues, accessibility problems, and consumers' general lack of knowledge of the benefits of F&V are the key barriers to encouraging increased consumption.   My F&V addresses these challenges by offering an innovative, user-centered solution. My F&V is a mobile app with Google Maps-like interface that visualizes the food environment of F&V in real-time, distinguishing between static sources (e.g., permanent market stalls) and dynamic sources (e.g., mobile hawkers, rolling stores). By integrating real-time tracking and local F&V data, the platform enables consumers to locate vendors, track routes, and plan purchases effectively toward their "F&V consumption goals". This means My F&V is also planning tool designed to empower consumers to meet regular (e.g. weekly) F&V consumption targets in line with personalized dietary goals, with reward systems and motivating interface with accurate nutrition and dietary information.   The system will involve F&V vendors, vendors association and local government units, who regularly update the platform with information on stock availability, vendor routes and even value chain-related information. Vendors also benefit from increased visibility and optimized routes. Adolescents, being the less consuming age group of quality F&V and the more tech-savvy, are a key focus of the system, benefiting from improved exposure to nutritious options.

Project Title: Terra Doce Program: Inclusive environmental prosperity
Executive Summary: Terra Doce promotes environmental, economic, and social transformation in degraded Atlantic Forest lands by replacing harmful practices with sustainable and regenerative agroforestry. This approach produces high-quality, pesticide-free food rich in complex nutrients while providing financial benefits to many rural families. Working on a landscape scale, we will offer our products with a Terra Doce certificate, which tells the story of this life-changing movement and provides consumers with the opportunity to make more conscious choices.
Innovation Description: Instituto Terra is located in the Doce River basin, Minas Gerais, Brazil, originally home to the abundant Atlantic Forest.   Over the years, this region has suffered significant damage due to deforestation, mining, extensive agriculture, and livestock farming, causing soil degradation, silting up of rivers, reduced water infiltration and biodiversity losses. More recently, in 2015, the collapse of one ore tailings dam in Mariana, Minas Gerais, caused profound socioeconomic and environmental impacts across the region.   In the social sphere, there has been an intense rural exodus, resulting from the impoverishment of the soil and living conditions in the countryside. As a result, various problems related to unemployment, urban violence and the poor urban structure in terms of basic sanitation, health and education mean that the region is classified as having an average human development index (HDI).  We aim to transform the Doce river basin into an example of socio-environmental resilience by integrating conservation, forest restoration, and income generation, while promoting water security and the well-being of local communities.   We offer technical assistance to transform rural productivity, implementing agroforestry systems to improve farm's productivity and produce quality while restoring soil and water. We also offer environmental education to children, adolescents and young adults, showing them a different perspective on their own land and how they can engage and improve it.  With this project we aim to provide financial gain to many rural families, while restoring water springs, forests and the soil, all being realized by the people from that land.

Project Title: Kitchen Gardens for Malnurished Households: Strengthening Offseason Vegetable Production.
Executive Summary: This project is designed to address this food shortage, so that poor families will be able to grow vegetables during dry season and during prolong dryness. Innovative approaches are developed to the constraints of the regions (short length growing period, poor quality of soil, water scarcity) and of the target groups (low capacity of investment, low agricultural knowledge). It specifically addresses climatic constraints in order to decrease the vulnerability of the people while building the capacity of the beneficiaries for improved, sustainable vegetable production.    The proposal includes the whole vegetable production chain, from seed management to nutrition/cooking class in order to address the needs of the beneficiaries both for the vegetable production and the nutrition knowledge and know-how (awareness, cooking classes). These two aspects are considered as major pillars to improve food security, notably at the household level. Indeed the action will promote innovative approaches to improving food security in Northwest, West, Southwest, Center and Littoral Regions of Cameroon, addressing old and new food security challenges through innovative and locally owned sustainable solutions, which could be scaled up and mainstreamed.    The objective of the project is to implement and mainstream innovative, sustainable, affordable and locally owned approaches to improve food security amongst 10,000 of the most vulnerable people (malnourished households in Cameroon by 2030.  The specific objective of the project is to enhance the capacity of resource-poor and poverty-stricken farmers and herders at low income brackets to produce a wide variety of vegetables using sustainable and environmentally-friendly technologies with integrated social ownership and management and involvement.    The goal is to increase local availability of safe, quality vegetables to enhance food security as well as achieving nutritional balance for 10,000 households through diversification of diets of the poorest segments of the vulnerable populations in target regions. Priority in selection of target groups and project beneficiaries is given to, female-headed households, newly settled families, resource-poor herders and farmers, and other vulnerable groups without access to secure livelihood. Aiming to increase economic capacity, ensures community buy-in, build climate resilience and increase food security for over 15 million people by 2030, through strengthening family farms and improving livelihoods.

Project Title: Deployment of High Zinc Rice to Address Zinc Malnutrition in Nepal
Executive Summary:
Deployment of high Zinc (Zn) rice varieties is one of the cheapest and most sustainable food-based solutions to address Zn malnutrition. At IRRI, we have developed high Zn rice breeding lines with an additional 8 to 10 ppm grain Zn content over the popular rice varieties along with high yield and grain quality traits. Some of these lines have been successfully released for commercial cultivation in several countries of Asia except Nepal. With the multi-country seed sharing agreement â€œseeds without borders,â€ now it is possible to release and deploy some of these high Zn rice varieties in Nepal with minimal testing.



Zn deficiency affects >50% of the worldâ€™s population by causing health problems such as stunting, diarrhea, impaired immunity and cognitive development, and poor growth and development. These health issues are highly prevalent in predominantly rice-consuming Asian countries. Thus, providing nutrition to vulnerable target populations is a priority sustainable development goal. In Nepal, 22.9% of preschool children and 24.7 % of non-pregnant women, especially those in rural areas, suffer Zn deficiency associated-health problems. Efforts to supply Zn through supplementation and rice fortification are limited by scale and effectiveness. While Zn biofortified rice supplies Zn on a daily basis in a readily available food matrix hence easily absorbed by the body and proven to be efficient in reducing Zn malnutrition in the target groups. It is cheaper and sustainable as the farmers can multiply and use their own seeds, no recurring investments are needed, scalable, easy to reach out to remote populations, and there are no barriers to consumer acceptance. Using this approach, it is possible to reduce the health burden significantly, so an increase in a healthy population can contribute to the economic development of a nation. Ours is the first attempt to introduce Zn biofortified rice in Nepal.

Project Title: Glycemic Reduction and Added Integrated Nutrients - Scaling the Low GI rice with increased protein content for the vulnerable Filipino population (GRAIN+)
Executive Summary: Asia faces a double burden of diabetes and malnutrition, particularly in low-income, rice-dependent communities. With diabetes cases rising, improving rice s nutritional quality is crucial. Our "Low GIPlus rice," with low glycemic index and high protein content, can regulate blood sugar with enhanced protein content. Challenges remain in scaling production and market uptake, requiring standardized testing and effective marketing strategies to make low GIPlus rice accessible and affordable for vulnerable populations.
Innovation Description: The Low GIPlus rice innovation addresses two critical challenges: the rising prevalence of diabetes and malnutrition in rice-dependent, low-income communities. Rice, a staple food, is often low in essential nutrients and has a high glycemic index (GI), contributing to elevated blood sugar levels and an increased risk of type 2 diabetes. This is especially relevant as diabetes cases are rising globally, with 4.3 million Filipinos diagnosed with diabetes in 2021.  The solution involves developing rice varieties with both low GI properties with extra protein. These rice varieties help regulate blood sugar levels and address protein deficiencies, improving diabetes management and overall nutrition. Scientific insights into rice breeding have enabled the integration of low GI traits into high-yielding varieties, maintaining productivity and taste.  The immediate benefits include improved health outcomes for consumers, especially those with diabetes and malnutrition. For farmers, the innovation provides a sustainable crop with low GI varieties having high yield potential, and early maturity requires minimal agricultural inputs, enhancing profitability as consumers are willing to pay a premium for low GI rice. Environmentally, the adoption of early maturity and nutritious varieties reduces water use and greenhouse gas emissions compared to traditional long-maturity crops.  The stable low GI trait ensures sustainability, allowing these varieties to be grown across multiple seasons. By addressing both health and environmental challenges, Low GIPlus rice provides lasting benefits to individuals, communities, and society, promoting better health and a more sustainable food system.

Project Title: Resilience through Regeneration
Executive Summary: Itanya Africa Group empowers smallholder farmers in semi-arid Kenya through regenerative agriculture, water infrastructure, and climate-smart solutions. We train farmers on sustainable practices like syntropic agroforestry, construct water pans to reduce reliance on rain-fed agriculture, and establish vertical gardens to enhance food security. By fostering social capital and leveraging community-driven initiatives, we aim to restore degraded lands, improve livelihoods, and build resilient, self-sustaining agricultural systems.
Innovation Description: Itanya Africa Group's innovation addresses the critical challenges of degraded soils, unreliable rainfall, and food insecurity faced by smallholder farmers in semi-arid Kenya. By integrating regenerative agriculture, syntropic agroforestry, and water-smart technologies, we provide a holistic solution to enhance productivity, resilience, and environmental restoration.  The problem is highly relevant as climate change intensifies, threatening agricultural livelihoods and ecosystems. Our approach combines scientific insights on soil regeneration with practical, locally adapted techniques. For example, composting agricultural waste into biofertilizer rejuvenates soil health, while syntropic agroforestry mimics natural ecosystems, increasing biodiversity and water retention. Additionally, water pans and vertical gardens reduce reliance on rain-fed agriculture, enabling year-round farming and optimizing water use.  Farmers benefit immediately through increased yields, diversified income streams, and enhanced knowledge. Long-term, the innovation promotes sustainable land use, combats desertification, and mitigates climate change impacts. Communities gain access to improved food security, economic stability, and a healthier environment. Society benefits from a replicable model for resilient agriculture that reduces emissions and supports local ecosystems.  This integrated, science-backed approach not only empowers farmers but also strengthens the social fabric of communities, fostering collaboration and shared growth.

Project Title: Agro-Processing
Executive Summary: This project aims at providing nutritious products from processed orange fresh sweet potato to refugees, displaced communities and host communities in Rwanda to confirm whether sweet potato flour can be adaptable to daily Rwandan meal. It will be executed by JIF CBC (orange sweet potato flour processor and main implementer) and Spirit of Peace and Solidarity (SPS, a Non-Profit-Refugee-Led Organization (second implementer) from January 2025 to December 2026.
Innovation Description: Sweet potatoes are massively grown and produced by almost each Rwandan household. They are even among major and commonly consumed food every day, particularly in rural and refugee camps areas. However, because sweet potatoes are generally produced once year with very few parts of the country that can produce twice per year and at large quantity. The marketplace becomes very saturated with these produces especially at the harvesting time, which often lead to the decrease of cost at 85% (MINAGRI, 2022) and also to poor nutrition (33%, MoH 2023) since they are forged to eat all of them within short time due to limited capacity for long term conservation. JIF CBC has availed the proccessing plant to rwandan farmers to process Vit A fresh sweet potato into flour and noodles so that the flour can be accessible to the communities yearlong. The factory was launched and preliminary production actvities have already started. This project aims at testisting if the product will be liked as a sustitute of orange fresh sweet potato for improved nutrition. It will also be executed alongside with other empowerement programs that will promote micro-climate resilence (waste recycling, composting&agro-forestry), increase their food purchase power in addition to income generation from fresh sweet potato farming (Business mentorship, Saving& Credit Groups). It will be executed by JIF as primary implementor and SPS as a non profit organisation acting as a mediator between JIF and MIDMAR (Ministry in charge of refugees) and UNHCR, Rwanda.

Project Title: Wasteless-to-feedwell
Executive Summary: Our wasteless-to-foodwell project tackles hunger and malnutrition in west Africa starting with Kano Nigeria  by converting excess vegetable waste into nutritious food. Our 3-in-1 bioconvertion hub features a community garden, eco-factory, and eco-mart, providing a safety net for vulnerable communities, economically empowering individuals, and establishing sustainable food waste management systems. This innovative approach breaks the poverty cycle, ensuring food security and dignity for the poorest, while promoting environmental sustainability.
Innovation Description: Wasteless- to- feedwell project is Addressing hunger & malnutrition in Africa starting with Nassarawa LGA, Kano State, where institutionalized begging is prevalent via the  Alma Jiri systems  (under aged street begging) Ironically in communities situated around abundance of organic waste like Yankaba Market (largest vegetable market in NE Nigeria) which we use as pilot and feasibilty study face: - Severe hunger/malnutrition - Excess vegatable waste (daily tonnes) According to FAO 1/3 of global food produced is wasted and Over 40% of Africa waste is organic. Our waste-to-food project tackles this paradox with goals to; - Improve food security for vulnerable communities by creating an alternate food path that serves as a safety net for the poorest in low income slums and ghetto communities like mine . - Economically empower vulnerable individuals and households to break the poverty cycle. - Establish sustainable systems that facilitate food waste collection, recycling, upscaling, and redistribution. our approach to providing this solution is a 3-in-1 bioconvertion Hub, comprising; 1. Community Garden: A shared space for; green houses, arable land parcels for group crop cultivation and free range space for poultry. 2. Eco Factory: A facility for recycling vegetables and organic food waste into useful inputs like biofertilizers, pesticides, BSF larvae and biodiesel. 3. Eco Mart: A makeshift structure serving as a weekly food-subsidy sales outlet for grains, vegetables, and agricultural inputs to our membership base, alongside a daily restaurant-food bank for feeding the homeless and needy using repurposed leftovers donated by food and hospitality businesses.

Project Title: Sustainable Transformation of Cashew Fruits: Zero Waste Solutions for Farmer Income Boost, Rural Employment, and Reduced Carbon Footprint
Executive Summary: Kamireddy Agro Foods Pvt. Ltd. is a zero-waste, sustainability-driven company transforming underutilized cashew apples into high-value products like vinegar, NATA de Cashew, beverages, and feed supplements. By integrating cutting-edge technology and engaging 1.5 million farmers, it creates economic, environmental, and social impact while catering to growing markets in food, cosmetics, and animal nutrition.
Innovation Description: India generates approximately 4 million tonnes of cashew apples annually, most of which are discarded as waste. This not only leads to significant resource underutilization but also contributes to environmental issues, such as 20 million kg of methane emissions from rotting fruits. Additionally, cashew farmers face limited income opportunities due to the lack of value-added processing for this byproduct.  Simultaneously, there is a high reliance on imported products like NATA de coco, while gaps exist in the market for innovative, cashew-based products such as beverages, vinegar, and feed supplements. Addressing these challenges can transform waste into economic value, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and empower rural communities.  Zero-Waste Philosophy: Kamireddy Agro Foods embodies a zero-waste model by converting underutilized cashew apple by-products into high-value products, addressing the environmental and economic inefficiencies in cashew farming. Innovative Product Line: NATA de Cashew: The first-of-its-kind alternative to NATA de coco, made using cashew apples instead of coconuts. Cashew Vinegar: Offers 80% metabolic similarity to apple cider vinegar, catering to a health-conscious market with a unique raw material base. Cajuice: A novel, palatable beverage created through innovative detannification technology. Cavita: A high-nutrition animal feed supplement derived from cashew fiber, supporting livestock industries. Environmental Impact: By utilizing cashew apples, the company prevents the release of 20 million kg of methane emissions, aligning with sustainability goals. Farmer-Centric Approach: Direct engagement with 1.5 million cashew farmers boosts their income by up to 40%, creating significant social impact.

Project Title: Revamping and scaling up  sustenanable agricultural activities of KADEC
Executive Summary: The prime objective of KADEC CIG is to contribute to alleviating poverty in the Kedjom Fondoms by strengthening the agricultural sector thereby creating jobs, fostering education and other developmental efforts as part of her corporate responsibility.  KADEC started her farming activities in 2015, and they were becoming very productive. These initial efforts were financed using contributions from members. Two years after the existence of KADEC, the political crisis started and destabilized the organization’s activities. The crisis was later compounded by the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic. These crises made movement to and from the farm land as well as cultivating around the farm land difficult due to insecurity from the political crisis and the movement restrictions that were imposed as part of the COVID-19 preventive measures. This caused KADEC to incur huge loses because crops that were cultivated got bad in the farm and consequently farming activities were suspended. At this point in time, there is reduced insecurity from the crisis and movement to the farm land and cultivation of the farm is possible, and currently ongoing at small scale. Also, the COVID-19 is under epidemic control and preventive measures restrictions that were imposed by the disease are no longer in force. Unfortunately, many KADEC members were rendered poor by the political crisis that caused some of them to became internally displaced persons. Additionally, the COVID-19 pandemic slowed down the personal businesses of many members. These have made the members to be unable the contribute finances for the revitalization of KADEC farming activities.  KADEC therefore see this funding opportunity to be very beneficiary in assisting her revamp her farming activities.     The initiatives envisaged through this support include the scaling up of irish potatoes farming activities by expanding of the farming areas and cultivating in both the raining and dry seasons (two cycles). The realization of this initiative requires the preparation of a larger farm area, installing water irrigation system in the farmland for use during dry season cultivation, procuring seedlings and a means of transportation of inputs and outputs from the farm.

Project Title: Resilient and Regenerative Villages (R2V)
Executive Summary: R2V will scale-up tested regenerative agricultural models in Kenya which were tested under 2-SCALE project and the on-going IKEA Foundation regenerative rice project. The focus will be adoption and structuring trade of the groundnut varieties (Mwangaza and Ndovu) tested in Eastern region of Kenya in partnership with Batian Nuts Ltd under 2-SCALE project. Other than promotion of the groundnut varieties, R2V will also promote regenerative agriculture technologies tested through R4iCSA Project.
Innovation Description: Eastern region of Kenya is prone to high occurrence of aflatoxin on grains with groundnut affected the most, for example, samples that were taken from this region in 2020 before the implementation of 2-SCALE groundnut project, had as high as 150ppb levels of aflatoxin. The area is also prone to drought as it is Semi-ASAL with many of the community members experiencing perennial famine, thus need to have an introduction of crop varieties that can easily adapt to low rainfall levels. Groundnut intrinsic valuable crop for both rural and urban communities in Kenya. Its absence in the agrarian ecosystem exacerbates socio economic challenges that suppress growth and development in many ways. Malnutrition typically evident through goiter and rickets are common deficiency symptoms seen in parts of the Eastern Region of Kenya.   Kilimo Trust in partnership with Batian Nuts Ltd and Egerton University tested new groundnut varieties that were able to grow well and are liked by both the community members and the groundnut off-takers (Markets). These groundnut varieties are more resilient to both aflatoxin and drought thus presenting the community with an alternative of having energy dense and aflatoxin free products from groundnut.   This initiative will see structuring and promotion for adoption of these improved groundnut varieties in Eastern region of Kenya for healthier lives and climate resilience in the region.

Project Title: Kilimomax BSF farming
Executive Summary: KilimoMax Solutions, in partnership with Dodoma City Council, is implementing a Black Soldier Fly (BSF) project at Chidaya Landfill to transform organic waste into sustainable animal feed and organic compost. This innovation addresses waste management, enhances soil fertility, and improves food security. By empowering marginalized communities, the project promotes environmental sustainability and economic opportunities while offering a scalable solution to tackle pressing agricultural and environmental challenges in Tanzania.
Innovation Description: Dodoma City generates approximately 350 metric tons of solid waste daily, with over 60% being organic. This waste remains underutilized, contributing to environmental pollution, methane emissions, and poor public health. Simultaneously, farmers face challenges like declining soil fertility, expensive animal feed, and limited access to sustainable agricultural inputs.  KilimoMax Solutions' Black Soldier Fly (BSF) project addresses these issues by transforming organic waste into valuable resources: nutrient-rich animal feed and organic compost. Through an innovative process, BSF larvae consume organic waste, rapidly converting it into high-protein larvae for livestock feed and compost that rejuvenates degraded soils.  This solution is grounded in scientific insights on BSF's ability to efficiently recycle waste and improve circular economies. It reduces waste pollution, lowers greenhouse gas emissions, and provides affordable alternatives to chemical fertilizers and conventional animal feed.  The project offers immediate benefits to farmers by increasing yields and reducing input costs, while communities experience cleaner environments and reduced health risks. Long-term, the initiative fosters environmental sustainability, strengthens food systems, and empowers marginalized groups such as youth and women.  This scalable and replicable model not only addresses Tanzania's pressing waste management and agricultural challenges but also contributes to achieving global sustainability goals, making it a transformative solution for food systems and environmental health.

Project Title: BRAVE
Executive Summary: This project KUECHO South Sudan shall an enable and support local communities and their South Sudanese partners to build inclusive, equitable and resilient value chains and agri-food enterprises, grounded on their entrepreneurial ideas, with specific attention for local seed security, rural entrepreneurship, and stakeholder collaboration. Food system transformation in South Sudan is not easy, because of multiple shocks and stressors, persisting conflict and violence , and natural resource deterioration. For many years, external aids.
Innovation Description: Main problems in the targeted county that need to be solved to achieve the desired impact: 1) Lack of good quality seed, in demand by local farmers, provided in a timely manner for affordable prices, 2) Poor agri-value chain and agri-food enterprise development to narrow the food gap and provide a diversity of healthy foods (including lack of participation by women and youth in seed production, agri-value chain and agri-food enterprise development), and 3) Lack of knowledge, learning and evidence-based programming in support of food systems transformation. The project will directly work with 20 local case owners, coordinating the development of 15 practical cases in a certain sub-sector and value chain in a specific context. The Sustainable Food System project counts with an average of 100 farmer households per case, targeting a total of 2,000 smallholder food producer households/entrepreneurs (projected at 15,000 individuals), of which 350 will be seed producer farmers (organized in 24 seed producer groups), with a keen interest in improving their production and scaling value chains and agri-business. Project Title: Fostering a sustainable poultry value chain: Reducing waste, and prioritizing public health
Executive Summary: This project seeks to commercialize a novel poultry feed formulation that utilizes the natural antibiotic properties of cloves as a substitute for human-grade antibiotics commonly used in poultry farming. $25,000 shall be directed towards equipment acquisition, certification and packaging which clearly communicates the safety of the product with its potential to reduce antibiotic resistance amongst chicken consumers. The project will also include training programs for small-holder farmers on sustainable poultry farming practices.
Innovation Description: Uganda faces a critical food security challenge, with malnutrition remaining widespread despite agricultural potential. While chicken offers a valuable protein source, the industry is challenged by high waste generation and rampart utilization of antibiotics, posing significant risks to human health (antibiotic resistance and non-communicable diseases). Kisakye Poultry Farm addresses Uganda's food security and health challenges by producing and promoting organic, antibiotic-free chicken through efficient feed formulation that utilizes essential oils. It was discovered that poultry farmers excessively add antibiotics to poultry feeds because the birds grow faster due to elimination of bacteria in the birds' gut.  We add natural phytogenic additives such as cloves which have antimicrobial properties thereby eliminating harmful bacteria in the birds' gut thus promoting bird growth without posing a public health challenge. Through farmer training, market creation, and skill development programs for marginalized communities, we foster a sustainable and equitable poultry industry which provides chicken consumers with safer chicken on the market thereby reducing chances of antibiotic resistance.

Project Title: Healthy Vegetables for All: Empowering Communities with Nutritious Vegetables to Tackle Malnutrition and Food Insecurity.
Executive Summary: Healthy Veggies for All is a vegetable farming initiative in Baleofiili, Ghana, providing organic vegetables like cabbage, tomatoes, and green peppers. We recycle food waste into compost, practice climate-smart farming, and empower smallholder farmers with training and market access. Our eco-friendly packaged vegetables are delivered to consumers  doorsteps. Through community programs, we promote healthy eating and combat malnutrition, ensuring accessible, nutritious food for all.
Innovation Description: Growing up in Baleofiili, a rural community in the Upper West region of Ghana, accessing fresh vegetables was extremely challenging. Farmers traditionally focused on growing grains such as maize and groundnuts, with less than 10% cultivating vegetables. Prolonged dry seasons and poor post-harvest management exacerbated the situation, leading to malnutrition, particularly among pregnant women and children. This scarcity and its effect on nutrition inspired my commitment to vegetable farming.  According to a 2020 World Health Organization report, Northern Ghana has the country s highest malnutrition rate at nearly 48%, largely due to insufficient consumption of nutrient-rich foods like vegetables. The few vegetables available are often cultivated using inorganic fertilizers and sold under unhygienic conditions, making them unsafe for consumption.   Healthy Veggies for All addresses these issues using a multifaceted approach. We grow vegetables such as cabbage and green pepper year-round using climate-smart methods, including compost from recycled food waste and solar-powered irrigation. Through our vegetable out-grower system, we empower smallholder farmers by connecting them to inputs and markets and training them in organic farming practices like composting. Additionally, we educate communities on the importance of vegetable consumption to combat malnutrition.   Our initiative allows consumers, especially children, pregnant women, and low-income families, to access affordable, nutritious vegetables, improving nutrition and health. Farmers reduce costs and improve yields by adopting climate-smart methods. Communities benefit from integrated nutrition programs that promote healthy eating habits. Environmentally, the initiative reduces greenhouse gas emissions, enhances soil health, and minimizes waste through sustainable practices.

Project Title: Development of Activated Carbon  Waste Water Purification System for Illegal Mining Communities in Ghana
Executive Summary: Illegal mining is rampant in Ghana. This has led to pollution of ground and surface water for drinking and agricultural production in affected rural communities with associated health and environmental concerns. The project aims to develop and test low-cost water purification systems for mining-affected rural communities. Waste organic materials such as rice husk and saw dust will be developed into Organic Carbon (Activated Charcoal) for purifying polluted water for consumption and vegetable crop production.
Innovation Description: Illegal mining in Ghana affects the quality of surface water and groundwater. This is poses a threat to women and children in affected communities (Gardner et al., 2015). A study by the Commission of Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ) of Ghana revealed that many rivers and streams providing safe water for the mining communities have been destroyed, polluted or dried up. Illegal small-scale mining is also increasing environmental pollution while affecting health, aquatic life, and agriculture (Nasirudeen, 2015). There is the urgent need to sustain the environment, agriculture, food systems and the health of vulnerable groups (Bansah et al., 2016).   Heavy metal pollutants, such as mercury, cyanide, cadmium, and/or arsenic from these illegal activities is appearing in the food chain. These pollutants affect humans ranging from mild eye, nose and skin irritations, severe headache, stomach ache, diarrhea, hematemesis, vomiting, dizziness, and organ dysfunction (cirrhosis, necrosis, low blood pressure, hypertension, and gastrointestinal distress) (Inyinbor et al., 2018).   Cognitive impairment, among others, have has been reported in some children. Babies have been born with their legs forming around the chest, neck and stomach while some are also born with one eye, without genitalia or suffer from kidney and hypertensive-related conditions as reported by a pathologist (Prof. Paul Poku Sampene Ossei). Drinking contaminated water or eating aquatic organisms or farm produce with the accumulation of these toxins also pose major threats.

Project Title: Integrated Aquaponics for Sustainable Livelihoods and Climate Change Resilience in Northern Ghana
Executive Summary: Northern Ghana is noted to be the most affected by climate change in the country. This project, therefore, seeks to strengthen the resilience of smallholder farmers through climate SMART technologies such as integrated fish and vegetable farming, energy saving cooking stoves, tree planting, farmer managed natural regeneration, organic pesticides and household manure preparation and utilization. It will also focus on improving nutrition through the promotion of orange flesh potato and nutritional educational program.
Innovation Description: Climate change severely impact women, children and the most vulnerable population in northern Ghana exacerbating existing social, economic, and political inequalities and threatening sustainable livelihoods. Due to climate change impacts, the agricultural sector in northern Ghana which relies heavily on rain-fed farming has become vulnerable due to rising temperatures, changes in rainfall patterns and extreme weather events.  The vulnerability in northern Ghana's agriculture has led to reduced crop yields, food insecurity, water scarcity, and increased poverty. To mitigate these impacts, innovative approaches that enhances agricultural resilience are crucial. Notably, aquaponics has immerged as the best recognized solution, offering a sustainable solution for producing fish and vegetables, and paving way for a transformative shift in northern Ghana s agricultural landscape.   The Aquaponics for Sustainable Livelihood and Climate Resilience initiative is a closed-loop system that combines aquaculture with hydroponics to provide sustainable fish and vegetables farming, enabling farmers to adapt to climate change and improve their livelihoods, thereby promoting climate-resilient agriculture. The heart of this innovative system is the symbiotic relationship between fish and plants. In this relationship (mutualism), waste produced by the fish is transformed into nutrients for plants, enabling nutrient cycling to occur with minimal waste and water usage. It is in leveraging this natural process that Aquaponics for Sustainable Livelihood and Climate Resilience develops such an efficient and sustainable production system for food. The immediate benefits of this solution will be increased access to nutritious food, better livelihoods farmers, and increased climate resilience while concurrently reducing environmental degradation

Project Title: Laser Weeding Technology
Executive Summary: LUXEED Robotics is building a machine for farmers that uses lasers and AI to burn weeds, completely eliminating the need for herbicides and significantly enhancing farmers' profit margins. The fully functional AI that detects where the lasers need to hit is built inhouse and is now working on onions, one of the crops vulnerable to weeds. We're making laserweeding accessible to small and medium scale farmers.
Innovation Description: Weeding is a global chronic challenge for farmers. They rely heavily on expensive and scarce manual labor and on herbicides, which are harmful to crops, the soil, and the environment. Even advanced farms still lose up to 50% yield on crops vulnerable to weeds, like seed onions. Our innovation reduces weeding costs over 10 years for farmers with 200 hectares around 7 million USD and enhances yield gain from 5 to 30%, thereby significantly affecting the farmers' profit margins and almost doubling produce on the same plot. The biodiversity and underground water channels will greatly benefit from the elimination of herbicides, as well as the soil and crops, which will contain 0 chemical residues when farmers adopt our technology. This technology as it exists today is bulky, expensive, and power-hungry, making it accessible to large-scale farmers (500 hectares and more), with only one commercial company, Carbon Robotics, in the market. Our innovation is 50% more affordable thanks to many aspects of the technology being developed to suit the demands and needs of small and medium scale farmers.

Project Title: Combating Desertification in the Cholistan Region, Punjab Pakistan, through climate smart agriculture
Executive Summary: The Cholistan Desert in Pakistan faces challenges in sustainable Agriculture which in result impacts food production. This project aims to improve Pakistan s Agriculture and ensure food security, improve livelihoods in rural areas, and reduce environmental degradation by introducing smart farming practices. Additionally, Artificial Intelligence, internet of Things, remote sensing and GIS technologies will be employed to monitor land conditions, enabling precise decision-making, optimize crop selection and resource management for enhanced agricultural productivity.
Innovation Description: The Cholistan Desert (Bahawalpur district), located in southern Punjab, Pakistan, faces severe desertification and significant challenges in producing sustainable food due to erratic climatic conditions, water scarcity, unsustainable, and limited agriculture infrastructure.   The project will introduce a combination of traditional knowledge and modern scientific methods to enhance food security, improving livelihoods, and mitigating environmental degradation. The implementation of sustainable practices, including organic farming, crop rotation will help restore soil health, reduce water consumption, and increase the resilience of the region s food systems to climate variability.  Crop growth in Pakistan is highly dependent on rainfall and irrigation system, providing a unique, efficient, simple and cost effective system through the deployment of advanced innovative irrigation methods such as drip, CPS and micro-sprinkler irrigation will help people in arid regions.  Whereas the changes in crop growth will be computed through remote sensing, AI, IoT and crop reporting data.   The changes in climatic variabilities from 1951 to 2024 will be assessed.   In order to raise awareness among local communities of farmers about the importance of sustainable farming practices, soil and water conservation will be through training programs and workshops.   The food security can be improved by promoting climate-resilient agricultural practices tailored to the local environment, such as cultivation of drought-resistant crops, better irrigation techniques and carbon credit.   Finally, it will enhance the quality of life and food security in arid regions and contribute to climate change adaptation and support the development of a competitive, inclusive and sustainable agribusiness industry.

Project Title: Transforming Water Management for Food Security in Northern Territory, Australia
Executive Summary: This project leverages Leakster's real-time water leak detection technology to address water scarcity challenges in Northern Territory, Australia. In collaboration with PowerWater, we will design and manufacture 20 sensors to be deployed in drought-prone areas for proactive leak detection. By reducing water loss in critical regions, this initiative aims to preserve resources for agricultural use, enhance food security, and build climate resilience for communities in the Northern Territory.
Innovation Description: Leakster s real-time water leak detection technology addresses the critical challenge of water scarcity caused by leaks in aging infrastructure. In regions like Northern Territory, Australia, where drought is a constant threat, up to 30% of treated water is lost before reaching its intended use. This wasted water limits availability for agricultural production, threatens food security, and increases operational costs for utilities and communities.  The innovation combines advanced IoT sensors and AI-driven analytics to pinpoint leaks in real time. These sensors monitor pipeline acoustics, identifying even the smallest leaks with high accuracy. The collected data is transmitted to a cloud-based platform where utilities can visualise leak locations and prioritise repairs. This proactive approach eliminates the inefficiencies of traditional reactive methods, which often fail to address water loss until major failures occur.  This solution is the result of advancements in acoustic analysis and IoT technologies, tailored for the harsh conditions of drought-prone regions. By deploying 20 sensors in collaboration with PowerWater, this project will target high-leakage areas in the Northern Territory, ensuring sustainable water management.  Benefits:  Immediate Benefits: Reduced water loss, lower operational costs for utilities, and improved water availability for farmers and communities. Sustainable Benefits: Increased resilience to drought, support for sustainable agriculture, and decreased environmental impact through reduced energy use for pumping and treating water. Leakster empowers communities with reliable access to water, directly improving food security and climate resilience.

Project Title: 2025 food rescue for the community in need in Baltimore
Executive Summary: Leftover Love helps rescue fresh leftover food at close of business from restaurants, cafes and bakeries and gets it into the hands of those in need.  We do this by dropping of food with other nonprofits that the community in need is already familiar with, therefore eliminating the need to establish a new date and time for a food distribution event, and therefore easing budgets, logistics and transport for those involved.
Innovation Description: Food rescue in the US is an epidemic, it is so much more convenient for people to throw food away.  In Baltimore, the community in need is prevalent in almost all communities, Black, Latinx X, Immigrant, Refugee or others that can benefit from this amazing fresh leftover food.  Most of the problem is education, where food donors like businesses do not know that there are tax benefits to donating leftover food to a 501c3 nonprofit and that the liability is also lifted during their donation in good faith.  Leftover Love is solving the problem of getting food into the hands of those that need it, by providing the transportation and logistics to get it from Point A, the food donor to Point B, the food recipient organizations.  This results in less food wasted, more food getting directly into the hands of those in need and also gives food donors a tax benefit and helps compliment the impact Leftover Love is able to make.  Our founders started asking in their neighborhood, "What happens with leftover food at close of business?" and the answer was the same.  They decided to bring together the community to help solve the problem by enlisting volunteers to make an impact for the city they care about. Those in need are able to get this fresh food from organizations they're already familiar with, feed their families and help the environment by wasting less perfectly good food.

Project Title: Expansion of K-12 STEAM Classroom Composting Program in Gulf Coast Region of the U.S.
Executive Summary: The Gulf Coast region of the United States faces severe climate challenges, including hurricanes, flooding, and food insecurity, disproportionately impacting low-income communities. Landfill methane emissions exacerbate these issues. Funding would support public school food waste reduction efforts in Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, and Florida for the 2025-2026 school year. We aim to deliver K-12 STEAM curriculum, educational supplies, and teacher training to economically disadvantaged areas, empowering schools to address waste reduction and environmental education effectively.
Innovation Description: The program solves the lack of environmental education in Title 1 schools, where underfunding prevents students from learning about waste reduction and climate issues. This problem perpetuates cycles of environmental degradation, health risks, and economic inequality. Addressing this gap is critical because it equips underserved communities to mitigate food waste and its impacts, including methane emissions from landfills. Our low-cost, low-tech solution is innovative because it is practical, accessible, and address real-world challenges effectively, without need for subscriptions or technology. The solution involves implementing a K-12 STEAM classroom composting program that provides reusable composting supplies, curriculum aligned with Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS), and teacher training. Students actively divert food waste from landfills, reducing methane emissions, creating compost, and learning about waste management, sustainability, and climate adaptation. Teachers and cafeteria staff collaborate to integrate these practices into daily routines. The insight behind this solution comes from understanding the link between food waste, landfill emissions, and disproportionate health and environmental burdens on low-income communities. Research on landfill methane emissions and the role of composting in waste reduction shaped the program s design. Immediate benefits include reduced landfill fees, fewer greenhouse gas emissions, and practical climate education for students. Long-term benefits include improved community sustainability, enhanced environmental stewardship, and workforce development opportunities in composting and waste management. Schools save costs on waste disposal, students gain career-ready skills, and communities experience reduced health risks. The program creates lasting impact through its scalable, affordable model, enabling underserved schools to address environmental challenges while fostering resilience.

Project Title: Lex Icons : A digital infrastructure for the positive impacts of food systems
Executive Summary: Lex Icons  offers a common language for food system actors to visualize their impacts in six key areas and share it with their partners. The infrastructure enables metadata embedding, real-time updates, and compliance tracking, promoting standardized, scalable icon use across various platforms. We will scale up the digital infrastructure for Lex Icons  (https://lex-icons.org), a respected, inclusive visual language of machine-readable icons that catalyzes support for positive impact projects.
Innovation Description: A challenge facing global food systems is the lack of a common language. Our website and tools fix that. Food businesses, charities, and social enterprises, use Lexicon of Food and the Lex Icons to build trust and align their activities with the mission-driven needs of potential clients, funders and partners. Especially when crossing boundaries across the Global South, scientists and knowledge creators who struggle to make their findings actionable and usable by those who must implement them we offer solutions. These producers can direct organizations, customers and funders Lexicon tools to deepen unity around complex topics.  Lexicon s system approach lets users express the full range of benefits offered in almost every domain. Visualizing positive impacts helps everyone involved in a food venture or non-profit initiative whether funders or intended communities on the ground to more easily and clearly understand the aspirations and outcomes of their collaborative activities. Lexicon of Food tools accelerate alignment and consensus on priorities, paving the way for catalytic capital to flow effectively.  While organizations working on the ground (and the measurement tools they use) excel at providing quantitative data, they often lack a shared language to visualize qualitative attributes effectively. Lex Icons  bridges this gap by helping actors in the food system articulate their practices and the benefits they create or support across six key areas of positive impact valued by investors, funders, clients, and policymakers: air, water, soil, biodiversity, equity, and carbon. This standardized format, or  expression layer,  can be integrated across data capture, storage, management, distribution.

Project Title: LimaBot AI
Executive Summary: LimaBot AI empowers African farmers with AI-driven tools to diagnose crop diseases, analyze soil health, and access actionable farming insights via SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile apps. By bridging the gap between farmers and critical resources, LimaBot enhances productivity, combats climate challenges, and promotes sustainable agriculture, contributing to food security and economic growth across the continent.
Innovation Description: In Africa, where over 40% of the population relies on farming for livelihood, limited access to agricultural experts, known as Bwana Shamba, poses a critical challenge. For instance, Tanzania has only 4,000 agricultural officers for over 2 million farmers, creating a ratio of one expert per 500 farmers. This gap leaves farmers vulnerable to crop diseases, pests, and poor soil management, exacerbated by climate change and limited access to accurate, real-time farming information.  LimaBot AI addresses this issue by leveraging artificial intelligence to provide farmers with instant, actionable insights. Through SMS, WhatsApp, and a mobile app, farmers can diagnose crop diseases, receive recommendations for pest control and fertilizers, and access weather forecasts. Our innovation also includes a soil sensor to analyze soil health and optimize farming practices.  The solution is built on advancements in AI and machine learning, enabling accurate diagnostics and tailored advice. Immediate benefits include reduced crop losses, increased productivity, and better-informed decision-making. Over the long term, LimaBot promotes sustainable farming, improves food security, and enhances farmers' resilience to climate change. By empowering communities with accessible technology, LimaBot drives economic growth and aligns with global sustainability goals, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

Project Title: Valley Bee For Food Security
Executive Summary: The Valley Bee For Food Security Project involves the manufacture and distribution of our AI, satellite technology, and hardware-enabled smart bee hives to create sustainable pollination systems to ensure food security in these critical times of global warming that is leading to dying bee colonies (bee pollinate 75% of all food crops globally). We also train rural farmers in advanced beekeeping techniques, hence our project helps increase crop yield and promote pollination.
Innovation Description: Valley Bee addresses the challenges of declining bee populations, food insecurity, and low agricultural productivity by introducing IoT-enabled smart beekeeping systems and sustainable honey production practices. Beekeeping plays a critical role in pollination, which directly impacts crop yield and biodiversity, yet traditional methods often result in low efficiency and productivity. Our solution involves equipping rural farmers with IoT-enabled smart hives that monitor and self-regulate hive health, temperature, and humidity in real-time, enabling proactive hive management, increased honey production and pollination to food crops in thousands of hectares around each hive. These hives use are crafted from upcycled agricultural waste, making them both sustainable and cost-effective. Alongside the technology, we provide comprehensive training in sustainable beekeeping and pollination practices to help local farmers fight the food crisis. The benefits are multi-faceted: -Farmers achieve increased income from improved crop yields due to increased pollination and revenue from honey sales as a by-product. -Communities no-longer fear for famine because of increased crop and bountiful local food production. Also gain from affordable and hygienic/locally produced foods as opposed to chemically produced and imported ones.  -The environment benefits from enhanced biodiversity and the upcycling of agricultural waste. Also, benefit from less fertiliser use as bees increase natural yield that was once only gotten from fertilisers. Our project is built on scientific insights into bee behaviour, environmental conditions, and pollination dynamics, providing a scalable, sustainable, and impactful solution to food system challenges. Our approach directly benefits farmers, improves food quality/security, and enhances environmental health.

Project Title: AI-Powered Pest Surveillance and Advisory for Paddy Farmers in India
Executive Summary: Rice is a vital global food crop and India is the world's largest exporter. With increasing demand for rice, improving production is critical. Small farmers who cultivate most of the paddy are the most vulnerable to yield loss due to pests infestation. To address this, an AI-powered pest surveillance solution, already used for cotton, will be adapted for paddy. It will offer real-time, localized pest identification and advisory via image analysis combined with science-based recommendations.
Innovation Description: Rice, the most cultivated crop in India, suffers an estimated 32.2 million tonnes of annual yield loss (25% of total yield). Marginal, small, and medium-scale farmers, who account for over 90% of cultivated land, often lack access to timely, reliable, and localized pest advisories. This results in overuse or mistimed use of pesticides, increasing costs, reducing effectiveness, and causing environmental damage, including soil and water contamination.  Climate-specific pests significantly exacerbate this challenge, as changing weather patterns and extreme conditions create favorable environments for the proliferation of pests and diseases in rice crops. Our proposed AI-powered pest advisory and surveillance solution aims to address these challenges for paddy farmers, building on our existing solution successfully deployed for cotton through a light-weight smartphone application. The AI model will provide real-time, accurate, and localized pest identification and actionable advisories based on images of pests/diseases taken using ordinary smartphones. Our solution will target 10+ pests and disease combinations of relevant importance in paddy crops.  The solution enables farmers to make informed decisions on pesticide use, preventing overuse and ensuring timely action to mitigate crop losses. This minimizes input costs, reduces environmental degradation, and enhances sustainable farming practices.  We will leverage partnerships and insights from a similar AI solution for cotton pests that we deployed with over 20,000 smallholder farmers and recorded an increase in net income due to lower pesticide expenditure. By providing scalable, accessible technology, this innovation empowers smallholder farmers to protect yields, improve profitability, and contribute to sustainable agriculture.

Project Title: Scaling MAMLO FOODS  Micro-Factory Model to Empower  Women Smallholder farmers  and Transform Peanut Processing
Executive Summary: MAMLO FOODS seeks to revolutionize Africa s peanut value chain by scaling its innovative Micro-Factory Model, empowering 500 women smallholder farmers while transforming peanut processing. This localized approach enhances efficiency, reduces post-harvest losses, and ensures farmers earn fair incomes. The $25,000 grant will be pivotal in procuring advanced equipment, delivering targeted training programs, and upgrading infrastructure, enabling us to produce premium peanut-based products and foster sustainable economic growth, gender equity, and community resilience.
Innovation Description: Africa s peanut value chain has long-standing challenges. Each year, 30% of peanuts are lost post-harvest, largely due to inefficient processing, poor storage, and limited market access. Women smallholder farmers, who make up 70% of the agricultural workforce in Africa, are particularly affected. Despite their efforts, many earn less than 20% of the market value of the final product, a situation perpetrated by unscrupulous brokers who exploit non-farmer-centered tactics, keeping them trapped in cycles of poverty. At MAMLO FOODS, we re addressing this challenge using our transformative Micro-Factory Model. Our pioneering micro-factory located in Amagoro, western Kenya processes up to 9 tonnes of peanuts each day. By bringing peanut processing closer to the farming communities, we are not only increasing farmers earnings but also cutting down post-harvest losses by up to 30%, effectively improving livelihoods and transforming peanut processing. Our solution also involves equipping 500 women farmers with advanced training in farming techniques, post-harvest handling, and value addition. This way, they can produce high-quality peanuts that meet market standards. We re also investing in efficient processing technology, which reduces waste and improves yields. This approach benefits not just farmers, but the entire community. Immediate benefits include: A 30% increase in farmer incomes. A 30% reduction in peanut losses. Creation of 10 local jobs in processing and distribution. In the long term, this model strengthens local economies, empowers women, and improves food security. Consumers get access to affordable, high-quality peanut products, while the environment benefits from reduced waste.

Project Title: Cassava for food and nutrition security (CAFNS) project.
Executive Summary: Cassava is a staple food in many parts of the world. It lacks protein, lipids, and many micronutrients and contains antinutrients. Consumption of cassava products without nutrient enrichment leads to malnutrition and development of some diseases that shorten the lifespan. This project seeks to increase the nutrient density of cassava-based food products; develop recipes from cassava composite flours; improve consumer awareness about diseases associated with the consumption of unfortified  ( not enriched) cassava diets.
Innovation Description: Improving the nutritional quality of cassava diets is a research priority since cassava is a major staple in many parts of the world and its consumption without appropriate complementation leads to malnutrition and development of diseases, promoting food insecurity. Most cassava diets provide carbohydrates and energy. They need to be complemented with proteins, lipids and micronutrients.   We intend to further our on-going research on improving the nutritional quality of cassava diets by formulating ready to prepare cassava composite products and recipes using (a) innovative technologies (modified solid state fermentation) to increase the protein and vitamin content of cassava (b) producing cassava flours with modified functional properties using safe levels of gamma irradiation to produce nanoparticles (c) complementing cassava with protein and micronutrient rich foods and developing recipes from them. Some enriched cassava products have been developed in our laboratory and by other researchers. Two new products will be developed. The knowledge of cassava consumers about its nutrient deficiencies and associated ailments and the need to prevent them will be improved, Consumer acceptability of newly developed nutrient dense cassava recipes will be evaluated in four states in Nigeria. Cassava producers and farmers increase their production and income. Cassava consumers will live healthier lives with diversified cassava diets. Nutritious cassava diets will be introduced into school feeding programmes. This project will address sustainable development goals (SDG.s) 2, 3, 10 1nd 12).
