Project Title: EMPOWERING TURKANA COUNTY IN KENYA THROUGH FOOD INNOVATION
Executive Summary: Tender Mercies (TM) innovation is a low cost, balanced, single complete nutrient-dense meal formulated to address hunger and malnutrition in nutrient-deficient communities in Kenya.  In Turkana, a severely food-insecure arid to semi-arid county, TM will be utilized in school feeding programs, at early childhood development centers and a girls high school to maintain attendance, thereby reducing teenage pregnancies and early marriages. Additionally, it will support women s entrepreneurship programs, fostering local sustainable solutions.
Innovation Description: Our innovation, Tender Mercies (TM), was formulated to address the problem of hunger and malnutrition in underserved communities like Turkana county that are food insecure, have persistent drought, hunger and have limited access to nutritious food. Turkana county has a hot, dry climate and is categorized as arid and semi-arid land.  Due to low agricultural productivity, and low access to nutritious food, chronic malnutrition remains a critical issue with high rates of stunting;  prevalence of  23% of children under 5 years, which is above the national  average (18%)  and wasting at 31.7%. (Kenya Demographic Health Survey, 2022).  This leads to developmental delays, reduced cognitive abilities, lower productivity, and weakened immunity, resulting in school drop-outs, teenage pregnancies, and  early marriages.  To alleviate this, TM will be used in school feeding programs in Early Childhood Centres and Milimatatu Girls' Secondary School.  TM is a single meal formulation mix of textured soy protein, rehydrated red beans, rice, salt, and enriched with vitamins and minerals.  Nutritionally; it provides macronutrients; 38.9% daily value allowance for protein per serving, 301 kilo calories per serving, and micronutrients; Vitamin A, Zinc, Iodine, Selenium, the B vitamins, among other vital nutrients, thus is ideal for Turkana.  Economically; it saves on fuel and time, thus is ideal for low income communities.  Environmentally; the reduced cooking time to 10-15 minutes due to precooking ingredients and soybean extrusion, reducing firewood use and in turn deforestation and carbon emissions.  Sustainability will be addressed through local women s entrepreneurship programs.

Project Title: Zero-Waste Food Production: Circular Economy Models for Sustainability
Executive Summary: his project creates a zero-waste food production model using circular economy principles to repurpose food waste into bioenergy, fertilizers, and upcycled products. By reducing waste, cutting emissions, and promoting sustainable practices, it enhances environmental health, economic resilience, and food security. Through innovation and collaboration, the initiative offers scalable solutions for a sustainable global food system.
Innovation Description: Food waste is a global issue, with nearly one-third of all food produced being discarded. This waste contributes to environmental harm, including greenhouse gas emissions and wasted resources like water and energy. Furthermore, food waste in landfills represents untapped opportunities for repurposing valuable by-products into useful products. This project offers a solution by implementing a circular economy model, transforming food waste into bioenergy, fertilizers, and upcycled products. By using technologies such as composting and bio-digestion, food waste is converted into renewable energy and nutrient-rich fertilizers for agriculture, reducing the need for chemical inputs and enhancing sustainability. The scientific insight behind this solution comes from the understanding that food waste can be an invaluable resource rather than a burden. Circular economy principles enable the repurposing of waste into valuable products, benefiting the environment, economy, and society. Benefits include: Farmers gain affordable, eco-friendly fertilizers. Communities benefit from redirected surplus food, increasing food security. Consumers enjoy access to affordable, sustainable products. The environment sees reduced greenhouse gas emissions and optimized resource use. Producers gain economic benefits from utilizing food waste as a resource. By reducing food waste and repurposing by-products, this project supports a more sustainable, efficient, and resilient food system for all stakeholders.

Project Title: Organic manure and biogas production from the market organic waste for improved food security, energy access and sanitation
Executive Summary: The economy of Malawi is agro-based, as more than 70% of the people are dependent on agriculture as their main source of livelihood. However, farmers and traders alike experience very high postharvest loss, which affects their income and also contributes to food insecurity. The problem is severe for perishable goods, such as, vegetables. Large quantities of vegetables can usually be seen dumped in open spaces, which contributes to poor sanitation of the markets.
Innovation Description: The innovation involves the development of biodigesters in community markets, which use market waste as feedstock. The biogas plants produce biogas, a clean cooking fuel, and liquid organic manure, which is used by smallholder farmers for vegetable cultivation. Therefore, the technology solves multiple challenges for the community. The use of market waste as a feedstock contributes to sanitation and helps to reduce the risks of waterborne diseases. The technology also helps to control GHG emissions from the waste sector. The surrounding community members also benefit from the organic manure and biogas produced from the market waste. Currently, smaller-holder farmers are increasingly relying on organic manure, considering that inorganic fertilizers have become less affordable. Thus, the use of the liquid organic fertilizer produced from the plant helps to improve food security and increase farmers income. On the other hand, biogas produced is considered a renewable and clean fuel that is used for cooking and heating. Currently, only 25% of the population in Malawi has access to electricity, and Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is less affordable and not widely accessible. Therefore, due to a lack of alternative sources of energy, the majority of households are increasingly relying on dirty cooking fuels, which are blamed for indoor emissions that cause respiratory illnesses. However, due to high rates of deforestation, firewood is becoming scarce and less affordable, and women and girls, who are tasked with households chores, spend more time searching for firewood instead of focusing on agriculture.

Project Title: Value Addition of De-Oiled Rice Bran Using Yeast Fermentation for Antibiotic-Free and Omega-3 Enriched Broiler Meat Production
Executive Summary: This project develops a yeast-based fermentation technology for value-adding underutilized agro by-product de-oiled rice bran (DORB) as a sustainable feed ingredient for broiler feed industry. This approach integrates Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Yarrowia lypolytica to produce quality feed ingredients, probiotics (yeast), and prebiotics (yeast metabolites). This reduces antibiotic dependency in broiler production, promotes omega-3 enriched meat, and addresses feed import dependency, ensuring safe, healthy broiler meat production in Bangladesh and other developing rice-producing countries.
Innovation Description: Problem: Broiler farming is critical in developing countries like Bangladesh to meet the people s protein demand. However, limited availability of affordable quality feed ingredients and reliance on costly imported feed ingredients, overuse of antibiotics, and at the same time inefficient utilization of local agricultural by-products hinder the growth of the industry. These issues contribute to risk in human health, including antibiotic resistance, compromised meat safety for human consumption, increased production costs, and environment burdens. Additionally, there is a growing demand for healthier meat enriched with omega-3 fatty acids, which is rarely addressed in traditional broiler production systems. Moreover, agricultural by-products like de-oiled rice bran (DORB), a by-product of rice milling industry, remain underutilized, despite their potential as a valuable feed ingredient. Solution: This project aims to address this challenge by enhancing the value of DORB through yeast fermentation technology, utilizing Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Yarrowia lypolytica. This process enhances the nutritional value of DORB, and the fermented DORB will serve as a sustainable, nutrient-rich feed ingredient for broilers. Yeast and its metabolites (beta-glucan, Mannan oligosaccharides, chitin, peptides, etc.) will act as probiotics and prebiotics, reducing the reliance on antibiotics while enhancing broiler gut health, immunity, and meat quality. Additionally, utilizing yeast in broiler diets enriches broiler meat with omega-3 fatty acids, meeting the consumer demands for healthier and safer poultry products. This approach promotes local resource use, reduces feed costs, and supports small-scale poultry farmers, aligns with consumer health trends, and contributes to global efforts to achieve sustainable food systems.

Project Title: Empowering Tigray's Farmers with Solar-Powered Cold Storage Technology
Executive Summary: The project introduces solar-powered cold storage units in rural Tigray. Its goal is to reduce food waste after harvest, improve food security, and help farmers earn more money. The initiative addresses major challenges, like a lack of storage facilities and unreliable energy access. These issues often lead to significant food loss. Innovation Description: The implementation of solar-powered cold storage technology in rural Tigray addresses a critical issue: post-harvest losses, which severely affect farmers' livelihoods and food security. The absence of adequate storage facilities and unreliable energy access often leads to considerable food waste, particularly concerning perishable goods. The proposed solution entails installing solar-powered cold storage units on farms, which will enable farmers to maintain their produce at optimal temperatures. This approach takes advantage of the abundant solar energy available in the region, presenting a sustainable and cost-effective method to extend the shelf life of perishable items. Solar-powered cold storage systems utilize photovoltaic panels to generate electricity that powers refrigeration units. This technology is particularly well-suited for off-grid areas, as it diminishes reliance on diesel generators and reduces carbon emissions. Research has demonstrated that such systems can significantly decrease post-harvest losses and enhance the quality of stored produce. By reducing spoilage, farmers can store produce longer, sell at higher prices, and boost their income. A Nigerian study showed that cold storage increased farmers' net sales by nearly 70%. Improved storage leads to fresher produce, enhancing food quality and safety. Additionally, using solar energy reduces reliance on fossil fuels, lowering greenhouse gas emissions and promoting sustainability. Hence, by adopting solar-powered cold storage technology, rural Tigray can improve food security, increase farmers' incomes, and contribute to environmental sustainability.

Project Title: Making chocolate from the desert: mesquite beans as an emerging staple legume in the future of our food system.
Executive Summary: Mesquite is often only associated with barbecue sauce in the current food system, but we think mesquite s headline should hone in on its delicious, nutrient-packed fruit. Mez Foods is dedicated to increasing access and awareness of this super food through thoughtfully crafted CPG products - starting with chocolate alternatives. This project will use grant funding to grow manufacturing capacity to positively impact the mesquite bean farmers of the Southwestern United States, Argentina, and Peru.
Innovation Description: Cacao, the foundation of chocolate products, faces a crisis due to climate change, labor exploitation, and unsustainable farming. With demand for cacao expected to double by 2033 and growing regions shrinking, the industry is under pressure to maintain flavor, affordability, and availability. These challenges call for innovative, sustainable alternatives that address both supply chain vulnerabilities and consumer health concerns. Mesquite offers a game-changing solution. This climate-resilient tree thrives in arid conditions, transforming barren land into thriving forests. Its beans are naturally sweet, high in fiber, and rich in protein, making them an ideal ingredient for crafting healthier alternatives to cacao-based products. Unlike traditional chocolate, mesquite-based bars provide indulgent flavor without bitterness, which allows us to use less sugar in our products and while offering essential macronutrients. Mez Foods partners with farmers who harvest mesquite beans as a supplemental crop, particularly valuable during periods of low soy or wheat yields. The challenge isn t producing mesquite beans but creating finished products that utilize them effectively. Mez Foods has bridged this gap, developing mesquite-based chocolate alternatives that provide the sensory appeal of chocolate while promoting health and sustainability. Our approach supports farmers with diversified income, offers consumers a guilt-free indulgence, and reduces environmental impact by preventing deforestation, combating desertification, and promoting agrobiodiversity. With this grant, Mez Foods will scale production and expand our product offerings, establishing mesquite as a key player in reshaping the global food system and providing a sustainable, healthy alternative to cacao.

Project Title: FarmHive Market: Transforming On-Farm Marketing Through Digital Innovation
Executive Summary: We plan to expand the FarmHive platform to include the FarmHive Market, an online market linkage tool for publishing expected harvest information to potential buyers. As part of our scale-up effort, we have identified agricultural extension workers as important nodes to onboard and support farmers using the platform. We propose to test and release these features in India and Nigeria while measuring the uptake of the tool among farmers, agricultural extension workers and produce buyers.
Innovation Description: Farmers and produce offtakers are often unaware of real-time supply and demand information, contributing to post-harvest losses and reduced efficiencies. Due to low information access, both sides suffer missed market opportunities, leading to food waste and reduced income. Our innovation consists of implementing a real-time data sharing platform that connects farmers with other value chain actors.  We will adopt an existing platform developed at the Migal Galilee Research Institute called FarmHive (www.farmhive.co), a mobile friendly application and website for facilitating information sharing among farmers, agronomists and researchers.  These features include a basic social network (Feed, Posts, Chat, Connections, etc) along with three features specialized to the agricultural sector: the Forum, for agricultural questions and answers, the Library, for agronomic resources, and the Farm Journal. The Farm Journal tool is a digital record of the farm, including cropping history and main activities, that can be easily shared with others such as farm advisors in order to accelerate knowledge sharing and collaboration. This tool will be finalized and adopted for this project to include a market linkage tool as well, FarmHive Market. This platform will enable real-time sharing of buyer and seller information along with contact information. Farmers, or their agricultural advisors, can share on-farm production information including expected and actual harvest quantities. Market players will be given access to the platform to receive the information and contact relevant sellers via phone - increasing market exposure to farm produce while it is still in the ground.

Project Title: Milk with Dignity: Building a Sustainable Dairy Industry for Workers, Farmers, and Consumers Alike
Executive Summary: For the past thirteen years, Latinx immigrant farmworkers in the U.S. Northeast have successfully organized through Migrant Justice, achieving a string of transformative victories. In 2017, Migrant Justice launched Milk with Dignity, a worker-driven program that wins binding agreements with corporations to raise wages, improve labor conditions, and ensure enforceable human rights protections in their dairy supply chains. Funding will support the continued implementation and expansion of the Program.
Innovation Description: Immigrant farmworkers are among the most marginalized and excluded people in the United States. As a legacy of chattel slavery, agriculture work continues to be performed by racialized groups excluded from basic rights afforded to other workers. The dairy industry is no exception, relying on undocumented workers laboring seven days a week, for below minimum wage, living in inhumane housing conditions, and subject to injuries, harassment, and violence.  The Milk with Dignity Program is based on the global model Worker-driven Social Responsibility, which leverages the joint power of workers and consumers worldwide to put pressure on corporations to reform their sourcing practices, redistributing wealth and power throughout their supply chain. The Program partners with corporations and institutions that buy dairy products. Buyers commit to sourcing their milk from farms enrolled in the Milk with Dignity Program and agree to pay a premium to the farms in their supply chains. The farms, in turn, agree to use that premium to improve wages, benefits, health and safety standards, housing conditions, and increase protections against violence, sexual harassment, discrimination, and retaliation.    The Milk with Dignity Program is transforming an industry plagued by severe and persistent human rights violations and putting power into the hands of workers themselves to determine and achieve dignified conditions. Milk with Dignity has resulted in the investment of millions of dollars into improved conditions on dairy farms, building a sustainable dairy industry in which consumers can buy dairy products with the knowledge that they were produced in fair conditions.

Project Title: Take a Teacher To Lunch
Executive Summary: Our Take a Teacher to Lunch program educates teachers on healthy eating and sustainable food practices by hosting catered "lunch-and-learn" style events featuring locally sourced meals, keynote speakers, and engaging activities.  Teachers participate in a full-service catering and event experience designed to enhance teacher appreciation, these events provide tools and resources for educators to promote nutritious habits and food sustainability in their classrooms, fostering consumer trust and advancing healthy diets within the community.
Innovation Description: The Take a Teacher to Lunch program addresses the critical issue of food insecurity and limited access to quality food education in marginalized communities, specifically within Title I schools often located in food deserts.  These communities typically lack access to fresh produce, sustainable food options, and educational resources about healthy eating habits, perpetuating cycles of poor nutrition and health outcomes.  Our program transforms traditional teacher appreciation events into educational opportunities by partnering with restaurants that source locally and practice sustainability.  Teachers are provided with healthy sustainably sourced meals and participate in "lunch-and learn" sessions featuring keynote speakers who are experts in the field and activities that focus on food sustainability, healthy eating, and practical tool they can integrate into their classrooms to also educate their students.  This innovative approach empowers teachers to serve as community ambassadors for food education, directly influencing students and families.  The solution is grounded in the understanding that educators are trusted community leaders, as well as consumers.  By equipping them with knowledge and resources, we extend the impact of our efforts beyond the individual to entire school ecosystems.  Immediate benefits include teacher appreciation, professional growth, and improved access to healthy meals.  Long-term benefits include fostering healthier eating habits, supporting sustainable local food systems, and reducing the environmental impact of food choices. The Moppet Champion initiative trains consumers to promote, sell, and earn income from Moppet products, driving conscious consumer choices and enhancing household income. Farmers are equipped with sustainable practices to optimize yield and reduce environmental impact. To solve the major challenge of lack of market access, Moppet s solar-powered production facilities provide a consistent market for these farmers, ensuring a steady income, and making affordable food accessible. Additionally, the Moppet WEM Hub empowers women entrepreneurs with production facilities for food product and safety training , building economic resilience and community-driven food systems. The solution is based on scientific insights into biofortification s role in addressing malnutrition and the need for renewable energy to tackle climate-induced challenges. By integrating agricultural innovation with energy efficiency, this approach provides a scalable and sustainable model. Immediate benefits include improved farmer incomes, access to affordable and nutritious food, and reduced food waste. Sustainable benefits encompass improved public health, strengthened local economies, climate-resilient agriculture, reduced carbon emissions, and a food system that ensures equitable access to safe and nutritious food for all.

These farmers will not only benefit from the access to market, we will also offer them trainings in Good Agricultural Practices and also offer them farm inputs, such as certified seed. Our food products are already in retail shops across the country and we are also selling to NGOs that run child feeding programs. Project Title: "Enhancing Climate-Resilient Sunflower  Farming for Sustainable Livelihoods and Environmental Regeneration"
Executive Summary: This project empowers smallholder farmers in semi-arid regions through climate-resilient sunflower farming practices like deep mulching, organic manure application, and crop rotation. By enhancing soil fertility, mitigating drought effects, and restoring degraded land, the initiative boosts crop yields and farmer incomes. To maximize benefits, we also focus on value addition by producing cold-pressed sunflower oil and sunflower seed cake animal feed supplements.  The innovation leverages scientific insights on water retention, soil structure improvement, and sustainable land management. Deep mulching minimizes water loss, regulates soil temperature, and prevents weed competition, while organic manure improves nutrient availability and soil health. Value addition transforms raw sunflower seeds into high-quality products, boosting profitability and creating diversified income streams.  Benefits  Farmers: Increased yields, stable incomes, and access to value-added markets for sunflower oil and animal feed supplements.  Environment: Regeneration of degraded land, enhanced soil health, and reduced carbon footprints.  Communities: Strengthened food security, job creation, and economic resilience.  Society: Contribution to sustainable agricultural value chains and global food system transformation.   This solution ensures immediate benefits, such as higher yields and value-added revenue, while addressing long-term environmental and socio-economic challenges, positioning farmers as leaders in climate-smart and value-driven agriculture.

Project Title: Reducing post-harvest losses with solar-powered IoT cooling hubs and sustainable preservation technologies
Executive Summary: Our project combats post-harvest losses by providing solar-powered IoT cooling hubs and a plant-based edible coating, extending the shelf life of perishable produce from 2 to 21 days. By offering affordable, sustainable solutions, we empower smallholder farmers, market grocers, and cooperatives to reduce waste, increase incomes, and enhance food security. With a growing customer base and proven impact, we aim to revolutionize agricultural value chains in Uganda, Zimbabwe, and beyond.
Innovation Description: In Uganda and Zimbabwe, over 50% of perishable produce spoils due to inadequate storage and cooling facilities, leading to significant post-harvest losses, reduced incomes for farmers, food insecurity, and environmental waste. This challenge is particularly relevant in rural and peri-urban areas where access to electricity and modern storage solutions is limited.  Our innovative solution combines solar-powered IoT cooling hubs and MunaFresh , a plant-based edible coating, to address this issue. The cooling hubs extend the shelf life of perishable produce from 2 to 21 days, while MunaFresh  further preserves fruits and vegetables by reducing moisture loss and microbial growth. These technologies are affordable and accessible, with farmers paying as little as $0.40 per crate per day, ensuring widespread adoption.  This solution is driven by insights into renewable energy, IoT technology, and agricultural science, designed to provide a sustainable, off-grid alternative to conventional cooling systems. Immediate benefits include a 40% reduction in post-harvest losses, a 30% increase in farmers  incomes, and improved food availability for consumers. Long-term, it supports environmental sustainability by reducing food waste and greenhouse gas emissions, and it boosts rural economies by creating jobs and supporting agribusinesses.  By transforming agricultural value chains, this project empowers smallholder farmers, grocers, and communities to achieve greater food security, economic resilience, and environmental sustainability.

Executive Summary: The project aims to combat malnutrition and address lower urinary tract syndrome in mature males by contributing to the sustainable production of pumpkins through the precise identification of disease-causing pathogens and the extraction and commercialization of pumpkin seed oil as a functional food for culinary uses. Furthermore, the project is aimed at increasing a critical mass of professionals in pumpkin plant pathology for sustainable pumpkin production in the region.
Innovation Description: The project aims to enhance disease prevention for sustainable pumpkin production through the precise identification of pathogens causing the diseases and to build a critical mass of human resources for improved pumpkin production. The project also aims at the formulation and commercialization of pumpkin seed oil for culinary purposes. Pumpkins are priced for their nutritious fruits, leaves, and seeds. In Uganda, the production of pumpkins is compromised by several diseases (Masika et al., 2022), affecting the quantity and quality, limiting their usage (Savary et al., 2012). Disease control will lead to increased production hence spurring value addition efforts towards production of pumpkin seed oil. Advanced molecular and sequencing techniques will be used to detect fungal pathogens for improved management. Sequencing allows for the identification of previously unknown and novel microbes (Ansorge, 2009). The project is further aimed at the formulation and commercialization of pumpkin seed oil, which has been used in culinary and traditional medicine for millennia as a functional food (Ceclu et al., 2020). In our previous study, viruses affecting pumpkin production were identified in pooled samples, and study for the formulation of pumpkin seed oil and its use in the management of lower urinary tract infections in rats has shown great promise. Identification of pathogens affecting pumpkin production will lead to better management of diseases and improved production. Formulation and commercialization of pumpkin seed oil for culinary purposes will increase access to notorious foods in schools and communities. This will lead to increased food, nutrition and income security.

Project Title: Empowering Communities by Transforming Agricultural Waste into Nutritious Food, Renewable Energy, and Soil Health Circular Economy Solutions
Executive Summary: Our project empowers Ugandan rural farming communities to convert agricultural waste into valuable resources within a circular farming model. We transform waste into substrates for producing nutritious mushrooms and generate renewable energy through biogas systems using spoiled and subpar mushrooms. Additionally, contribute to soil health improvement with champost. This circular economy approach addresses food insecurity, creates income opportunities, and promotes sustainable agricultural practices, contributing to environmental resilience and community well-being while fostering regenerative farming methods.
Innovation Description: Uganda faces significant challenges related to food loss, food insecurity, and poverty, exacerbated by practices such as bush burning, inadequate waste management, climate variability and environmental degradation. Approximately 797,000 people in Uganda are currently experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity, with projections indicating this number could rise to 953,000 by mid-2025 if no interventions are made. Additionally, about 20.3% of the population lives below the poverty line, and one in four children under five is stunted due to malnutrition.  Our project addresses these critical issues by transforming agricultural waste into valuable resources through a circular economy model, reducing the environmental impact of agricultural  systems and reclaiming value for the poor rural agragrian communities. We convert agricultural by-products, such as husks and stalks, into substrates for growing nutritious mushrooms to enhance food security by providing access to nutrient-rich food. Furthermore, we generate renewable energy from spoiled and subpar mushrooms using biogas systems, which mitigates reliance on traditional energy sources.  The scientific insight behind our solution is rooted in waste valorization principles that emphasize reusing agricultural by-products to create sustainable systems. The immediate benefits for farmers include increased income opportunities through mushroom sales and improved soil health via the production of champost. Ultimately, our initiative promotes sustainable agricultural practices, enhances community resilience, and contributes to achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2 (Zero Hunger), 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 13 (Climate Action), fostering long-term benefits for society and the environment.

Project Title: Solid state fungal fermentation platform for nutrient dense high protein ingredients
Executive Summary: Protein ingredients are currently produced via resource intensive processing methods, leading to negative health outcomes and outsized carbon footprints. Mycsology Foods solves these problems by fermenting plant inputs using fungi, to transform the nutritional and organoleptic profiles of the starting substrates with minimal processing. While fermented foods are consumed globally, for example cheese, sourdough and yogurt, they represent isolated data points in the vast, multidimensional space of possible productive fermentations. We are developing a scalable and high-throughput solid state fermentation system to rapidly sample and profile candidate solid state fermentation parameters. We plan to launch with a DTC brand to demonstrate the utility of this platform and gain consumer traction. Following market validation, we aim partner with food manufacturers to supply them with ingredients that have tailor-made nutrient, taste and allergen profiles.

Project Title: Improved agricultural practices that increase yields and preserve soil health in the Democratic Republic of Congo
Executive Summary: Nabahya Food Institute (NFI) is a non-profit organization based in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to bring local farmers work in cooperatives, mitigating the cycle of poverty, starvation and climate change while promoting access to clean Energy and Resilient Food Systems with commitment to tackling the dual challenge of increasing food production and protecting natural resources and the environment. NFI is a grant award winner for the Water and Energy for Food Grand Challenge for Development (WE4F). WE4F is an international initiative jointly supported by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, the European Union, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Government of the Netherlands, the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation (Norad), the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida), and the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID). NFI is also a grant award winner of the TerraFund for AFR100 Landscapes Restoration Champions, a program jointly run by World Resources Institute, One Tree Planted and Realize Impact.    Field activities:  -	Regenerative Agriculture  -	Clean Energy  -	Reforestation and Conservation  -	Rural Women Empowerment    We produce, process and do research that helps to building equitable, inclusive and sustainable food systems in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Our work develops resilience among communities severely affected by starvation and climate change.  Nabahya Food Institute (NFI) produces briquettes at scale and promotes them as an alternative source of household and food processing energy in order to save the environment and improve livelihood of smallholder farmers. The briquettes bring a unique approach of cooking food without destroying trees. Briquettes are made using crop residues, biomass, dead leaves, palm shells, coconut shells, maize stalks. This innovation reduces the household cooking energy expenses, boosts food productivity, avoids air pollution, protects natural resources and the environment, empowers women, and helps consumers save time and money.    NFI also help farmers’ yields through the production of bio-fertilizers and bio-pesticides.         Our Reforestation and Conservation program brings local farmers to reforest the bare places within the Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo to create community forests which restore soil nutrient, animal habitats and biodiversity.  NFI engages the Community (individual and community engagement). They are grouped in cooperatives according to their respective villages. Cooperative members agree to follow a set of community-based rules. These include their right to benefit from their work through legal harvesting of tree products (fruit, honey, medicines, etc). They provide green manure for nursery preparation and organize a daily patrolling team to monitor our planted trees.   To empower women, NFI has set up Farmer-Field Schools to teach small-scale farmers - of which the majority are women - the techniques of using Bio-fertilizers and Bio-pesticides to increase their agricultural yields. No chemical additives.  Smallholder farmers follow an intercropping approach by using fodder trees and fruit trees.  We focus on tree species like Faidherbia albida, Moringa oleifera and Gliricidia sepium. These species deposit abundant quantities of organic fertilizer by falling leaves and pods onto the food crops to provide nutrients and increase yields. They also provide livestock and bee forage.

Project Title: Nagida leverages technology to optimize the staple food value chain for businesses & individual consumers while supporting local farmers with access to affordable inputs, financing & technical support
Executive Summary: NAGIDA is a tech-driven platform optimizing the staple food value chain end-to-end. It empowers individuals and businesses with access to fresh, affordable, & hygienic staples with "customized processing" options while supporting local farmers with affordable inputs, financing, and technical assistance. Focused on sustainability and efficiency, NAGIDA addresses food inflation, supply chain inefficiencies, and operational challenges, promoting rural & urban economic impact & creating a scalable solution with a clear competitive edge in local and global
Innovation Description: 70% out of the 80% of smallholder farmers in Nigeria live below $5 and 58% of this live below the extreme poverty line despite their hard work, amounting to over 40 million local farmers across the 6 geo-political zones of the country. With Nigeria's Inflation reaching over 39%, These farmers face significant challenges such as High input costs, finance support, post-harvest losses which have spiked suicide rates among rural farmers, limited access to sustainable farming techniques, logistic support & direct off-takers leading to inefficiencies, Inequality & exploitation from middle-men living with them within same community who pay these farmers stipends to farm on their own land and take over all harvests. In addition, Over 19.8 million unemployed Women and youths in both rural and urban living below the poverty line lack adequate training, resources, and market access needed to explore small-scale agribusinesses that could boost their incomes and stabilize local food supplies. These challenges further exacerbate food insecurity, Social breakdown, and inequalities in society. Through an innovative and state-of-the-art technology-driven platform supported by AI, IoT & Blockchain, Nagida bridges these gaps by empowering farmers with affordable inputs, financing, technical support, logistics, and direct market access. Unemployed women and youths receive training and are onboarded as SME suppliers, fostering economic stability. For consumers and businesses, Nagida offers customizable solutions for accessing fresh, affordable, and hygienic staples tailored to specific preferences, from fresh produce-preprocessed-processed-meal kits. This helps individuals save time and navigate inflation, while businesses optimize operations, cut costs,and manage inventory efficiently.

Project Title: Building a post-harvest chain platform that allows rural farmers to store, manage and monetize their produce
Executive Summary: Intended to address key agricultural challenges related to poor post-harvest management, recognizing the multi-dimensional nature of poverty where technology is one of the factors contributing to livelihood improvement, the project will enable effective management of post-harvest processes for at least 2000 farmers cultivating maize, beans, rice and grains/pulses, so they will scale to deliver surplus harvests to markets with a peace-of-mind.
Innovation Description: The agricultural supply chain in Uganda is unnecessarily long, intricately disconnected and disintegrated. The mostly smallholder farmers suffer a significant gap in connectedness and infrastructure, and as a result, they lose 30-50% or 120-170kgs (over 1.3 billion tons) of produce annually to post-harvest spoilage. Add climate change to this scenario, problems multiply because the food spoilage process is often quickly expedited, forcing farmers to quickly sell what they can - and at huge discounts, or risk their produce rotting, keeping them trapped in poverty cycles. In addition, urban dwellers also find it hard to access quality, safe and fresh food due to massive distribution delays and poor handling by third parties, leading to massive food waste   the cost of which is passed on to end consumers who are paying high price points, often 200% on average for semi-fresh food from food retailers.  To protect food security in Uganda, Nampya Farmers Market provides solar-powered micro-warehouses near farm clusters, making it easier and more affordable for smallholder farmers to store and insure more of their harvest. We also run a USSD-based, tech-enabled food supply platform connecting rural farmers directly to urban food retailers and off-takers, bypassing exploitative middlemen. This allows farmers to sell their produce at fair prices, promoting economic self-sufficiency and supporting sustainable food supply chains. With mobile money payments integrated into the system, Nampya facilitates smooth, direct transactions, helping greengrocers, hotels and restaurants source better-quality and competitively-priced food straight from the farmgate to their doorstep.

Project Title: Nandi hills animal feeds junction
Executive Summary: Nandi Hills Animal Feeds Junction, founded in 2019, specializes in producing affordable, quality animal feeds and silage for smallholder farmers. We aim to scale operations by acquiring advanced equipment to improve production, efficiency, and accessibility, empowering farmers to maximize their yields and profits.
Innovation Description: Nandi Hills Animal Feeds Junction has developed an innovative solution to transform animal feed production and silage management for smallholder farmers. The initiative focuses on acquiring advanced machinery such as a pellet-making machine, modern silage chopper, silage baler, and feed mixer, alongside a tractor for transport and field operations.  Problem Solved: Smallholder farmers struggle with inefficient feed production, poor feed quality, and high transportation costs. These challenges lead to lower livestock productivity and reduced income. Relevance: Access to high-quality, affordable feed is critical for sustainable livestock farming, especially in regions reliant on small-scale agriculture for food security and income generation.  Solution: The innovation combines modern equipment with localized expertise to produce pelletized animal feeds, uniformly mixed rations, and baled silage. This approach ensures affordability, consistent quality, and ease of transportation.  Scientific/Technical Insight: The adoption of pelletization enhances feed digestibility and reduces wastage. Balers preserve silage for extended periods, while mixers ensure nutrient uniformity, directly addressing feed quality issues.  Benefits:  1. Farmers: Increased livestock productivity and income through affordable, high-quality feed.   2. Communities: Improved food security due to enhanced livestock production.   3. Environment: Reduced feed waste and efficient use of by-products like maize stalks.   4. Society: Economic empowerment of rural communities by reducing dependence on imported feeds.    This solution fosters immediate benefits while supporting long-term sustainability, resilience, and environmental stewardship.

Project Title: Lamatu Precision fertilization for sustainable food system and soil health
Executive Summary: Lamatu champions AI-navigated, advanced non-polymer nanoparticle as the core component of its technology for controlled-release fertilizers. By integrating smart nutrient delivery systems, the project aims to enhance crop yields, improve soil health, and reduce environmental impacts resulting from fertilizer inefficiency, primarily nitrogen pollution. Through precision fertilization, Lamatu warrants  environmentally responsible fertilization practices, ensuring long-term food security while fostering harmony between agriculture and the planet's ecosystems.
Innovation Description: The global agricultural system faces significant challenges related to the inefficiency of traditional chemical fertilizers, with nitrogen fertilizers among the key contributor. These fertilizers are subjected to nutrient loss, often observed through leaching, volatilization, and runoff. As a result,  plant nutrient uptake decreases creating a starvation situation  besides, contributing to environmental pollution. Fertilizer inefficiency results in farmers needing to apply fertilizers multiple times throughout the growing season, which increases labor costs and fuel consumption. This is compounded by the rising prices of chemical fertilizers, which have been heavily impacted by global supply chain disruptions and the increasing cost of raw materials, such as natural gas, which is a key component in fertilizer production (Haber process). Chemical fertilizers are primarily derived from non-renewable resources, such as phosphate rock and natural gas. As these resources become scarcer and more expensive, the long-term sustainability of conventional fertilization practices is increasingly questionable. Furthermore, the labour shortage in agriculture exacerbates the problem, as farmers struggle to manage multiple fertilizer applications and additional labour costs.   Lamatu offers a sustainable solution by using controlled-release fertilizers (CRFs) with coatings made from nanoparticles derived from rice husk agro-waste. This renewable material gradually releases nutrients, improving fertilizer efficiency and reducing nutrient loss due to leaching and runoff. By minimizing the need for multiple applications, it reduces labor, fuel, and equipment costs. Additionally, the rice husk coating provides secondary nutrients like silica, benefiting soil health. This approach not only cuts production costs but also supports environmentally friendly and sustainable agricultural practices.

Submitting Organization: National Agricultural Research Organization (NARO) - National Semi-Arid Resources Research Institute (NaSARRI)
Project Title: Enhancing household nutrition through adoption of climate resilient greengram and sorghum varieties and biodynamic manures in drier regions of Uganda
Executive Summary: The semi-arid regions of Uganda are faced with high malnutrition and extreme household poverty due to low crop productivity caused by declining soil fertility, frequent droughts, and the cultivation of low-yielding varieties with low levels of nutrients. Therefore, the proposed project intends to validate and promote climate-resilient greengram and sorghum varieties that are high in nutrient levels, and locally made biodynamic manures to enhance crop productivity and address the household food and nutritional insecurity challenge.
Innovation Description: The semi-arid regions of Uganda are characterized by low agricultural productivity, high malnutrition, and extreme poverty (UBOS 2017).  The main causes of this are; frequent droughts, declining soil fertility, and cultivation of varieties that are low yielding and low in nutrient content. Given that agriculture is the dominant occupation of farmers in the regions, validating, disseminating, and promoting improved agricultural technologies adapted to semi-arid conditions is key in addressing household food and nutritional insecurity.  Adopting resilient greengram and sorghum varieties with a high level of nutrients could enhance crop productivity and household food nutrition.  The National Agricultural Research Organization has developed greengram and sorghum varieties lines that are tolerant to drought and rich in iron, zinc, calcium, and carbohydrates.  The improved greengram and sorghum lines and locally made biodynamic manures are ready for on-farm evaluation before they can be disseminated to the farming communities in the region.   The inclusion of these greengram and sorghum varieties in diets will lead to the well-being of children, expectant and lactating mothers, and school children. Greengram is known to enrich soil fertility, therefore, its cultivation and application of locally made biodynamic manures would improve and sustain soil fertility.  Therefore, this project proposal is submitted to the Institute of Food Technology for financial support to enable the project team to conduct on-farm evaluation and dissemination of the developed improved greengram and sorghum varieties and locally made biodynamic manures to the farming communities to enhance household nutrition and income security in the project area.

Submitting Organization: National Root Crops Research Institute, U,mudike. Nigeria
Project Title: Women-led Revolution for Resilience: Climate-Smart Cassava, Sweet Potato, Cocoyam, and Nigerian Orphaned Fruit Trees for a Food-Secure Nigeria (WORR)
Executive Summary: The Women-led Revolution for Resilience project supports vulnerable women farmers in Abia and Ebonyi states. We're empowering 600 women through training and climate-resilient crop distribution. Our goal is to improve their livelihoods, promote sustainable farming practices, and drive progress toward the UN's Sustainable Development Goals. By working together with local stakeholders, we aim to enhance the women's capacity to adapt to climate change, improve soil fertility, increase crop yields. and secure women farmers future .
Innovation Description: Climate change is having a devastating impact on smallholder women farmers in Nigeria, particularly in the southeastern states of Abia and Ebonyi. According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), climate change is projected to lead to a decline in agricultural productivity, exacerbating poverty and food insecurity among vulnerable communities (IPCC, 2019). In Nigeria, women make up approximately 60% of the poorest people, with limited access to resources, markets, and financial services (World Bank, 2020). Our project addresses this pressing issue by promoting climate-resilient agriculture and agroforestry practices among women farmers. We're introducing improved crop varieties and Nigerian orphaned fruit trees, which are better adapted to the changing climate. Each of the 600 selected women will receive 5 bundles each of improved cassava, sweet potato and 5kg of improved cocoyam seeds. Again, each of the women will receive budded fruit tree seedlings of African star apple, African pear and Bush mango. Furthermore, by providing training and technical assistance, we're empowering women farmers to improve their crop yields, increase their income, enhance their food security and contribute to biodiversity conservation through agroforestry. Our project's innovative approach is rooted in scientific research, which highlights the importance of agroforestry and climate-resilient agriculture in enhancing the resilience of smallholder farmers to climate change (FAO, 2017). We strongly believe and confident that by adopting this approach, our project will have a lasting impact on the lives of women farmers and their communities and prepare our women farmers to contribute to seeding the future. initiative.

Executive Summary: Our innovation transforms sorghum (a staple cereal) into more nutrient-dense products that are affordable, accessible, and desirable. Central to our success is collaboration and building a circular economy to ensure that our fortification ingredients are organic, locally available, and culturally accepted. Innovation Description: According to the 2020 Kenya Demographic and Health Survey (KDHS), 41% of children under five and 24% of women of reproductive age suffer from anemia (Kenya National Bureau of Statistics, 2020), leading to poor birth outcomes, maternal mortality, and developmental delays. Furthermore, chronic malnutrition has led to stunting in 18% of children under five nationwide, with Siaya (19.2%) recording among the highest rates, affecting children's growth, cognitive development, and future productivity. Promoting indigenous crops like sorghum, amaranth, and orange-fleshed sweet potatoes that are rich in iron, zinc, and vitamin A offers a sustainable solution. This project utilizes organic acid-rich plant foodstuffs and beta-carotene-rich plants, such as guava fruit and amaranth leaves, to improve the mineral bioaccessibility of whole grain sorghum flour and porridges in order to help reduce malnutrition in the target communities. Findings from our proof of concept proof stage show a formulation/recipe ratio of 100:1 (sorghum: natural plant fortificants) citric acid to iron molar ratio would yield maximum nutrient bioavailability in a fortified flour/porridge. Most of these nutritious fortificants (fruits and indigenous vegetables) go to waste due to their perishable nature. Project Title: Empowering Local Organic Growers: Certification & Capacity Building for Sustainable Growth
Executive Summary: This project empowers local organic grower groups to meet certification requirements and supports the certification process for premium pricing. Many regions in Nepal are organically farmed but lack evidence to assure consumers. The project trains Internal Inspectors to assist growers and offers certification services. After this period, the groups will be fully certified and self-sustaining, able to continue the certification process independently.
Innovation Description: The demand for organic foods is rapidly growing, however, many local organic grower groups of in rural Nepal remain uncertified. This stems from two key challenges: a lack of skilled personnel to guide farmers in certification processes such as Internal Control Systems, inspections, and documentation, and the high cost of organic certification at least at the initial stages.  Nep.Cert addresses these issues by training local human resources and certifying products without imposing financial burdens on farmers. Over three years, farmers achieve full certification, enabling their products to bear the certification logo and command premium market prices. This boosts producer confidence and equips them to continue certification independently, creating a self-sustaining model. Successful examples inspire replication in other regions without external support. The project emphasizes organic farming by utilizing local renewable resources, contributing to increased farmer income, better food quality, and biodiversity conservation. Local certification forms the foundation for international accreditation, enabling farmers to transition from seasonal crops to high-value herbs and spices with global market potential. Nepal, rich in medicinal and aromatic plants, holds immense potential to supply niche Himalayan products globally. By empowering farmers with certification and market access, this project strengthens rural economies, enhances food security, and positions Nepal as a leader in sustainable organic farming.

Project Title: Climate-resilient nutritious crop irrigation system
Executive Summary: Provide climate-resilient Nutritious crop irrigation system powered by solar and artificial intelligence driven to optimize energy and water use for farming, helping millions Nutritious crop growers/vegetables, fruits and cereal farmers adapt to unpredictable climate patterns while enhancing nutritious crop yields eliminating acute food insecurity and malnutrition. The system uses Chabot and bulk SMS technology sending SMS to Nutritious crop growers with tailored tips and reminders for optimal long term sustainable Nutrition crop irrigation farming.
Innovation Description: Problem; Currently, less than 5% of cultivated land in sub-Saharan Africa is irrigated. The reliance on rainfed agriculture prevents farmers from cultivating high-value nutritious crops that often need large amounts of water that are applied more frequently. Some vegetable crops consist mostly of water, and their yield and quality, deteriorate rapidly under water stress. Rainfed agriculture limits smallholder production and profitability, particularly under climate change. It is therefore associated with higher food insecurity, poor diet quality, and high seasonal variability in diets.   Solution; Provide climate-resilient Nutritious crop irrigation system powered by solar and artificial intelligence driven to optimize energy and water use for farming, helping millions Nutritious crop growers/vegetables, fruits and cereal farmers adapt to unpredictable climate patterns while enhancing nutritious crop yields eliminating acute food insecurity and malnutrition at the same time mitigate carbon dioxide emissions. The system uses Chabot and bulk SMS technology sending SMS to Nutritious crop growers with tailored tips and reminders for optimal long term sustainable Nutrition crop irrigation farming. Nutritious crop growers are registered to data base and receive electronic cards which saves as digital wallet used for paying irrigation bills on pay as you irrigate or pay per use. Nutritious crop growers who are youth and women with serious financial limitation have access to on credit and installment purchase as a special program allowing use the irrigation service and pays later after harvesting. We provide training to Nutritious crop growers using FAO climate smart irrigation training curriculum ensuring Nutritious crop sustainable farming.

Project Title: Scaling Sustainable Aquaponics for Food Security and Climate Resilience in Africa
Executive Summary: Our project scales innovative aquaponic systems (growing both fish and soilless crops in one system) to empower smallholder farmers in Africa with sustainable food production. By combining fish/crop farming, our solution optimises resource use, enhances food security, and builds climate resilience. By also integrating AI-driven monitoring and solar energy, we ensure efficiency, affordability, and sustainability. This project addresses food insecurity, promotes economic growth, and creates scalable impact for underserved communities, aligning with global sustainability goals.
Innovation Description: Our innovative aquaponic system addresses critical challenges of food insecurity, resource inefficiency, and environmental degradation in underserved regions. The problem is urgent: conventional farming consumes excessive water and land, depletes soil fertility, and struggles to meet the demands of growing populations, especially in climate-vulnerable areas. On average smallholder farmers earn $160/yr putting them under the poverty income line.  Our system integrates fish farming and hydroponics, creating a closed-loop system where fish waste nourishes crops and plants purify water. This drastically reduces water usage by up to 95% compared to traditional agriculture, requires less land, and eliminates harmful chemical fertilisers. Solar-powered AI-driven monitoring ensures optimal production, reduces operational costs, and empowers farmers with real-time insights for decision-making.  The innovation emerged from scientific and technical insights into circular food production systems and the need for scalable, low-cost solutions in resource-limited environments. Our solution directly benefits smallholder farmers by increasing yields, diversifying income streams, and improving food security. Communities gain access to affordable, nutritious produce while reducing environmental impact. The scalable design enables rapid adoption, creating ripple effects of economic and social resilience.  Immediate benefits include increased food production efficiency (3000% more fish and 700% more crops in the same space), reduced resource consumption (using 95% less water), and farmer empowerment through accessible technology that increases their income by up to 10x! Long-term, our innovation builds climate resilience, fosters sustainable agricultural practices, and contributes to global food system transformation.

Project Title: Wood to Food: Building an enduring alternative to animal-based food products
Executive Summary: We develop highly sustainable meat alternatives by transforming woody biomass waste streams into fermentable substrates, grow specialty mushrooms on them and process the mushrooms into delicious food products. When scaling up we will partner globally with the forestry industry to produce the substrates, with farmers to cultivate the mushrooms and produce the fungal protein food, and with food services to serve delicious, affordable, healthy and easy to use food to their customers.
Innovation Description: The problem is that animal-based protein production has massive negative impact on climate, environment, biodiversity and animal welfare, and uses too much land. In addition, many of the currently available meat alternatives have issues with taste and texture, have too many ingredients, making them unhealthier again, are too expensive and use the same agricultural land to be produced.  By using woody biomass as the main feedstock, we require virtually no agricultural land to produce our products, while replacing meat will free up large areas of agricultural land, that can then be used for reforestation, nature development, extensivation of other agricultural production. (sustainable benefits)  Prior research and development in using wood as a carbon source for food and feed production led to the idea and insight that wood-based edible mushrooms can do exactly this. The technological process development involves developing optimal pre-treatment conditions for the woody biomass to obtain  the most productive substrates.  By partnering with farmers to participate in this production they will play a more meaningful role in the protein transition by producing higher margin products that just soybeans or peas for the protein industry.  By partnering with food services they will get more and better options to serve their (vegan, vegetarian, flexitarian) customers delicious food, and the products can be easier tailored to their customers taste and preferences compared with meat alternatives produced in large centralized industrial factories.

Project Title: Promoting Bio-Fertilizer Adoption for Sustainable Farming in Tanzania's Drought-Prone Regions
Executive Summary: NovFeed Project combats soil degradation in Tanzania by introducing biofertilizers that restore soil health, boost crop yields, and reduce dependence on chemical inputs. The initiative enhances food security, creates jobs, and increases farmer incomes by leveraging Local Service Providers (LSPs) for farmer training, technical support, and market access. This sustainable approach empowers communities, fosters economic growth, and strengthens resilience against climate challenges, ensuring a more productive and environmentally friendly agricultural system.
Innovation Description: Soil degradation affects over 65% of Tanzania s arable land, driven by erosion, nutrient depletion, and heavy reliance on chemical fertilizers. These fertilizers worsen soil acidity, reduce productivity, and contribute to greenhouse gas emissions, threatening food security and farmer livelihoods. Crop yields, such as maize, have declined by 40% over two decades, further exacerbating food insecurity.  Our innovation introduces biofertilizers as a sustainable alternative to chemical inputs. These eco-friendly products restore soil health by enriching it with essential nutrients and beneficial microorganisms. Unlike chemical fertilizers, biofertilizers reduce soil acidity, improve fertility, and enhance water retention, creating sustainable conditions for agriculture. The solution draws on scientific insights into microbial soil enrichment and its ability to stabilize yields under changing climatic conditions.  The project integrates Local Service Providers (LSPs) to ensure farmers access biofertilizers, receive training, and adopt climate-smart techniques. This decentralized model promotes adoption, enhances technical support, and creates income-generating opportunities for LSPs.  Farmers benefit immediately through increased yields, reduced input costs, and improved incomes. Long-term benefits include healthier soils, reduced emissions, and greater food security. Communities gain from resilient agricultural systems, while the environment benefits from reduced chemical runoff and enhanced biodiversity. This innovation empowers farmers with sustainable tools, addressing pressing challenges while fostering economic growth and environmental protection.

Project Title: Innovation for a Healthy Diet in Uganda: NutriPosh Program
Executive Summary: NutriPosh Program has already incorporated consumer feedback during the development of affordable, trusted, safe and nutritious fortified composite flours for complementary feeding and school feeding programs in Uganda. Besides providing enhanced nutrition through the inclusion of pumpkin seeds in stable composite maize flours, NutriPosh sources ingredients produced through regenerative agricultural practices, utilizes solar powered dehydration technologies in its composite flour production and uses biodegradable packaging. NutriPosh approach ensures environmental sustainability across the entire supply chain.
Innovation Description: In 2023, 37.7 million Ugandans could not afford a healthy diet. Malnutrition accounts for 4 in every 10 child deaths in Uganda. 764,576 children are underweight (too small for their age), 228,584 are wasted  (too thin for their height), and 2.4 million Ugandan children are stunted (too short for their age) (UNICEF, 2024).  Mandatory fortification applies to large mills with an output capacity of >20 metric tons (MT) per day, in Uganda. But most schools and households usually prepare meals using unfortified maize flours purchased from small mills, who according to the Food and Drugs (Food Fortification) Regulations, 2005, are not required to fortify   as their daily output capacity is  20 MT.   Most students in Uganda come from "food insecure households  and  often depend on school meals to meet their daily energy and nutritional requirements. If the school meals remain innutritious, the risk of children suffering from micronutrient and omega 3 deficiencies is increased; and this negatively impacts their cognitive health and educational outcomes.  NutriPosh program benefits include; Farmers: NutriPosh Program accelerates uptake of regenerative agricultural practices; increases crop resilience against extreme weather and climate change; improves crop yields; and diversifies income streams.  Schools: NutriPosh Program increases conscious consumerism; minimizes age-for-grade heterogeneity; and helps schoolchildren perform academically well.  Society: NutriPosh Program increases conscious purchasing among nursing mothers and caregivers with post-6months old infants;  stimulates cognitive development; and increase children s chances of academic success.  Environment: NutriPosh Program promotes sustainable carbon capture and storage, at every step of the value chain.

Project Title: Solar UV Technology for Cocoa Honey Preservation and Transforming By-products into Superfoods in Regenerative Food Systems
Executive Summary: Our project uses solar UV technology to preserve cocoa honey, transforming agricultural by-products into high-value superfoods within regenerative food systems. By empowering smallholders with innovative processing and traceability solutions, we enhance sustainability, reduce food waste, and improve livelihoods in the cocoa value chain. With strategic partnerships and a scalable model, we aim to deliver nutritious and deliciosus upcycled products while setting new standards in sustainable food innovation.
Innovation Description: Our project tackles the pressing issue of waste and inefficiency in the cocoa supply chain, where 52,000 tons of byproducts are discarded annually in Brazil. Among these, cocoa honey a nutrient-rich byproduct with natural sweetening and antioxidant properties is often wasted due to microbial spoilage and inadequate preservation methods. To address this, we developed an innovative mobile solar UV technology that stabilizes cocoa honey directly on farms, reducing microbial activity, extending its shelf life, and preserving its properties for transformation into a natural sweetener for superfoods, including the world s first zero-fat chocolate enriched with vitamins and antioxidants. This is especially relevant as the global food system struggles to meet the nutritional needs of 10 billion people by 2050 while reducing waste and environmental impact. Our solution utilizes the germicidal effects of UV light to disrupt microbial DNA, combined with a custom-designed pilot reactor to enhance UV penetration and microbial inactivation. Computational modeling optimizes this scalable process under varying environmental conditions, ensuring efficiency. The preserved nutritional and functional properties of cocoa honey are maintained in superfood formulations. The benefits are wide-ranging. Smallholder farmers gain a sustainable revenue stream, increasing their income by up to 35% per harvest. Consumers and industries benefit from healthier, nutrient-rich alternatives to cane sugar, which is linked to obesity and diabetes. Environmentally, our approach reduces cocoa waste by 40% and promotes regenerative food systems. By transforming waste into high-value products, our innovation reduces environmental impact, supports healthier diets, and fosters sustainable consumption, setting new standards in food innovation.

Project Title: Food Identity: a path to a food system s approach with future
Executive Summary: This project aims to empower knowledge on food identity upon multiple stakeholders in the food sector. It focuses on three main objectives: provide specialized training to various entities (municipalities, schools and restaurants) to improve their food offer; promote food identity among producers to preserve ancient seeds; inspire individuals to make food choices with more social and environmental responsability. Together, these efforts aim to build resilient and sustainable food systems for the future.
Innovation Description: The food identity of a territory is the essence that allows it to be recognized in terms of food. It consists of the characteristics that, despite the normal dynamics of change, remain and enable continuity. This project addresses the decline of primary sectors like agriculture, challenges associated with rural depopulation, the underutilization of local resources, and the loss of food traditions that are intrinsic to territorial food identity. Additionally, it responds to consumer trends seeking more local and authentic experiences, starting with the food they eat.  Promoting and providing training on food identity of a territory is essential in the context of building sustainable and resilient communities.   This systemic approach benefits the environment and economy and reinvigorates local pride and the sense of belonging, promoting a vision where territories are recognized as exemplary models of balance, sustainability, and innovation. It s relevant since it aligns with global priorities, such as the preservation of cultural heritage, sustainable development, and food security.   The solution is grounded in the insights and methodologies developed from the creation of Manuals of Food Identity, which involved comprehensive territorial and anthropological studies across 31 portuguese municipalities.  An aspect of this approach was the individualized mentorship, effective in unlocking stalled dynamics, reactivating suspended initiatives, and crafting forward-looking strategies.  Immediate benefits of this project include improved market access and training for farmers, education on sustainability for schools and facilitated link between tourism and agriculture. Long-term benefits feature economic resilience, healthier communities, biodiversity conservation, and strengthened local food systems.

This holistic strategy ensures that Indigenous youth excel academically and flourish in their careers while maintaining their cultural identities. Addressing gaps in education and employment, the initiative empowers youth to become leaders, role models, and agents of change within their communities.  The solution is deeply rooted in cultural relevance, ensuring all resources and programs honour Indigenous traditions while providing modern skills necessary for success. The initiative enhances the community's ability to grow sustainably by uniting Indigenous wisdom with contemporary competencies.  The advantages include heightened educational achievement, better job prospects, and increased community participation. Indigenous youth will develop confidence, acquire skills, and gain cultural pride, which will contribute to their communities' overall resilience and development. This project has a far-reaching impact on individuals and fosters broader societal objectives by encouraging equity, diversity, and inclusion. It meets immediate needs while establishing sustainable opportunities for the upcoming generation of Indigenous leaders.

Project Title: OKRA&KALE
Executive Summary: The global food system faces multidimensional challenges environmental degradation, dietary imbalances, unsustainable resource use, vulnerability to climate change, and lack of transparency. No single solution area can fully address these issues in isolation. Instead, integrating Protein Diversification, Sustainable Agriculture, Targeted Nutrition, and Circular Food Systems can create a more holistic and adaptive framework. By aligning interventions across these four areas, the food system can transition towards improved health outcomes, environmental stewardship, economic viability, and social equity.
Innovation Description: These interconnected issues threaten food security and public health while exacerbating environmental harm. Addressing these problems demands a holistic and adaptive approach that promotes health, sustainability, and equity across the food ecosystem.  OKRA&KALE tackles these challenges by producing premium, sustainably cultivated spirulina in a certified organic farm. Spirulina is a nutrient-dense, eco-friendly superfood containing 70% protein by weight, along with iron, vitamins, and antioxidants. Spirulina is grown in an environmentally friendly manner, offering a scalable solution for nutritious and sustainable food sources.  The innovation extends beyond production through a Machine Learning platform that unites consumers to the full lifecycle of spirulina. This platform ensures supply chain transparency via QR code tracking, provides tailored recipes to promote dietary health, and integrates tools to minimize food waste, optimize nutrition, and assess environmental impact.  Scientific insights into spirulina s exceptional nutrient density and its low environmental footprint compared to traditional protein sources form the foundation of this solution. Immediate benefits include healthier diets for consumers, reduced food waste, and carbon footprint awareness. Long-term impacts include improved health outcomes, we have a catalogue of spirulina infused products which we hope to ship in the upcoming future i.e Spirulina Honey.

Project Title: One Smart Kitchen (OSK) Hub: User Field Trials for An AI-Enhanced Camera System to Reduce Food Waste in Home Kitchens
Executive Summary: The proposed field trial provides a fundamental step towards validating that the OSK AI technology encourages conscious consumer choices to reduce food waste. Users will be given prototype camera systems that track food items, suggest meals, and issue spoilage alerts to optimize food utilization. The trial data will help us train our AI and understand user behaviors to minimize waste. The knowledge gained will enable OSK to scale and maximize the overall food system impact.
Innovation Description: Solving the global food waste challenge requires changes at the individual level, yet consumers are often disconnected from the global impact of their daily choices. Globally, the UN estimates that approximately one-third of all food produced for human consumption is lost or wasted, contributing to nearly 8% of global greenhouse gas emissions. The average American consumer wastes about 260 pounds of food annually or approximately $1800 per household. According to EPA estimates, food waste is the largest category of items in disposal facilities in the USA. About two-thirds of household food waste occurs due to improper storage, lack of visibility in refrigerators, unused ingredients, and misjudged food needs.  OSK translates the global food waste problem into a meaningful format to promote change at the individual level by enabling conscious consumer choices. The OSK hub is an AI-enabled camera system that can be placed on top of a refrigerator to track perishable items. Using AI, we segment the images from the camera to identify the items as they are placed into the fridge or pantry and track when they will spoil. Busy individuals and families receive timely alerts and suggested recipes when food needs to be used. This empowers consumers to make conscious choices to reduce food waste and build sustainable habits.  Our affordable smart device prioritizes consumer choice, prevents vendor-lock to an appliance manufacturer, and supports habit changes over time. The OSK hub leverages recent advances in low-cost computing, camera sensors, and AI to enable conscious consumer choices.

Project Title: Commercializing indigenous Bambara Groundnuts as an alternative protein source to empower farmers and promote nutrition security in Kenya
Executive Summary: OnlyPlants is an alternative protein startup harnessing indigenous African crops to drive protein intake and empower smallholder farmers (SHFs). We have developed a novel enzymatic formulation for plant-based milk from Bambara groundnuts, a protein-dense legume traditionally cultivated by women SHFs. A key barrier to commercialization is the lack of high-quality seeds. OnlyPlants is partnering with KALRO and Egerton University to identify high-yielding varieties, train farmers on cultivation best practices, and establish an outgrower program.
Innovation Description: Problem: OnlyPlants addresses a critical food security challenge in Kenya- the growing need for accessible and nutritious protein sources amidst a changing climate and growing population. Kenyan agriculture, heavily reliant on rain-fed systems, faces increasing vulnerability due to unpredictable rainfall patterns, impacting crop yields and farmer livelihoods. Simultaneously, increasing awareness of health concerns and high lactose intolerance rates (approx. 85% across Sub-Saharan Africa) are driving demand for alternative proteins. OnlyPlants tackles this challenge by innovating new products that drive market demand for Bambara groundnuts (BGN), a drought-resistant, indigenous crop with high nutritional value.  Solution: OnlyPlants tackles the underutilization of BGN by promoting their commercialization. We have developed proprietary enzyme-based process for BGN milk, ensuring cost-efficiency, high nutritional value, and optimal flavor. It brings out the milk s natural sweetness without added sugar and delivers strong functional attributes incl. heat stability and foaming capacity. Compared to oats, almonds and soy, BGN milk offers key advantages. BGN are grown locally, improve soil fertility through nitrogen fixation, and are drought-resistant. This creates an opportunity locally, where the product will be more affordable than imported alternatives, and for export markets, due to its strong nutrition and sustainability benefits.       Benefits: Formalizing the BGN supply chain will empower women SHFs by providing access to higher-yielding seeds, technical support, and guaranteed market access. Furthermore, BGN are drought-resistant and fix nitrogen in the soil, allowing for lower input costs and improving yields of other crops grown in rotation. Finally, consumers benefit from n accessible, affordable, and nutritious protein source.
