Project Title: Scaling Climate-Smart Farming Solutions: Bundling Pay-Per-Use Irrigation with Sustainable Advisory Services for Smallholders
Executive Summary: Oorja is a Farming-as-a-Service (FaaS) company offering affordable, sustainable irrigation,  with no upfront cost using a Pay-Per-Use (PPU) model, and climate-smart advisory to smallholders. Oorja proposes to scale its climate-smart advisory by bundling services into a comprehensive package, including soil testing, seed supply, on-farm training on sustainable practices, and a mobile app, enabling farmers to access training schedules, agronomy advice, weather updates, and personalized recommendations.
Innovation Description: Oorja s innovation is a farm-based service package powered by decentralized solar energy, using a unique Pay-Per-Use (PPU) model. It addresses smallholder farmers' challenges of high irrigation costs, inadequate access to reliable energy, and unsustainable farming practices. In India, 30 million farmers rely on costly diesel pumps, consuming 12% of the country s diesel. The poorest farmers often rent pumps, paying 20-60% more than diesel costs, leading to under-irrigation, reduced yields, and limited cropping seasons. Unsustainable farming practices further degrade soil health and perpetuate poverty, with climate change exacerbating these issues. Oorja installs, owns, and operates solar pumps on farms, offering irrigation at 3-4 INR/m  (4-5 US /m ), 20-60% cheaper than diesel. Farmers pay only for the water they use, measured by flowmeters. This model reduces costs, enables year-round cropping, and increases yields. Oorja complements irrigation with climate-smart advisory services, including soil testing, seed supply, and on-farm training in sustainable practices like natural input preparation and climate-resilient cropping. By bundling these services, including a mobile app for agronomy advice, weather updates, and training schedules, Oorja empowers farmers to adopt profitable, resource-efficient practices. This holistic approach improves productivity, enhances income stability, and reduces environmental impact, offering immediate and sustainable benefits to farmers, communities, and the environment.

Project Title: Public Procurement Toolkit for Health, Sustainable, and Economically Inclusive School Meal Programs
Executive Summary: This project will apply open contracting principles to create a practical toolkit for governments to enhance the inclusiveness and sustainability of school meal programs. It will provide guidance and procurement strategies for using data to engage small and local vendors. The toolkit will include actionable recommendations to improve access to affordable, healthy, locally produced food and offer practical tools, such as guidance on creating a catalog of healthy foods and implementing inclusive procurement policies.
Innovation Description: This project addresses exclusionary and unsustainable procurement practices in school meal programs, which waste resources, serve unhealthy food, and exclude small-scale farmers and minority producers. According to a survey conducted by the Global Child Nutrition Foundation, globally, 408.2 million children received school meals in 2022, yet only 13% of school-aged children in low-income countries benefit, compared to 48% in high-income countries. Per-child budgets in low- and middle-income countries dropped from $35.70 in 2017 to $28.04 in 2022, while only 10% of programs link small-scale farmers to school feeding.   We will develop a bilingual toolkit (English/Spanish) leveraging open contracting principles to improve inclusiveness and sustainability in school meal procurement building on lessons from Colombia and Mexico. Bogot  expanded vendors from 14 to 55, saved 10-15% in costs, and served 800,000 meals daily by exposing price-fixing. Palmira boosted vendor diversity by simplifying procurement processes for local and women-led businesses. Mexico City s Mi Tiendita Virtual streamlined vendor registration for SMEs, Indigenous groups, and rural producers.  The toolkit will include: 1. Vendor Empowerment Tools: Templates for simplified procurement processes and guidance for showcasing locally produced and sustainable foods.  2. Data Frameworks: Strategies for identifying and engaging women-led businesses, rural producers, and Indigenous groups through procurement data.  3. Policy Roadmap: Step-by-step guidance for governments to implement inclusive and sustainable policies.   Outcomes include healthier meals for children, stable markets for smallholder farmers, empowered marginalized producers, and more sustainable food systems. These changes will strengthen local economies, improve nutrition, and reduce environmental impact.   Pitch video: https://youtu.be/52I4hja0YT4

Project Title: "Transforming Community Behaviors and Health Systems for Sustainable Nutrition in Bussi Islands, Wakiso District"
Executive Summary: This project seeks to address high rates of malnutrition in Bussi Islands, Wakiso District, by strengthening community health systems alongside behavioral change. Interventions like targeted nutrition education, improved health services, and community-based interventions will reduce stunting, wasting, and underweight conditions among children and improve maternal and child nutrition. Through harnessing local knowledge and integrating evidence-based practices, we will be improving nutrition at community levels toward contributing to the national goal of reducing malnutrition by 2030.
Innovation Description: Malnutrition remains a critical public health issue globally and in Uganda, contributing to high rates of child mortality and impaired development, especially among children under five and pregnant or breastfeeding women. Despite some progress, approximately 25.4% of children in Uganda are stunted, while 3.6% suffer from wasting, and 32.8% of women are affected by anemia. These figures reflect a broader crisis, as the country grapples with a triple burden of malnutrition undernutrition, overnutrition, and micronutrient deficiencies. In Bussi Islands, Wakiso District, the situation is dire, with 16.1% of children underweight and 7.8% experiencing wasting. Contributing factors include food insecurity, large household sizes, poor sanitation, and weak nutrition practices. Furthermore, insufficient community-based interventions, limited health-seeking behaviors and impacts of extreme weather event due to climate change exacerbate the problem. The solution proposed in this project uses several innovative approaches, including: Digital tools like an interactive USSD platform to share nutrition tips with farmers and local community to increase knowledge on food and good diet.  Capacity building through training Village Health Teams (VHTs) on using digital tools like the GIS mapping and for malnutrition detection and timely referral. Sustainable Practices like demonstration gardens with biofortified crops, regenerative agriculture techniques coupled with food preservation training to reduce waste. These initiatives will have Immediate benefits to the community as they will gain knowledge of nutrition, better detection and treatment of malnutrition, and improved food security. In the long term, outcomes will include sustainable health systems, climate-resilient agriculture, reduced child mortality, and empowered communities.

Project Title: Cultivating Resilience: Promotion of Cover Crops for Sustainable Agriculture in West Africa
Executive Summary: Cover crops offer a scalable solution to the chronic problem of land degradation in West Africa. By covering and protecting the soil, they minimize erosion from rainfall and wind, and they can be quickly planted across many acres of fields. Cover crops add nitrogen and organic material to fields without the need for transport or agricultural chemicals. This project builds upon the 2023 seed grant to further expand cover crop seed production and implementation.
Innovation Description: Throughout West Africa, subsistence farmers face a soil degradation crisis. Previously fertile fields are now so  tired  that they can no longer produce sufficient harvests, even with significant applications of expensive chemical fertilizer. Before, farmers would often allow fields to fallow for several years between periods of cultivation. Now, due to population pressure, most agricultural lands are farmed or grazed every year. Eventually, these fields become exhausted and are abandoned, forcing people to migrate to more productive areas or move into crowded cities.  Across the Sahel countries of Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso, the long term impacts of soil degradation are evident. Ten of thousands of farmers have been displaced and the resulting instability and poverty makes it easier for violent militant groups to capture territory and conduct attacks on vulnerable rural populations. Finding few options for gainful employment in rural areas, many young people move into cities that are already struggling with overcrowding and high rates of unemployment.  Cover crops allow farmers to continue to cultivate their fields, while simultaneously repairing and improving the soil. They grow quickly, and throughout the growing season add significant amounts of nitrogen and organic material to soil. Over several seasons, they can rehabilitate previously exhausted fields. Planting cover crops offers an ecological alternative to the overuse of agrochemicals. With time, they can help revitalize rural communities as farmers are able to produce healthy food with fewer costly inputs. This promotes stability and can provide an alternative to migration or relocation to urban areas.

Project Title: Budigot, From waste to Sustainable food Security
Executive Summary: Budigot. From Waste to Sustainable Food Security. This project is a revolutionary solution in organic and food waste management using BSF maggots. This project not only reduces greenhouse gas emissions, but also produces high-quality protein-rich animal feed and organic fertilizer. With an efficient and sustainable circular economy approach, Budigot supports global food security, strengthens environmental sustainability, and drives greener and more resilient local economies.
Innovation Description: Budigot is an innovative solution that processes organic waste, especially food waste, using BSF (Black Soldier Fly) larvae to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. By 2023, FAO recorded that around 1.3 Billion tons of food is wasted every year worldwide, resulting in a loss of USD $990 Billion, contributing to pollution and resource waste. The project addresses this problem by converting food waste into high-protein animal feed and high-quality organic fertilizer that can be used by farmers.  The global demand for animal feed and organic fertilizer continues to increase, but many countries are unable to meet the demand. The soaring prices of chemical fertilizers and non-organic animal feed make it difficult for farmers and producers. In addition, the use of chemical fertilizers has a negative impact on soil and ecosystem health, while non-organic feed risks reducing the quality of livestock and human health.  Budigot offers a relevant and sustainable solution by utilizing BSF larvae to process food waste into high-value and environmentally friendly products. The circular economy approach implemented ensures efficient waste management and produces affordable, high-quality animal feed and organic fertilizer. In this way, Budigot not only helps reduce waste and greenhouse gas emissions, but also supports global food security and environmental sustainability for communities and future generations.

Project Title: Harnessing the Potential of Seaweed As Versatile Packaging Material to Stop Nanoplastic Contamination in Human Body
Executive Summary: We convert seaweed into versatile bio-packaging options, such as edible sachets, cups, and cookie envelopes. Our goals are to address the environmental crisis and mitigate plastic waste pollution by providing sustainable alternatives that safeguard consumers from nanoplastic contamination and ensure convenience. By establishing a new market sector for seaweed and utilizing surplus seaweed, we are also improving the livelihoods of disadvantaged populations in coastal areas, particularly seaweed producers.
Innovation Description: Nanoplastic contamination is a growing global concern, with food packaging being one of its largest contributors, alongside plastic utensils, toothbrushes, and clothing. When tea bags, coffee cups, and instant meal containers come into direct contact with hot water, they unintentionally expose consumers to nanoplastics, which they then consume along with their food or drink. Indonesia is the world's largest consumer of microplastics and the fifth-largest plastic waste contributor. We offer four uncompetitive advantages. First, Indonesia ranks as the second-largest seaweed producer globally, with over 80% of its oceanic potential still untapped. Unlike bioplastics from terrestrial crops, Biopac does not contribute to food scarcity or deforestation. Second, we have been pioneers in seaweed-based packaging development since 2010 and established our innovative edge with four patents on flexible packaging and one on seaweed-based tableware. Comprehensive certifications, including compostable, food packaging, and conformity certificates, back our products, ensuring their safety for human consumption and the environment. Third, Biopac eliminates the risk of nanoplastic contamination in food and beverages, ensuring safer daily consumption. Environmentally, Biopac significantly reduces plastic waste pollution while offering fully biodegradable solutions that align with SDGs. For local communities, seaweed cultivation creates jobs and drives sustainable economic growth, especially in coastal areas with untapped marine resources. Fourth, our product price is affordable compared to the total cost of conventional plastic, as reported by WWF. By combining sustainable innovation and eco-conscious practices, we aim to redefine packaging while addressing critical global challenges like microplastic contamination and environmental degradation.

Project Title: Empowering Dryland communities through Climate-Resilient Cacti-Farming: Regenerative Farming for food security, Nutrition and Sustainable Livelihoods.
Executive Summary: Dunia Bora leverages the drought-resilient cactus to produce nutrient-dense foods and converts waste generated into organic fertilizer. We convert the prickly-pear opuntia cactus fruit into nutritious juice and jam. The ingredients used in fortification are locally sourced and reduce food waste whereas the waste generated is treated into a Vermi-culture which produces a liquid fertilizer. Through this innovative value addition, we address food system challenges through nature-based solutions while restoring degraded soils and conserving water.
Innovation Description: Dunia Bora is addressing the problem of food insecurity and environmental degradation in arid regions by transforming the invasive prickly pear cactus into nutritious juice and jam. This innovation is particularly relevant as many communities face challenges related to drought, malnutrition, and the spread of invasive species that threaten local ecosystems. The prickly pear cactus, which thrives in dry conditions, offers a sustainable solution to these issues. By utilizing this resilient plant, Dunia Bora not only provides a source of nutrition but also helps mitigate the negative impacts of the cactus on local grazing lands. The process involves harvesting the fruit to create juice and jams, which are rich in vitamins and can be marketed both locally and internationally. This approach is rooted in scientific insights about the cactus's nutritional benefits and its capacity to grow in poor soils with minimal water. By focusing on value addition rather than eradication, Dunia Bora promotes a circular economy that benefits local farmers and consumers alike. Immediate benefits include improved nutrition for communities, new economic opportunities for farmers through crop diversification, and reduced reliance on water-intensive crops. Sustainable benefits encompass enhanced food security, environmental restoration by controlling invasive species, and increased resilience against climate change impacts. Overall, Dunia Bora's innovation fosters a more sustainable food system while empowering local communities.

Project Title: Circular Economy for Sustainable Food Security Using Ezee DIY Aquaponic System (EDAS)
Executive Summary: The project addresses climate change challenges, such as flooding, by enabling communities in Kedah and Perlis to produce food sustainably in small spaces. EDAS uses a controlled, regenerative aquaponics system that minimizes water use, eliminates chemical fertilizers, and upcycles waste, contributing to planetary health. Through community-wide adoption, the project ensures that local agricultural produce meets or exceeds industrial crop yields, enhancing food security and resilience to climate impacts.
Innovation Description: Food insecurity, environmental degradation, and climate change impacts such as flooding are major issues for underserved communities in Kedah and Perlis, Malaysia. Approximately 25% of global food production is lost or wasted annually, worsening food insecurity (FAO, 2019). Climate change is further straining agriculture, with increased flooding and unpredictable weather patterns threatening crop yields. The Ezee DIY Aquaponic System (EDAS) offers a sustainable solution. Aquaponics, which integrates aquaculture and hydroponics, uses up to 90% less water than traditional farming (FAO, 2020), making it ideal for water-scarce and flood-prone areas. The system recycles water and nutrients in a closed-loop, optimizing space and resources. Research shows that aquaponic systems can yield up to 10 times more food per square meter than conventional agriculture (University of Arizona, 2020), enabling high-density food production in small spaces like homes or schools. EDAS also reduces the need for synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, helping protect the environment by lowering chemical runoff and greenhouse gas emissions. Studies show that aquaponics generates fewer greenhouse gases compared to traditional farming (UC Davis, 2018), contributing to environmental sustainability. For communities in Kedah and Perlis, EDAS offers immediate benefits such as increased local food production, improved climate resilience, and reduced environmental impact. It empowers communities to produce their own nutritious food, strengthening food security while promoting sustainable, regenerative farming practices and contributing to planetary health.

Project Title: Sustainable Seafood, Resilient Coasts: Harnessing Marine Aquaculture to Empower Mangrove Restoration and Novel Crops
Executive Summary: Pine Island Redfish technology is a blueprint for the future of resilient coastal communities, where ecosystems thrive, people enjoy nutritious, traceable seafood, and communities are strengthened for the future. Our land-based, regenerative aquaculture farm technology is replicable in seaside communities worldwide. We utilize recirculating aquaculture systems to grow redfish, a native fish harvested to the brink of extinction. Our fish nourish more than our community; the waste products are fertilizer, growing mangroves for coastal restoration.
Innovation Description: 40% of the world s population lives within 100km of the coast and are facing multiple threats: unpredictable weather, sea level rise, fewer economic opportunities supported by commercial fishing, ecosystem declines and deteriorating ocean water quality. In the South coast of the US, evidence of these threats is everywhere, from high water temperatures fueling the strongest and costliest storm seasons ever recorded to increased algal blooms fueled by agriculture runoff. Yet, people s will to stay, continuing their coastal livelihoods is stronger than ever. Worldwide, coastal migration is increasing at twice that of inland areas. The future is not abandonment of the coast but creating environmental and economic resilience in the face of these challenges - creating diversified economic opportunities that work in harmony with restoration and strengthening of the coastal ecosystems. Pine Island Redfish s regenerative aquaculture solution is based on Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS) technology; producing sustainable, traceable, and locally grown marine protein while cultivating nutrient-dense and carbon sequestering plants. Circularity of our technology is unique; it addresses a major challenge for aquaculture   saltwater waste mitigation, which is currently capex intensive and operationally complex. Our technology captures nutrient dense waste to be repurposed for carbon-sequestering mangroves and nutrient-dense halophytic vegetables. We are on-course to restore thousands of mangroves equaling hectares of habitat and additional carbon sequestration capacity. The end result reaches beyond this; application of our regenerative practices will become the requisite approach to seafood production, with regionally relevant fish providing healthy protein and fueling restoration of coastal ecosystems.

Project Title: Miniaturized spectrometer powered with artificial intelligence for food quality analysis
Executive Summary: Today, there is no affordable and reliable system for onsite and on demand quality analysis food produce. In India, the agriculture production mainly takes places in the rural areas and test laboratories are located in remote cities. Thus, farmers or consumers have limited accessibility to the testing services, they find it very expensive, and due to the delay in getting test results decision making takes time. As a result, being unaware of the quality of the commodity, farmers and consumers either suffer from unfair pricing practices or fall prey to the ever-expanding adulteration market. As a solution to these problems, we propose to build a miniaturized handheld device for testing food produce, that is affordable and gives instant results at press-of-a-button. This device will enable unlimited onsite testing without use of chemicals.

Project Title: Full Circle Hubs for Cassava Processing and Farming
Executive Summary: We want to operationalize of a utility that creates a safe, profitable, and future-proof cassava value chain for smallholder farmers. By integrating renewable energy, advanced agronomy, carbon removal, and digital chain-of-custody innovations, it reduces food loss by 60%, eliminates carcinogenic molds, and doubles selling prices for farmers and processors. It also revitalizes soil health through biochar and unlocks climate financing opportunities.
Innovation Description: Cassava farmers in Africa face significant challenges, including limited access to drying infrastructure, difficulty meeting market standards, severe pest and disease pressures, lack of clean seed and improved varieties, inefficient fertilizer use, and increasingly frequent droughts. These interconnected issues contribute to an estimated annual revenue loss of $3 billion across Sub-Saharan Africa, leaving farmers among the world s poorest and most climate-vulnerable populations.   Due to the low market price and slim profit margins for cassava, farmers have little means and motivation to invest in proper agronomic practices. Many therefore opt for other crops like maize that are more marketable, which is however also more dependent on synthetic fertiliser and less climate resilient, thus leading to food insecurity. Low-cost greenhouses and hybrid systems with nighttime heating via furnaces have been introduced, but they fail to achieve the drying speed and quality needed to preserve cassava roots effectively.  Our solution centers on a clean, decarbonized pyrolysis system that transforms cassava stems and excess biomass into energy for rapid drying. This innovation reduces processing costs, sterilizes diseases, and produces biochar a valuable soil amendment. Biochar supports disease-free plantlet propagation and generates additional income through carbon credit sales.  By addressing key bottlenecks and promoting sustainable practices, our approach boosts farmer incomes, enhances resilience, and creates a cost-effective, climate-smart cassava value chain. This integrated model delivers immediate benefits while fostering long-term agricultural and economic sustainability for cassava-growing communities."

Project Title: Feeding Our Neighbors
Executive Summary: Plenty! Farm and Foodbank nourishes the community, valuing freshness in food with the goal of providing access to healthy food for all. Located in and serving Floyd Co., VA, Plenty! distributes over 6,000 pounds of food a week via our drive through pantry and year-round home delivery and mobile pantry program. It is imperative that Plenty! find and receive funding to continue its life changing mission and goal of "Feeding Our Neighbors".
Innovation Description: During 2023 Plenty! served a record number of Floyd County residents. 2024 have continued to set new records. Plenty! conducted its biannual patron survey in the Fall of 2022 and found that in the past 12 months Floyd County residents were more food insecure than in 2020. Patrons reported the following, 47% reported being Moderately Food Insecure (i.e., skipping meals), more than double the rate in 2020, and 29% reported Severe Food Insecurity (i.e., going a day without eating), nearly double the rate in 2020. Patrons also reported that since coming to Plenty! their experience of food insecurity decreased and they were able to eat a greater variety of foods, (61%), eat more fresh foods and (62%) and do more "From Scratch" cooking.   To address these needs Plenty! has pantry hours available three days a week, Monday's 1-4PM, Tuesdays 10AM-1PM and Thursday's 4-6PM. Pantry is set up similar to a drive thru where patrons can select items via menus that are distributed while individuals wait in line. When the patrons reach the pantry, they have the opportunity to step out of the vehicle and shop our outdoor farmers market area and large produce fridge to select fruits and veggies as well as breads and baked goods. Plenty! also offers year-round home deliveries and mobile pantry to families that do not have adequate transportation to come to the pantry.

Project Title: Transforming Food Security and Equity for Underserved Communities
Executive Summary: This initiative combats food insecurity and systemic inequities by delivering immediate hunger relief, rescuing surplus food, and empowering underserved communities with nutrition education and economic opportunities. Through sustainable practices, local partnerships, and innovative solutions, the program ensures equitable access to nutritious food, fosters community resilience, and addresses long-term disparities. The vision is to create a regenerative, inclusive food system that improves health outcomes, reduces waste, and positively impacts vulnerable populations across Canada and the U.S.
Innovation Description: The Princen Sammy Foundation Canada  Food Security and Hunger Relief Program directly addresses the urgent problem of food insecurity and systemic inequities in access to nutritious food. Millions of families, particularly from underserved groups such as Black, Indigenous, and other marginalized communities, face barriers to consistent, affordable, and healthy food, compounded by economic challenges, inefficient food distribution systems, and lack of nutrition education. These challenges lead to adverse health, social, and economic outcomes, perpetuating cycles of poverty and inequality.Our solution combines innovative, community-based approaches with sustainable practices to create immediate and long-term impact. The program integrates food rescue initiatives to reduce waste and redistribute surplus food, ensuring equitable access to nutritious meals. By partnering with local organizations, we strengthen food systems, empower communities with financial literacy, and provide economic opportunities through social enterprises.A key innovation is our culturally tailored nutritional education program, which equips underserved groups with tools to make informed, affordable, and healthy food choices, improving long-term health outcomes. Additionally, we champion regenerative agricultural practices to enhance soil health, reduce environmental footprints, and upcycle food byproducts into nutrient-rich ingredients.This solution benefits end users by ensuring access to safe, nutritious, and affordable food, fostering resilient communities, and promoting sustainable food systems. Farmers and producers gain from improved resource efficiency and reduced waste, while consumers enjoy healthier diets and empowered decision-making. By combining technological insights, community engagement, and environmental stewardship, our program addresses systemic disparities and builds pathways toward an equitable and sustainable global food system.

Project Title: Establishing a Pawpaw Research & Breeding Orchard Network in the USA
Executive Summary: Project Pawpaw will establish its second research orchard at a site in Wisconsin as part of a nationwide network of pawpaw orchards. Each planting will feature rootstocks from a shared seed lot, and will be grafted with all available named cultivars and progeny from elite crosses. These orchards will generate performance data, develop breeding tools, support market development with fruit production, and provide a disease-free scion source for nurseries, advancing pawpaw cultivation and industry growth.
Innovation Description: Project Pawpaw addresses the challenges of underutilized perennial tree crops by creating a USA-based network of research orchards to advance breeding and market development for the North American pawpaw (Asimina triloba). Despite their potential as a high-value, climate-resilient crop, pawpaw cultivation faces barriers such as limited improved cultivars, a lack of performance data, slow breeding cycles, and short fruit shelf life.  This application seeks funding to establish a second orchard in Wisconsin, featuring replicated plantings of named cultivars and progeny from elite crosses. This orchard will conserve rare varieties, generate performance data, and provide disease-free scion wood for nurseries. It will also supply fruit for market development and strengthen local food systems by reducing reliance on globalized supply chains.  Over time, this orchard network will enable the use of advanced genomic tools like Genomic Selection (GS) and Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS), now accessible due to falling genotyping and computing costs. These tools allow us to screen large populations at the seedling stage and make more informed breeding decisions. This approach will accelerate the development of superior cultivars tailored to diverse environments.  Pawpaws are not only gaining popularity in the U.S. but are also fueling emerging industries in rural Croatia, Slovenia, France, Italy, and Canada, showcasing their adaptability and market potential. Immediate and lasting benefits include empowering farmers with high-performing cultivars, increasing rural economic opportunities, conserving biodiversity, and promoting regenerative systems that enhance soil health. This orchard will position pawpaws as a climate-smart, equitable, and globally relevant crop.

Project Title: Isolation & purification of functional leaf protein "RuBisCO" isolates from agricultural waste leaves
Executive Summary: The project seeks to improve our patent pending lab-scale methods for RuBisCO extraction and purification, aiming to achieve higher yield and purity at pilot scale, thereby clearing the path for commercial scale. Key objectives include optimizing technology for large-scale production including commercial viability and enhancing the nutritional value and environmental sustainability of our RuBisCO isolates. The  isolates fill a critical market gap and position Proleri as a leader in innovative, sustainable, plant protein solutions.
Innovation Description: Current Plant proteins like Soy, Pea and Wheat have allergens, are incomplete proteins and have significant off notes making it difficult for plant product companies to compete with animal products. For decades, this has led to extensive growth in animal agriculture causing significant environmental damage. Leaf Protein "RuBisCO", often referred to as "Holy Grail of Plant Protein", is allergen free, has all essential amino acids, perfect digestibility and great functional properties. It is a true replacement of animal proteins. And the best part is that it is present in all leaves making it the most abundant protein in the world.   At Proleri, we have developed proprietary technology to isolate RuBisCO protein isolates from waste leaves. It represents a significant breakthrough in protein extraction technology. Unlike traditional methods that yield green or brown isolates, this process produces high-purity, white/off white protein isolates ideal for health drinks, protein bars, and other food applications requiring a neutral colour and taste.  Our current technology focuses on two methods for extracting RuBisCO protein from plant leaves. The first method uses a combination of coagulation & precipitation to isolate the protein. The second uses homogenization, sieving, centrifugation, depigmentation and dialysis to obtain depigmented and purified RuBisCO protein. Both methods are efficient, scalable, and free of harmful by-products, utilizing agricultural waste from crops like broccoli, cauliflower, sweet potato etc..   The resulting white/off-white RuBisCO isolate functions as a versatile ingredient in plant-based foods, serving as a protein booster or substitute for chemical binding agents or thickeners

Project Title: Geospatial Mapping of Soil Microorganisms: Tracking Soil Microbial Biomass In Pursuit of Sustainable Soil and Food production
Executive Summary: The relationship between plant-microbe nutrient exchange is unknown by most food producers, hindering soil regeneration efforts. Microbiomes' invisibility prohibits transitioning to organic practices while retaining profitable yields. MicroBIOMETER's affordable technology enables crop-specific guidance, and predictive modeling for improved agricultural choices. Implementation includes standardizing sampling, upgrading mobile apps, while fostering collaborations. We will deliver a spatially explicit microbial biomass analysis to soil stewards, aiding food producers in vulnerable regions facing economic and climate-related food shortages.
Innovation Description: The MicroBIOMETER test kit revolutionizes soil health assessment, offering an accessible method to measure an elusive but key indicator of soil health: microbial biomass carbon(1-2). The brainchild of Dr. Judy Fitzpatrick, this innovative tool has evolved over a decade, enhancing its global reach and precision. The kit addresses soil microbiome health invisibility, which often leads to harmful practices like the overuse of pesticides and chemical fertilizers(3). It allows soil stewards to test the effects of their regenerative practices over time(4-5). This project will introduce groundbreaking integrative, statistical, and spatially explicit results with predicting capabilities to aid food producers and soil stewards. Our global soil microbiome database (>10K entries from over 7,000 customers) and biogeographical and statistical analyses will help food producers link soil health to yield projections on their land. Adding spatial mapping to the soil microbiome will allow us to identify patterns at local-to-landscape scales, which will deliver data-driven decision-making for targeted soil management strategies(6). Our affordable tests allow growers to conduct testing over wide-geographic ranges and across different periods, providing rich datasets for analysis. Improving soil health aligns with the 'One-Health Concept '(7-8), a holistic approach that recognizes the interconnectedness of human, animal, and environmental health. This concept posits that better soils lead to better human health and environmental well-being, as healthy soils support carbon accumulation in soils(9) on top of supporting the growth of nutrient-rich crops and reducing the need for chemicals. This project represents a significant leap forward in precision, sustainable agriculture of nutrient-rich food production

Immediate benefits include increased food production, job creation, and reduced reliance on imports. Sustainable benefits extend to environmental restoration, community empowerment, and cultural preservation. By providing training and economic opportunities for farmers and youth, the project addresses food insecurity while fostering long-term resilience. Protectores de la Tierra offers a scalable model for restoring food sovereignty and creating equitable, sustainable food systems in marginalized communities worldwide.

Project Title: Sustainable Feed Solutions and Regenerative Farming
Executive Summary: Our project focuses on creating sustainable feed solutions and integrating regenerative farming practices to improve food production efficiency. By utilizing innovative upcycling methods for agricultural byproducts and implementing eco-friendly technologies, we aim to reduce waste, enhance soil health, and increase yields. This approach empowers farmers, supports resilient food systems, and provides nutritious, affordable food to communities while protecting the environment.
Innovation Description: Our innovation introduces sustainable feed solutions and regenerative farming practices to address food insecurity and agricultural inefficiency. These issues are particularly relevant in regions where access to affordable, nutritious food is limited, and environmental degradation threatens long-term agricultural viability.    We solve these problems by upcycling agricultural byproducts, such as crop residues and animal waste, into high-quality, nutrient-rich animal feed. This reduces dependency on expensive commercial feed while minimizing agricultural waste. Additionally, we implement regenerative practices like organic fertilization, intercropping, and precision irrigation, which enhance soil health, conserve water, and improve yields.    This innovation is rooted in insights from circular agriculture, demonstrating that sustainable resource use not only benefits the environment but also lowers costs and boosts productivity for farmers. Life Cycle Assessments reveal that upcycling reduces greenhouse gas emissions by 25% and agricultural waste by 40%, making it both practical and impactful  Immediate benefits include lower costs for farmers, increased productivity, and improved food availability. Over time, regenerative practices restore soil fertility, reduce the environmental footprint of farming, and ensure a more resilient food system. These benefits extend to consumers through more affordable and nutritious food, to communities by creating local economic opportunities, and to the environment by promoting sustainability. This comprehensive approach ensures both immediate and long-term impacts on food security and environmental health.

Immediate benefits include increased food production and enhanced incomes for beneficiaries. In the long term, this approach builds resilience to climate impacts, improves resource efficiency, and contributes to regional food security. Project Title: Empowering Mothers: Optimizing Breastmilk Storage  for Improved Infant Outcomes and Planetary Health
Executive Summary: PumpKin is developing an affordable, sustainable solution using upcycled ingredients to preserve breastmilk and reduce waste. This project will analyze our formulation's impact on breastmilk's composition during household storage. By extending shelf-life and ensuring optimal nutrition, we democratize access to this vital resource, empower mothers globally, minimize spoilage, and promote a healthier planet. Our innovation supports maternal and infant health while addressing climate challenges associated with breastmilk waste and the environmental footprint of formula production.
Innovation Description: The World Health Organization recommends infants be exclusively breastfed for the first 6 months of life. Fewer than half of all infants meet this guideline, and 60% of parents fail to accomplish their breastfeeding goals. Many mothers are full-time employed at the time of childbirth and rely on freezer storage to enable continued breastfeeding. However, stored breastmilk loses nutritional value and can become rancid, leading infants to reject it. Challenges with feeding stored milk force parents to switch to formula, which is an imperfect breastmilk substitute and environmentally costly to manufacture. PumpKin's patented solution combines three safe, food-derived ingredients into an easy-to-use liquid concentrate that, when added to pumped breastmilk, extends frozen shelf-life. Our innovation preserves breastmilk nutritional value by reducing >60% of fat breakdown   a property associated with rancidity   for >6 months of storage. Our primary ingredient is sustainably sourced from citrus peels derived from existing waste streams. Unlike freeze-drying and pasteurization, which are expensive, energy-intensive, and often inadequate to preserve nutritional content, PumpKin's solution provides an affordable and sustainable at-home method for breastmilk preservation. Breastmilk is a scarce resource, yet 75% of US parents report discarding breastmilk. Assuming this waste represents 10% of their supply, over 1 billion ounces are discarded annually. PumpKin's innovation will reduce infant rejection of freezer-stored breastmilk, reduce breastmilk waste, and enable women to participate in the workforce. By lowering reliance on commercial formula, our solution conserves water and energy, reduces greenhouse gas emissions, and decreases packaging waste associated with formula production.

Project Title: Building up the food supply chain for nutrition: Biofortified bread in Nigeria
Executive Summary: This project contributes to reducing malnutrition by reducing barriers to the production of orange-fleshed sweetpotato bread, which would increase vitamin A consumption among Nigeria s poor.  This will support the food system and supply chain, from local farmers to bakeries and to consumers. Through training, supply chain optimization, and a rigorous impact evaluation, this initiative promotes sustainable agriculture, nutrition improvement, and economic growth, with the potential to benefit millions across Nigeria and sub-Saharan Africa.
Innovation Description: Malnutrition affects millions of people globally, with disproportionate impacts on developing countries (Bird et al., 2017; FAO et al., 2023; Harttgen & Seiler, 2023). In particular, nearly 48% of children under five in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) suffer from vitamin A deficiency, leading to increased risks of blindness, immune system deficiency, and mortality (Amare et al., 2023; Song et al., 2023).   Biofortified crops, enhanced with nutrients through cross-breeding rather than genetic modification, offer a cost-effective solution to micronutrient deficiencies (Avnee et al., 2023). In particular, biofortified orange-fleshed sweetpotato (OFSP) is rich in beta carotene, a precursor for vitamin A. About 125 grams of OFSP provides the daily vitamin A requirement for a young child. OFSP puree can be used as a partial substitute for wheat flour in bread, making bread a significant source of vitamin A. Since bread holds a central dietary role in many African countries, OFSP bread could substantially increase year-round nutrition (Wanjuu et al., 2019).   While OFSP bread has the potential to make a huge impact on nutrition in SSA, several challenges remain. First, most bakers are not aware of OFSP bread.  Second, conversations with Nigerian bakers who are interested in making OFSP bread suggest that it is difficult to procure raw OFSP root from farmers.  Our project plans to solve these problems by working with bakers in Nigeria to increase their awareness of OFSP and link them with farmers who can consistently supply OFSP for them to bake into nutritious and affordable bread.

Smallholder farmers gain immediate benefits, such as increased productivity and reduced costs, while enjoying long-term sustainability by scaling their operations.  Communities and society at large benefit from improved local fish production, adding 10,850 metric tons of high-quality exportable traceable fish over two years. This helps bridge the fish demand gap, enhances food security, and creates employment opportunities. Environmentally, the Smart Pond promotes resource efficiency, reducing waste and encouraging sustainable aquaculture practices.  This holistic approach fosters equitable access to innovation, empowering farmers to thrive while contributing to a sustainable food system.

Project Title: Empowering Tanzania s Cashew Farmers Through Sustainable Processing and Global Market Integration
Executive Summary: Our project transforms Tanzania s cashew industry by creating a decentralized, farmer-centric processing ecosystem. Currently supporting 2,000 smallholder farmers, the initiative increases farmer incomes by 40%, reduces post-harvest losses by 25%, and ensures access to global premium markets. By integrating sustainable practices, including zero-waste processing and regenerative agriculture, the project aligns with global food security goals. With a scalable model, we aim to empower 50,000 farmers, create thousands of jobs across Africa.
Innovation Description: Tanzania, the fourth-largest cashew producer in Africa, faces significant barriers in realizing the full value of its industry. Over 95% of cashews are exported raw, resulting in an estimated $200 million annual loss in potential revenue. This dependency on raw exports limits value addition, job creation, and economic empowerment, particularly in rural communities where cashew farming is a primary livelihood. Smallholder farmers face low incomes, supply chain inefficiencies, and market access challenges, while the environment suffers from unsustainable farming practices and waste mismanagement.  Our innovation addresses these challenges through a decentralized, farmer-centric processing ecosystem. By establishing six rural primary processing centers and a central processing facility, we integrate smallholder farmers into the value chain, ensuring immediate cash payments, reduced post-harvest losses, and improved quality control. Cutting-edge technology enables zero-waste processing, converting byproducts into Cashew Nut Shell Liquid (CNSL) and organic fertilizers, promoting environmental sustainability.  Scientific and technical insights drive our approach, leveraging regenerative agriculture and advanced processing techniques to optimize efficiency and quality. Immediate benefits include a 40% increase in farmer incomes, a 25% reduction in post-harvest losses, and the creation of 2,500 jobs, 95% of which are for women. Sustainable outcomes include enhanced food security, reduced environmental footprints, and economic empowerment for rural communities.  This scalable model aligns with global food security and sustainability goals, transforming Tanzania s cashew industry into a driver of inclusive growth and environmental stewardship.

Executive Summary: Indonesia has a high stunting rate, affecting 30.8% of children under 5. To address this, Rahsa Nusantara will partner with women in East Indonesia, to develop Moringa leaf supplements. Moringa is abundant and easy to access locally but remains underutilized despite its rich nutrients. This initiative equips women with skills and tools to process Moringa, empowering them to improve family nutrition, create economic opportunities, and develop community resilience while combating malnutrition.
Innovation Description: Rahsa Nusantara addresses Indonesia s pressing stunting problem, which affects 30.8% of children under five, by introducing a plant-based innovation using Moringa leaves. Despite being abundant in East Nusa Tenggara area, Moringa remains underutilized. Known for its high content of vitamins, minerals, and protein, Moringa offers an effective natural solution to combat stunting and improve maternal and child health.  The project partners with women and young women in Rote Ndao to develop Moringa-based supplements that boost maternal nutrition, particularly during pregnancy. Rahsa Nusantara provides training, tools, and equipment to empower these women to process Moringa leaves into versatile raw materials and supplements. This initiative not only addresses stunting but also creates economic opportunities, diversifies the local economy, and strengthens community resilience.  Scientific insights into Moringa s nutrient richness led to this solution, combined with the use of solar drying technology for efficient, eco-friendly processing. The immediate benefits include better health outcomes for pregnant women and their children, increased income for women and local farmers, and greater nutrition awareness. The sustainable impacts are equally significant, including reduced healthcare costs, a stronger local economy, and a more resilient food system.  By focusing on empowering women and leveraging local resources, Rahsa Nusantara s project addresses stunting, improves maternal health, and help to develop economic and environmental sustainability. This holistic approach ensures the innovation delivers measurable benefits to families, communities, and the broader society, creating a healthier and more equitable future.

Project Title: Regenerative agriculture for a planetary health: Community supported agriculture in Colombia
Executive Summary: Our project seeks to expand agroecology and regenerative agriculture in Colombia through the growth CSA Colombian Network with new communities of farmers and consumers, that join the exchange model that guarantees fair incomes, diversified organic foods, creates seed guardians of adapted crops to climate conditions and additionally we ll implement an educational strategy to highlight the benefits of the CSA model in society, biodiversity and the planet.
Innovation Description: Despite Colombia's extraordinary biodiversity and agricultural potential, food insecurity persists, affecting around 30% of the population. Violence, inequality, and the degradation of natural resources further deepen this crisis. In response, the CSA (Community-Supported Agriculture) Colombian Network emerged as a collective of farmers and urban families. Its purpose: to empower small-scale farmers by transitioning from conventional agriculture to sustainable, agroecological practices. The CSA model stands out as an innovative economic framework and a practical option for small farmers to commercialize their production while fostering direct connections with consumers. By bridging urban and rural communities, the network has redefined food sovereignty and created a pathway for farmers to earn 50% more than the national minimum wage, ensuring financial stability in vulnerable rural economies because they sell at a fair price their product and avoids food waste. This approach goes beyond economics. Today, 14 active CSAs serve over 400 families, promoting agroecological knowledge-sharing through workshops on biodiversity, soil regeneration, and sustainable practices tailored to local contexts. A cornerstone of the model is the conservation of native seed guardians of agrobiodiversity and key to achieving true food sovereignty, responding to climate change and the biodiversity crisis. Moreover, the network has catalyzed the empowerment of women and youth by providing training in project management, decision-making, and technology use. It emphasizes sustainability not only in farming practices but also in the relationships it nurtures between growers and consumers.

Project Title: Diamond Matrix Bioconversion: Revolutionizing Farming with Sustainable Crop Solutions
Executive Summary: Our project transforms organic materials, including sargassum seaweed and tithonia, into innovative sustainable crop inputs like biostimulants, fertilizers and composts. These solutions significantly enhance soil biodiversity, nutrient cycling, and health, while boosting crop yields and reducing reliance on synthetic chemicals. By leveraging natural resources, we provide chemical-free, cost-effective, eco-friendly inputs that support regenerative agriculture, improve food security, and address environmental challenges, revolutionizing farming practices for a sustainable and resilient food system.
Innovation Description: For over five decades, the agrochemical industry has relied heavily on synthetic, fossil fuel-derived products such as fertilizers, pesticides, and herbicides. These chemicals have failed to meet expectations, causing significant environmental damage and deteriorating soil health across regions like Barbados and the Caribbean. The widespread use of these products has led to nutrient-depleted soils, polluted ecosystems, and harmful impacts on public health, including rising chronic diseases due to poor-quality food.  In response to this crisis, I founded Red Diamond Compost with a mission to provide sustainable, organic alternatives to toxic agrochemicals. Our key innovation is the Diamond Matrix Bioconversion (DMB) system, transforming organic materials including invasive plant species and compost crops like sargassum seaweed and tithonia into high-quality, sustainable crop inputs. By harnessing natural processes, our products support the growth of beneficial soil microbes, improve soil structure, and promote nutrient cycling. This results in healthier, more fertile soils, enhanced water retention, and improved crop yields without the harmful effects of synthetic chemicals.  Our solutions benefit a wide range of end users, including home gardeners, farmers, landscapers, and communities seeking to improve food security and environmental sustainability. Through our innovative approach, we empower consumers with access to clean, nutritious food, while supporting regenerative farming practices that restore and protect ecosystems. This work is deeply personal to me as I ve seen firsthand the damage caused by conventional agricultural practices, having to overcome by own health crisis and the potential of organic solutions to drive positive change for both people and the planet.

Project Title: Your Food Regulatory Assistant
Executive Summary: Regasis is a startup that helps food manufacturers in Africa navigate complex regulatory requirements. Its platform automates compliance tracking, integrates with local databases, and provides real-time updates on regulations. Key features include intuitive dashboards, automated reminders, and tailored guidance. Regasis reduces risk, avoids penalties, and frees up resources, empowering small to medium-sized enterprises to focus on growth and confidently scale in a competitive market.
Innovation Description: Regasis is an innovative solution designed to address the challenge of regulatory compliance for food manufacturers in Africa. Food businesses, particularly small to medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), often struggle to keep up with the constantly changing regulations across various African countries. This complexity consumes time and resources, while non-compliance can lead to costly fines, legal issues and wastage in production.  Regasis solves this problem by offering a user-friendly digital platform that eases the compliance process. The platform integrates with national regulatory data, tracks in national legislation, and provides real-time updates on regulatory changes, ensuring that food manufacturers are always compliant. It features intuitive tools, automated reminders for audits and certifications, and country-specific guidance tailored to each food product. The scientific and technical insight behind Regasis is its ability to streamline regulatory management through automation and data integration, minimizing human error and manual tracking. By leveraging technology, the platform significantly reduces the compliance burden.  Immediate benefits include time savings, risk reduction, and cost savings for manufacturers. Sustainable benefits include enhanced food safety standards, improved industry transparency, and greater confidence in local food supply chains. For end users, including consumers and communities, this means safer food products, better consumer protection, and a more efficient food production system. Regasis fosters growth in the food industry while supporting the regulatory frameworks that ensure public health and safety.

Project Title: RemAI: Empowering households to make data-driven decisions to reduce household food waste
Executive Summary: The IFT Seed Award would be used to develop and scale Remy s own advance AI agent: RemAI. The aim of the RemAI is to enhance Remy s mobile application to further increase the user experience through AI, thus, maximising the impact, usability and savings Remy can produce for its users. The project will last 10 months and will have a total cost of $131,000, encompassing the research, development and implementation phases of RemAI.
Innovation Description: Household food waste is the leading driver of waste along the food supply chain, causing around 65% of the total generated waste. At a global level, food waste would be the third-largest emitter of GHG if it were a country, only following China and the USA. European avoidable household food waste causes approximately 73Mt CO2e and costs households  170bn annually. Food waste reduction is the second-biggest impact households can make to fight climate change, yet there is no viable, comprehensive and usable digital solution; Remy wants to change this.  Remy is Europe s first automated, AI-driven household kitchen management application that helps users know what ingredients they have at home, when it s going to expire, how they can incorporate them into their meals and lets them buy anything that s missing directly from their smartphones. In doing so, Remy saves households  2000, 100+ hours and 3000kg CO2e per year and can reduce 25.6Mt CO2e per year at scale by ensuring they only buy what they need and cook what they buy before it expires. Through the app, Remy can collect novel user emissions and behaviour data, which can be leveraged by retail partners to satisfy upcoming scope 3 reporting regulations and build data-driven waste prevention strategies.  Unlike prior attempts, Remy works because the commercialisation of AI and the change in reporting regulations for retailers make the proposition seamless for end users while providing leverage to scale cost-effectively through large retailers.

Project Title: ACCELERATING SOLUTIONS FOR FOOD WASTE - UPCYCLING AND THE CIRCULAR ECONOMY
Executive Summary: Rescued is a circular, upcycled food processor, ingredient supplier and service provider. Collaborating and innovating with stakeholders to accelerate upcycling and the circular economy as solutions for food waste.  Our stakeholders include farmers, growers, government, academia, manufacturers, technology partners, innovators, entrepreneurs, charitable food rescue organisations and go-to-market partners.   Project goals.   Complete development of Rescued Power Flour. Scaled trials of dehydration equipment and technology.  Four new upcycled food products developed.  International expansion strategy, including supporting technology.
Innovation Description: Problem - Food waste.   Project Drawdown, the global leader in ranking climate solutions, explains preventing food waste is the single most effective solution to prevent global warming of more than 2 degrees Celsius.   Solution - Upcycling and the Circular Economy.  Product innovation - Rescued Power Flour  Bread is one of the most wasted products globally. With a global annual production of 100 million tons, it is estimated that over 900,000 tons annually of all manufactured bread is wasted. (Source: ScienceDirect). Accelerating and scaling Rescued Power Flour innovation will be a significant contributor to achieving food waste reductions targets.   Rescued Bread Flour is Upcycled Food certified, zero-waste and a wheat flour alternative made by dehydrating and milling in-date surplus bread from supermarkets, bakeries and manufacturers into a fine powder. Once processed, Rescued Bread Flour has a shelf life of two years and offers manufacturing and shelf-life advantages over wheat flour.   Rescued Bread Flour is scientifically challenging to work with. From our experience we know a blended flour that incorporates Rescued Bread Flour, regeneratively grown grains, other diverse ingredients and other upcycled ingredients e.g., brewers spent grains is a valuable solution.  Benefits.   1. Reduced bread waste and associated negative impact and cost to the environment, economy and society.  2. Reduced bread packaging waste - recycled into new products.  3. Reduced demand on resources to grow wheat and manufacture bread (land, soil, water, energy, fertiliser, transportation)  4. A new upcycled ingredient available to manufacturers supporting food waste reduction targets and consumer sustainability demands.

Project Title: Urban and Peri-Urban Agriculture for better Health and Climate Resilience
Executive Summary: Indian cities are becoming more polluted and Indian agriculture is using more chemicals and water, causing negative health and environmental consequences. Our mission is to develop and scale  appropriate  UrbanAg technologies and operating models for Indian cities.   Large rooftops, dirty / unused plots, and urban infrastructure (roads, metros, parking lots, ponds) are our targets for urban farms. For large-scale and impact. Fresh, organic, zero-waste, urban vegetables can actually cost less than current market prices.
Innovation Description: Indian agriculture uses too much chemical fertilizers, dangerous pesticides and water, and farms are far from consumers. Both factors reduce food nutritional value, increase carbon footprints and increase wastage, driving up food prices. Consequently, malnourishment is at sub-Saharan-levels and India is the 3rd largest GHG emitter.   UrbanAg is nearly non-existent because of:    (a) Lack of suitable technologies for Indian cost-price-food choices combination, and   (b) No imaginative operating models for India s over-crowded cities.   High-tech farms are commercially unviable. And low-tech   low-productivity options are uneconomical.   Our collective experience is 30+ years in rooftop organic farming; sensors, automation and big data for environmental monitoring; and business models for sustainable buildings and cities.    Living Greens  proven, modular, 100% organic rooftop Portable Farming Systems ( PFS --1,500+ sold) delivers 3x the productivity of normal farms. We will add sensors and other technologies and build 0.5-1 acre farms on large roofs (schools, hospitals, factories and residential buildings) and unused / dirty plots with strong operating processes, to double yield per square foot. Once proven, these can be built above parking lots, ponds and even roads and railways huge potential even in the densest cities.   Economical technology with high yields plus nearly zero transportation and wastage, can deliver the healthiest produce with minimal environmental impact at lower than current market prices! Improving health, making cities greener, recycling used-water and compost from waste, absorbing GHG, making roofs and buildings cooler (hence less AC), and creating green urban jobs are the benefits.

Project Title: Mixed Bean Tempeh: A Local Solution for Global Food Sustainability
Executive Summary: This initiative promotes mixed bean tempeh using jack beans and soybeans as a sustainable alternative to reduce Indonesia's reliance on imported soybeans (90% sourced from Argentina, the U.S., and Brazil). Incorporating jack beans supports local farmers through fair trade, improves livelihoods, and enhances soil health via regenerative and organic farming practices. This approach strengthens food security and builds a resilient, eco-friendly, and inclusive agricultural ecosystem.
Innovation Description: Indonesia relies heavily on soybean imports, with 90% of its 2.2 million tons consumed in 2023 sourced from the U.S., Argentina, and Brazil. This dependency creates economic vulnerabilities, environmental degradation, and high greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The intensive soybean production in exporting countries often leads to deforestation, soil degradation, and unsustainable farming practices. Additionally, transporting soybeans across continents generates significant carbon emissions, contributing to climate change and undermining efforts for sustainable food production. Our initiative addresses these challenges by introducing mixed bean tempeh, combining jack beans with soybeans as a sustainable alternative. Jack beans have a nutrient profile comparable to soybeans, making them a suitable ingredient for tempeh production. Consumer tests have shown the taste of mixed bean tempeh to be well-accepted, ensuring market viability. Jack beans are nitrogen-fixing legumes that naturally enhance soil fertility, reducing reliance on synthetic fertilizers and their associated emissions. By cultivating jack beans through regenerative and organic farming systems, we empower local farmers with sustainable practices that improve soil health, reduce input costs, and diversify their income sources. This solution strengthens food security while offering consumers a nutritious, locally produced alternative to conventional tempeh. Reducing reliance on imported soybeans lowers carbon footprints and supports a transition to a resilient, self-sufficient food system. Our initiative mitigates the environmental impact of imports, improves farmer livelihoods, and promotes sustainable, health-focused food, aligning with global goals to combat climate change and enhance community well-being.

Project Title: Shifting from wet to dry granulated organic wastes composting with incentives to farmers for behavioral change toward compost application
Executive Summary: Our project is bringing new approach to transform organic waste into granulated compost through EM-tech innovative, climate-smart practices that reduce landfill pressure from waste accumulation. Wastes are recycled into eco-friendly agro-inputs to promote natural-based crop nutrients and soil organic matter (SOM). The project aims at changing farmers distrust of organic wastes generated from waste by considering them garbage. This means from wet to dry and granulated compost similar to chemical fertilizer.
Innovation Description: Organic wastes generated from domestic and urban public landfills may cause to 25% of GHGs emission. IPCC 6 assessment report shows that around 2.01 billion tons of municipal solid waste (MSW) are annually produced. According to Rwanda Environment Management Authority (REMA) 2023 reports, estimated 1,800 2,000 tons of wastes are produced per day. Of which more than 70% are organic and 50% of them are of good quality for compost use. However, only 2% of these organic wastes are managed and recycled. In combination with very high unemployment statistics from National Statistics of Rwanda (NISR report, 2022), of which Youth unemployment account 20.5% where females represent 19.8% of the total, Rwanda Government and partners have made a lot of efforts to attracted SMSs-SMEs in recycling of organic wastes to agro-inputs. However, despite the efforts made, SMSs-SMEs invested in waste recycling has failed due to high number of farmers distrust of waste compost due to its wet-form, which makes farmers consider it as lifetime garbage. After our 2022 preliminary discussions with 120 farmers, about 100% of them have mentioned that wet form of compost are always looking like garbage. And suggested that if is dried and transformed to look or mimic chemical fertilizer, farmers are willing to change and adopt new product. In this context, our project aims at shifting from wet to granulated organic waste composting with certain incentives to farmers for behavioral change toward compost and awareness on its adoption as new locally made agro-input.

Project Title: Irrigation Systems In Africa
Executive Summary: With the global population expected to reach over 9 billion by 2050, there is a continuous need to increase food production and we believe Irrigation systems can help achieve that. Project Title: Enhancing Sustainable Cassava and Maize Production for Improved Food Security and Nutrition in Tanzania
Executive Summary: This project focuses on enhancing sustainable cassava and maize production in Tanzania to improve food security, nutrition, and livelihoods. It will implement regenerative agricultural practices, reduce food waste, and promote nutritious, affordable food. Innovation Description: In Kigoma region, Tanzania, food insecurity and malnutrition are significant challenges, particularly in rural areas, refugee camps, and host communities. Limited access to nutritious, affordable food, compounded by unsustainable agricultural practices, exacerbates these issues. The lack of proper post-harvest management techniques leads to high food waste, further reducing food availability.  Our project tackles these challenges by enhancing sustainable cassava and maize production through regenerative agricultural practices. This includes improved crop management, efficient resource utilization, and the reduction of food waste. By incorporating innovative post-harvest techniques and promoting nutrient-rich, affordable food, the project ensures that vulnerable populations have access to safe and nutritious food. It also focuses on empowering local farmers and refugees through education and capacity-building, enabling them to adopt sustainable farming practices that increase productivity while preserving the environment.  The scientific and technical insights underpinning this solution stem from agroecology and regenerative agriculture, which emphasize soil health, water conservation, and minimizing the environmental footprint of food production. These practices are projected to increase crop yields by 2,000 tons annually, reduce reliance on chemical inputs, and mitigate the impact of climate change on agriculture.  Immediate and Sustainable Benefits:      Consumers will have access to healthier, more affordable food.     Farmers will experience improved livelihoods through increased productivity (an additional 2,000 tons annually) and better income opportunities.     The environment will benefit from reduced agricultural waste and more sustainable land use, saving up to 30 million liters of water annually.     Communities will see enhanced food security, reduced malnutrition, and stronger local economies.

Project Title: Building a Circular Economy with Certified Shea Processing & Sustainable Cooking Practices in Ghana
Executive Summary: This project empowers rural Ghanaian communities through organic and fair trade certifications, a HACCP-compliant processing facility, and sustainable cooking practices using shea waste. By addressing land challenges, providing training, and certifying shea, neem, groundnut, and soybean oils, the project enhances market access and income for smallholder farmers. Partnering with Mukuru Clean Cookstoves, it promotes a circular economy, reduces environmental impact, and prepares communities for premium global markets with sustainable, certified, and climate-positive products.
Innovation Description: This project addresses the dual challenges of environmental degradation and limited market access for rural Ghanaian communities by creating a circular economy centered around sustainable shea processing. Currently, communities face barriers like high certification costs, lack of compliant infrastructure, and harmful traditional cooking methods that rely on firewood, contributing to deforestation and emissions. These issues limit income potential and sustainability for farmers and producers.  To solve this, the project integrates several innovations. It secures organic and fair trade certifications, enabling smallholder farmers to access premium markets globally. A HACCP-compliant processing facility will maintain certification standards while increasing production capacity. The project also partners with Mukuru Clean Cookstoves to design larger, efficient stoves fueled by shea waste. This circular economy reduces reliance on firewood, decreases emissions, and provides a cost-effective energy source.  Scientific insights include the efficient conversion of agricultural waste into fuel and the implementation of certification processes that meet global standards. Technical innovations include clean cookstove engineering and HACCP facility design.  Immediate benefits include improved income for farmers through premium market access, reduced deforestation, and safer cooking practices. Long-term, the project fosters sustainability, enhances food security, and diversifies income streams by certifying neem, groundnut, and soybean oils. Communities gain resilience through training in branding, packaging, and sustainable practices, preparing them for global competitiveness. This integrated approach supports local economies, protects the environment, and builds sustainable livelihoods, positively impacting farmers, producers, and the broader society.

Project Title: Sea-Land Symbiosis
Executive Summary: SOS transforms invasive seaweed into sustainable, nutrient-rich agricultural products that enhance crop yield, reduce chemical fertilizer use, and improve soil health. By upcycling invasive seaweed, we support regenerative practices that reduce ocean pollution and empower coastal communities through job creation. Our approach addresses food security, environmental resilience, and sustainable agricultural growth, helping build a more sustainable food system from the Caribbean outward.
Innovation Description: SOS addresses the critical problem of invasive sargassum seaweed in the Caribbean, which devastates marine ecosystems, threatens coastal economies, and leads to significant waste and environmental pollution. Leveraging biotechnology, we sustainable harvest and transform this seaweed into nutrient-rich, eco-friendly products that support agriculture, aquaculture, and soil health, effectively turning a harmful waste product into a resource. Our innovation replaces synthetic fertilizers with an organic, nutrient-packed alternative that improves crop yield, enhances soil microbiome health, improves crop nutritional value and reduces greenhouse gas emissions. This process not only benefits farmers through higher productivity and lower input costs but also contributes to regenerative agricultural practices that restore soil vitality and reduce dependency on harmful inputs. The scientific foundation of our solution comes from understanding the biochemical richness of seaweed such as sargassum, which is naturally high in polysaccharides, antioxidants, and other growth-promoting compounds such as phytohormones. By converting sargassum into valuable products like crop enhancers and hydroponic substrates, we provide immediate benefits to farmers, communities, and ecosystems. Coastal communities gain economic opportunities through sustainable seaweed harvesting and product development, while society at large benefits from a healthier ocean, reduced environmental damage, and greater food security. This approach is immediately impactful and scalable we are already working in 6 countries, providing sustainable benefits across agricultural, environmental, and economic domains. Our end-users, including from small to big farmers and coastal communities, gain both environmentally-friendly solutions and economic resilience, making our innovation a model for transforming ecological challenges into sustainable development.

Project Title: Farm Urban App: Simplifying urban farming for a healthier and more resilient food system
Executive Summary: With Farm Urban, we re building a sustainable future where cities can grow their own food, one farm at a time.  By incorporating AI technology to enhance urban farming, Farm Urban App connects urban farmers with all the resources needed to farm successfully within cities farmable landowners, weather & indoor information, AI harvest calendar, compost makers, and regenerative knowledge   while providing a platform to sell harvested fresh produce directly to city dwellers.
Innovation Description: Africans do not have equal access to healthy food.  Poor health outcomes related to unhealthy food consumption such as diet-related illnesses, including obesity, diabetes, and heart disease, do not reflect food preferences but are tied to poor accessibility to healthy foods due to the displacement of agriculture to forested rural areas far from the cities where 80% of food produced is consumed. If the rates of diet-related illnesses are to decline, we must increase the accessibility of healthy foods within our cities. We are solving this problem with Farm Urban App. Our app uses geotagging to quickly locate urban spaces and evaluate them on farming potential. A user can find a location listed by urban space owners, mark the outline of their desired farm space, choose a farming method, and a selection of produce to grow on the farm. The AI algorithm on the app will then let the user know how much of each product the farm can produce and how many people can be fed. The profitability of the farm is calculated by the app based on real calculations of the harvest calendar, allowing everyone with an interest in urban agriculture to discover the feasibility of farming in their cities and connecting them to the landowner, organic fertilizers, regenerative knowledge etc. During harvest, the app notifies consumers about the new harvest, connecting the closest farms to buyers.  We are helping our target customers to increase access to healthy, locally grown, and culturally appropriate food sources.
