Project Title: The Farmlink Project
Executive Summary: The Farmlink Project’s mission is to connect surplus produce to communities in need, reduce carbon emissions, and empower the next generation of young changemakers. The Farmlink Project serves as a “link” connecting the broken supply chains of the agricultural and food access industries.    Our vision is to transform the food system, end food insecurity and eliminate food waste at the agricultural level.    The Farmlink Project was founded in April 2020 by a group of college students in response to the pandemic, which had exposed flaws in our food system, causing millions of American families to face a new reality of food insecurity, all while billions of pounds of fresh food rotted in fields, and has since grown to a team of 130+ college student volunteers guided by 21 full-time team members.    Thus far, we have delivered over 130 million pounds of food which has made millions meals possible for individuals in food insecure communities across the United States and Mexico. As a growing organization we are focused on creating large-scale food system reform, decreasing our operations and redistribution costs, and ensuring equitable access to food for underserved communities.    Our team provides seamless logistics to connect farmers and food relief organizations across the United States. We are building a scalable, self-sustaining food network with a technology platform to automate transactions and transportation while also working to offset carbon emissions.    Currently, 26.4% of the global population struggles with food insecurity, while at the same time 1.2 trillion pounds of food go to waste every year. Rotting food creates methane, turning a social disaster into an ecological one. If food waste were a country, it would be the third-largest emitter of global greenhouse gas emissions.

Project Title: Empowering1000Women
Executive Summary: The Empowering Women for Climate Resilience and Economic Independence project strengthens vulnerable women s economic self-reliance and climate resilience. By providing training in financial literacy, climate-smart agriculture, and environmental stewardship, the project enables women to lead sustainable, income-generating activities and adapt to climate impacts. Through community-driven initiatives like Village Savings and Loan Associations and Women s Climate Action Groups, the project builds lasting resilience, supporting food security, economic growth, and climate justice in rural communities.
Innovation Description: In Sierra Leone, rural women face economic insecurity and heightened vulnerability to climate impacts, which include soil degradation, erratic rainfall, and loss of biodiversity. These challenges, combined with limited access to resources, perpetuate cycles of poverty, food insecurity, and environmental decline. Women, who are primary contributors to agriculture, often lack training in sustainable practices and financial resources to transition to resilient, eco-friendly livelihoods. Our solution empowers these women by providing training in climate-smart agriculture, financial literacy, and leadership, equipping them with tools to adapt to climate change and achieve economic self-sufficiency. Through establishing Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) and Women s Climate Action Groups, participants can save, access small loans, and invest in sustainable farming and small businesses. Agroforestry and soil conservation practices are introduced, improving yields while protecting the environment. The innovation lies in combining economic empowerment with climate resilience, addressing both immediate needs and long-term sustainability. Women gain critical skills, increasing food security and reducing dependency on environmentally damaging practices. Communities benefit from improved ecosystem health, greater economic activity, and resilience to climate shocks. This solution not only elevates the role of women as community leaders but also fosters sustainable development, aligning economic growth with environmental conservation.

Project Title: Scaling in Kenya and expanding into other African countries: Breakthrough bioherbicide technology improves food and economic security for small-scale farmers
Executive Summary: Toothpick Project's innovative bio-herbicide technology uses a selected strain of host-specific fungus to protect crops from Striga witchweed, Africa's worst pest threat to food security for small-scale farmers. Our selected fungal strain is a unique nature-based herbicide distributed to farmers and applied as a seed coating to restore their crop yield. One of the first bioherbicides to be commercialized in the world, the game-changing agri-tech is a safe, effective, affordable alternative to traditional chemical herbicides.
Innovation Description: Striga, an invasive parasitic weed, attacks the roots of staple crops like maize and sorghum, reducing crop yield up to 100%. 50 million hectares of croplands (~40 million farms) in sub-Saharan Africa show Striga infestation, causing $9+ billion in crop loss annually. Striga forms an intense soil seed bank by adding over 50,000 seeds per season. The seeds spread easily across farms through wind, human and animal traffic, and farming tools. Our beneficiaries, smallholder farmers, are generally below the poverty level of $2.15/person per day.   After decades of research and development with team members from three continents, our technology uses a strain of endemic Kenyan fungus, Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. strigae, selected for over-production of specific amino acids to kill striga but not crops. The resulting product, Kichawi Kill (kichawi means  magic  in Swahili), is a groundbreaking approach to striga management and global weed management. Proof-of-concept trials took place in 2014-2015, showing a 42-56% increase in yield. The fungi were originally grown on toothpicks and delivered to the village level for a secondary inoculum production. The pilot social enterprise in Kenya launched commercial distribution in 2021. In 2023, the seed coating product was approved in Kenya, significantly reducing the price and increasing the shelf life. TCL is expected to break-even in Kenya in 2025. Expansion efforts to Uganda started in 2024, followed by other sub-Saharan Africa countries in 2025.   The technology improves food security and economic stability for farmers and reduces biodiversity loss caused by synthetic chemical herbicides.

Project Title: UVC LED-based systems to clean water in the field and other emergency situations across the world: Ukraine case

Novel UVC LED-based water systems for disinfection are compact  and easily installed in the water dispensing devices as plug-and-play water treatment systems  for most point-of-use applications. The use of UVC LED for water can save people's lives by  ensuring sustainable access to clean, disinfected water  After first 25 UV LEDs mobile kits were delivered and tested in Ukraine, funding is required to  scale project and efficacy validation studies, and provide more UVC LEDs installations in  critical locations. Project Title: Scaling and Improving UVC LED Water Disinfection for Global Impact to Protect Vulnerable Communities Against Waterborne Diseases
Executive Summary: Further develop, validate and  deploy advanced mobile water disinfection kits that utilize germicidal ultraviolet light (UVC) LED  technology in combination with pre-treatment cleaning modules.  These kits are sustainable, low cost and safe alternative for  plastic bottles and designed for easy transport, operation and distribution, making them ideal for displaced families and vulnerable communities facing water scarcity due to conflicts and environmental degradation.
Innovation Description: Global climate change and geopolitical conflicts are closely tied to issues of water accessibility and quality. Natural and human-made disasters can destroy or contaminate water supplies, increasing the risk of diseases. Currently, distributing water in plastic bottles is a common emergency solution. However, the high costs of production and transportation, along with plastic waste, microplastics contamination of water and soil make it an unsustainable option in crises.  Germicidal ultraviolet (UVC) light is known as effective nonthermal nonchemical nonionizing physical method at killing waterborne pathogens. UVC LED systems are compact, efficient,  safe and easily installed as plug-and-play solutions for point-of-use water purification. UVC LEDs, combined with necessary pre-treatment methods, can clean and  disinfect water from local sources such as rivers, lakes, and wells, providing microbiologically and chemically safe drinking water. This local water treatment ensures fast, cost-effective, long-term access to clean water, reduces call and  reliance on plastic, chemical disinfection and minimizes environmental pollution.  Access to safe drinking water  in crisis situations reduces the risk of waterborne diseases like diarrhea, typhoid, and cholera, leading to better diets, health and fewer medical expenses.  UV4Good collaborates with local scientists and engineers to create customized solutions, guided by community input. We use local resources and test solutions to ensure their effectiveness. By adapting innovative technologies to address climate change and human-made disasters, we can protect human health, save lives, provide access to better diets  and reduce environmental pollution.

Project Title: Building a Digital Twin of the Global Water and Food System
Executive Summary: Our solution is to build a  digital twin  of the global water and food system, driven by the latest climate data, continuously calibrated against production, resource use, and trade data amongst other information sources using machine learning. In this project we will track, in real time, unsustainable water use and the export of associated risk via virtual water trade and provide quantitative data on alternative water conservation strategies so that organizations can take informed decisions.
Innovation Description: Providing sufficient food in a changing climate will be one of the great challenges in the years ahead. The increasing frequency and intensity of extreme events such as floods and droughts, and their spreading impacts, ask for faster and different responses to crises than before. Water resources and food stores are being depleted rapidly, reducing our buffer to deal with extremes. While ever more data becomes available, experience tells us how demanding it is to gather and analyse up-to-date information on climate, water, and food security from a wide variety of online resources. Farmers, cooperatives, NGOs and other frontline organizations, even those large and established, generally lack the capacity and capability to monitor the impact of their activities or decisions under highly variable and changing climatic conditions and other externalities, even more so in times of crisis. AI has the potential to facilitate and speed up the process of fact-based decision making.  Our operational digital twin covers the information gap between current scientific analysis which is often isolated and irregular, and real-time decision making. We aim to pilot a novel approach to track, in real time, unsustainable water use including the export of associated risk via virtual water trade. Reliable, up-to-date information will help farmers target investments and resource use to improve their livelihoods, water, and food security in a changing climate. It will also help consumers, agri-food businesses, and policy makers, to understand the remote and interlinked impact of their decisions.

Project Title: Functional Foods from Cultured Milk Products Supplemented with Baobab  Fruit.
Executive Summary: The baobab (Adansonia digitata l.) tree is endemic to the drylands and semi-arid regions of Kenya, which are often hotspots for food insecurity. Baobab products can boost the nutrient uptake and prevent nutritional deficiencies. However, there is limited utilization of baobab products despite the abundance of essential nutrients and bioactive components. The innovative formulation in this case enhances the suitability of the baobab fruit pulp in addressing various micronutrient deficiencies. Baobab fruit pulp is first separated from the shells, fibers, and seeds. Baobab fruit pulp is blended with the milk, the mixture is then pasteurized at 85℃, rapid cooling and mesophilic culture inoculation carried out at 25℃. Incubation is done at ambient temperatures for 16 to 18 hours, after which the curd is broken and the product cooled to 4℃ to stop further fermentation. The product is then packaged in a sustainable package. The product also offers potential supply of prebiotics and probiotics as functional food especially for vulnerable populations due to the many health promoting properties. Further, the cultured milk enriched with baobab pulp has a high potential for commercialization ultimately improving livelihoods and nutrition among communities living along baobab regions. Promotion of the developed product should also be carried out among people beyond the baobab growing areas to increase utilization of the fruit pulp. This has a practical implication in meeting the demand for commercialization of nutritious and health food trends in the Kenyan market.

Project Title: Vertical Block Farming for Urban Land-constrained Communities
Executive Summary: This project targets land-constrained urban communities, including refugees and stay-at-home mothers in Kampala. This innovative project will install vertical farms in greenhouses using a block farming model to optimize space and productivity. The initiative aims to combat hunger, starvation, and malnutrition by empowering beneficiaries to grow their own food sustainably.  By integrating organic gardening training, market linkages, and value addition, VMG aims to strengthen food security and build economic resilience within urban vulnerable communities.
Innovation Description: Uganda faces a critical food insecurity challenge. As of January 2023, approximately 16.4 million Ugandans struggled with insufficient food consumption (EPRCUG). Alarmingly, 28% of households experienced food insecurity in 2022, with three in ten skipping meals or going a day without food (Monitor). This issue is exacerbated in urban areas, where limited land availability compounds the problem. Globally, solving food insecurity would require farmland almost the size of Brazil an impractical solution.  VMG s Vertical Block Farming provides an innovative response to this crisis by maximizing food production in land-constrained urban environments. Through installing vertical farms in greenhouses under a block farming model, VMG transforms small urban spaces into highly efficient food production units. This approach addresses hunger and malnutrition while reducing the environmental footprint of traditional farming.  The system integrates vermicomposting, ensuring sustainable nutrient recycling. Beneficiaries, including refugees and stay-at-home mothers in Kampala and Wakiso, receive training in farming techniques, value addition, and market linkages to improve livelihoods.  Immediate benefits include increased access to fresh, nutritious food and enhanced household income. Over the long term, the solution promotes food security, reduces urban hunger, and contributes to climate-smart agriculture by optimizing land and resource use. VMG s innovative approach transforms food production, providing a scalable and sustainable solution for urban food insecurity.

Project Title: Smart biocapsules for sustainable agriculture: reducing agrochemical use and enhancing food safety globally.
Executive Summary: Vexxel develops innovative protein-based biocapsules that enable precise, on-demand delivery of inputs in agriculture. These biodegradable, non-toxic capsules reduce agrochemical usage by up to 90%, enhance crop protection, and improve food safety. By integrating biosensors that detect pathogens or environmental conditions, our technology promotes sustainable farming, lowers costs, and minimizes environmental impact. This project advances global food systems by improving access to safe, nutritious, and affordable food while addressing planetary health challenges.
Innovation Description: The global food system faces critical challenges: excessive agrochemical use leads to environmental damage, high costs, and growing resistance from pathogens, while only 1-5% of applied chemicals reach their intended target. This problem is relevant because it exacerbates environmental degradation, compromises food safety, and increases economic burdens on farmers, hindering sustainable agriculture worldwide. Inefficiencies contribute to unsafe food, soil degradation, and climate change, as highlighted by the FAO, which reports that agrochemical overuse is a major driver of agricultural environmental harm. Vexxel addresses this with smart, protein-based biocapsules, an innovative, biodegradable, and non-toxic solution. These biocapsules integrate advanced biosensors to detect pathogens or environmental conditions and release active compounds precisely when needed. Pilot tests have demonstrated a 90% reduction in agrochemical usage, cutting farmers' costs by 60% while ensuring effective pathogen control. This minimizes environmental impact and makes sustainable farming more accessible and profitable. This solution is rooted in cutting-edge protein engineering, leveraging proprietary nanotechnology that ensures scalability and adaptability to existing agricultural practices. Unlike traditional methods, Vexxel s technology empowers nature to decide when inputs are required, reducing waste and increasing efficiency. Immediate benefits include safer food, healthier soils, and reduced farmer costs, enabling compliance with regulations and access to premium markets. Treating 30,000 hectares with Vexxel's biocapsules reduces 77,000 tons of CO₂eq equivalent to avoiding 320,833 short-haul flights or 17,500 flights around the world per passenger. Validated eco-impact studies demonstrate this significant impact aligns with global climate goals.

Project Title: Waste to Nutrition: Women-Led Sustainable Manufacturing for Safe, Nutritious, and Resilient Food Systems
Executive Summary: Our project empowers low-income women to build sustainable food manufacturing businesses using renewable energy-powered hubs and waste-to-wealth solutions. By converting organic waste into biogas for energy to power the hub, and biofertilizer for farming by our farming partners, we improve clean energy access, food safety, and climate resilience. Through training, resources, market access, and sustainable practices, we help women transform homegrown ideas into thriving enterprises, driving food security, economic growth, and sustainable communities.
Innovation Description: In rural communities in Nigeria, women possess homegrown knowledge of food production, but a lack of funds, resources, and training prevents them from turning this knowledge into viable enterprises. As a result, farm produce goes to waste due to the absence of processing facilities, while communities depend on imported, additive-filled foods. Additionally, these communities face drought, flooding, and low farming yields, further threatening food security and livelihoods. WEM HUB Africa addresses these challenges through a holistic solution that combines: Renewable Energy-Powered Manufacturing Hubs: Providing access to shared facilities powered by biogas and solar energy, reducing costs and enabling sustainable food production even during drought-related power disruptions. BIOCOIN Program: Transforming organic waste into biogas for energy and biofertilizer for farming. This improves soil health, boosts crop resilience to drought and flooding, and enhances moisture retention, leading to higher farming yields. Training and Market Access: Equipping women with skills and pathways to produce safe, nutritious food and bring products to market, reducing dependence on imported foods and minimizing post-harvest losses. This innovation mitigates flooding by reducing organic waste clogging drainage systems and ensures access to clean energy and biofertilizer, supporting sustainable agriculture. Immediate benefits include improved livelihoods, food security, and health outcomes. Long-term benefits include climate resilience, reduced environmental pollution, and stronger local economies. By empowering women and transforming waste into resources, WEM HUB Africa builds resilient communities where everyone has access to safe, nutritious, and affordable food despite environmental challenges.

Project Title: Shameta; From Tradition to Maternal Nutrition to Improve Nutritional Status of Lactating Mothers in Ethiopia
Executive Summary: Shameta is a traditional porridge made from grains, commonly consumed by lactating mothers for recovery, strength, and breast milk production. However, research has highlighted a gap between community perceptions and the actual nutritional value and safety of Shameta. This initiative seeks to enhance the nutritional status of lactating mothers through food-to-food fortification and the development of starter cultures. By incorporating nutrient-dense ingredients such as high-quality protein maize, soybean, barley, and linseed, the project aims to boost Shameta's nutritional profile. Additionally, it focuses on improving shelf life, creating effective packaging materials, and developing starter cultures. To raise awareness about the improved Shameta, the project will organize workshops, and training sessions, and produce a documentary showcasing the preparation process and utilization benefits.
Innovation Description: The nutritional status of lactating mothers in Ethiopia is influenced by food insecurity, poverty, cultural practices, and poor dietary diversity (Haileslassie et al., 2013; Alemayehu et al., 2015; Moges et al., 2018; Kejela et al., 2019; IFRC, 2021). To address this, a multifaceted approach is needed, including better access to nutrient-rich foods. Upgrading traditional fermented foods like Shameta, porridge made from grains and used for lactating mothers to the purpose of recovery, strength and breast milk production can provide affordable and nutritious food. However, studies revealed a gap between community perceptions and the actual nutritional value and safety of Shameta (Kitessa et al., 2022a; 2022b; 2024), indicating the need for further research on its impact on mothers and infants. Optimizing the processing conditions and ingredient ratios of Shameta is crucial for ensuring its safety, quality, and nutritional values. Using high-quality protein maize (rich in lysine and tryptophan), barley ( -glucan), soybeans (packed with protein, polyunsaturated fatty acids, and calcium), and linseed (rich in omega-3 fatty acids) enhances the flour nutritional profile for shmaeta preparation. A well-defined starter culture further improves fermentation control, safety, and consistency. Exploring its potential to promote breast milk production and support infant growth is also a topic of interest. Additionally, evaluating the shelf-life of flour used for Shameta preparation and selecting appropriate packaging materials are essential for efficient distribution and transportation across regions. Upon successful project completion, end users will gain immediate access to affordable, optimized flour and starter cultures to prepare Shameta at home or for business purposes. This will promote enhanced maternal and infant health, boost breast milk production, support optimal infant growth, and foster job creation. Over the long term, the product becomes affordable throughout the country, and both mother's and infant's health benefits, and economic empowerment.

Project Title: Climate Resilient Digital Agronomy Platform for the Farmers and Professional Growers
Executive Summary: This platform delivers climate-resilient crop advisory and agronomy solutions to smallholder farmers and professional growers, enabling cost savings on inputs like agrochemicals and fertilizers, efficient use of natural resources (soil and water), and reduced greenhouse gas emissions from agricultural activities.
Innovation Description: Problem: Scientific Information gap in the farmer and growers communities for climate resilient farming practices. Less crop  diversification among farmers causing commoditization of crop output leading less market price. No incentive is given to farmers for growing crops through  climate friendly farming practices   Innovation and Solutions : This innovation bridges the scientific information gap among farmers and growers by providing tailored climate-resilient crop advisory and agronomy practices. It equips smallholder farmers and professional growers with actionable insights, ensuring efficient use of inputs like agrochemicals and fertilizers, optimizing soil and water usage, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.  The platform addresses two critical problems: low crop diversification and lack of incentives for climate-friendly practices. Limited crop diversification leads to market saturation, reducing profitability, while traditional farming methods often exacerbate environmental degradation.  Through advanced digital tools, IoT devices, and real-time data analysis, the platform offers precise recommendations for crop diversification, sustainable resource management, and climate-smart farming techniques. These insights are based on cutting-edge research and climate modeling, ensuring actionable and region-specific solutions.  Immediate benefits include:      For Farmers: Lower input costs, increased profitability through market-relevant crop diversification, and incentives for adopting eco-friendly practices.     For Consumers: Access to sustainably grown, high-quality crops.     For the Environment: Reduced greenhouse gas emissions, improved soil health, and water conservation.     For Society: Promotion of sustainable agriculture, enhancing food security and resilience against climate change.  This innovation transforms agriculture into a sustainable, climate-resilient practice, benefitting farmers, consumers, and the planet.

Project Title: Smart Solutions for Sustainable Food Systems and Resource Optimization
Executive Summary: WeavAir leverages IoT, AI, and drone technologies to prevent food spoilage, optimize agricultural practices, and enhance sustainability. Our smart storage systems monitor 20+ metrics in real-time, reducing waste, energy use, and costs. Combined with precision agriculture tools, we empower farmers and businesses to boost productivity, improve resource efficiency, and create new revenue streams through carbon credits. This innovative approach ensures safer, more resilient food systems while supporting environmental and economic sustainability globally.
Innovation Description: The global food system faces critical challenges, including food spoilage, waste, resource inefficiency, and climate resilience. Up to one-third of food produced globally is wasted, contributing to hunger, economic loss, and environmental degradation through greenhouse gas emissions. Farmers and producers struggle with unpredictable environmental conditions, limited data for informed decision-making, and high operational costs.  WeavAir addresses these challenges with innovative IoT, AI, and drone-powered solutions. Our smart food storage systems use multi-sensor IoT devices to monitor over 20 metrics, such as temperature, humidity, and gas emissions, in real-time. These systems detect spoilage conditions early, prevent waste, and optimize energy use, cutting operational costs by 30% and energy consumption by 60%.  In agriculture, our platform integrates drone technology, satellite hyperspectral imagery, and field sensors to enable precision agriculture. By providing accurate, real-time data, it optimizes crop rotation, improves resource use, enhances climate resilience, and reduces costs tenfold. The solution also supports sustainability by validating carbon credits, creating new revenue streams for farmers.  This innovation combines cutting-edge technology and practical application to deliver measurable benefits: safer and fresher food for consumers, reduced waste and costs for producers, improved productivity for farmers, and lower environmental impact for society. These insights empower stakeholders across the food system to make data-driven decisions, ensuring a sustainable, equitable, and resilient global food network.

Benefits:  Immediate: Access to fresh, nutritious food, reduced household food expenses, and new income streams. Sustainable: Improved livelihoods, self-reliance, community food systems resilience, and reduced environmental impact through resource-efficient farming practices. Project Title: Farmers Post: Getting Food from Farms to Families
Executive Summary: Farmers Post aims to transform our food system by directly connecting farmers to consumers using the United States Postal Service (USPS)   reducing food waste, supporting small farms, and delivering fresh produce to those in need. WWF has advanced Farmers Post from concept to reality through research, partnerships, and pilots. With the USPS on board, we re poised to expand pilots and test packaging solutions, gathering critical insights to scale Farmers Post for a nationwide roll-out.
Innovation Description: Across the US, some of the most food-insecure counties are the same ones producing abundant fresh produce yet much of it never reaches those in need. Our current food system fails to connect farms directly to consumers, leaving small farmers struggling to profit while millions lack access to healthy food. Just one in ten adults in the US eats enough fruits and vegetables, yet up to 40% of fresh produce grown in this country is wasted. There is increasing recognition of this problem and a broader push to address it through Food is Medicine (FIM) initiatives, which focus on local food systems and preventative healthcare through healthy diets; however, last mile delivery and consumer reach remain major pain points. Farmers Post addresses these challenges by leveraging USPS  logistics expertise to deliver fresh produce from farms to consumers, reducing waste, improving access to nutritious food, and supporting small farmers.  With IFT s support, WWF has advanced this from concept to reality. What started as research on viable solutions and feasibility has now moved into the planning and implementation stages. Through key partnerships and pilot programs with 4P Foods, a Virginia-based food hub, and Healthy PlanEat, a Connecticut-based sustainable food tech platform, we have refined the Farmers Post model, inspiring USPS to explore a full Farmers Post program. By creating avenues for small farmers to ship directly to consumers, while leveraging the work of food hubs and FIM initiatives, Farmers Post offers a transformative path forward for farmers, consumers, and the environment.

Project Title: Garden To Table Pipeline (G2T) Chicago
Executive Summary: The G2T Pipeline is a sustainable and circular food system that revolves around nutrient rich locally grown produce from 23 community gardens on 8,100 sf of land, strategically distributed across the community. Five local nonprofit partners support gardens and distribute food to anyone in need.  By working together this partnership grows 13,000 pounds of produce, distributes 48,000 prepared meals,  rescued 250,000 pounds of food and serves 87,738 individuals each year.
Innovation Description: North Lawndale is a community of 35,000 individuals served by one sub-par mid-size grocery store. While we are located in the city of Chicago, there is no traditional local food supply in our community. The G2T Pipeline is the community s response  to simply feed our neighbors by growing the most nutrient dense locally grown produce and distributing it at 23 local gardens and three community food hubs.    Statistical data can be provided to support this reality if requested. Based on the lines of individuals forming early for fresh produce and prepared meals at our 3 food hubs the need is dramatic.  In 2023 more than 112,000 human encounters occurred at G2T Pipeline food/meal distributions.  This number is 3 times larger than the community we serve.    Our non-traditional food supply is growing exponentially in terms of production, distribution, growing capacity, manpower and financial support; however the lines of individuals waiting for food exceed the supply we have.

Project Title: Waste4Food
Executive Summary: Waste4Food is an innovative program that tackles plastic waste and food insecurity by exchanging plastic waste for farm produce. Partnering with local farmers and waste collectors, we aim to reduce plastic waste, promote sustainable agriculture, and provide affordable nutritious food to underserved communities.

In these regions, plastic waste clogs waterways, harms wildlife, and exacerbates flooding, while many families struggle to access nutritious food.  Waste4Food addresses these challenges by creating a closed-loop system where plastic waste is collected and exchanged for farm produce. Our innovation partners local farmers, waste collectors, and community groups to:  - Reduce plastic waste in landfills and waterways - Increase access to fresh, nutritious produce for underserved communities - Support sustainable agriculture and boost local economies  Our solution leverages insights from circular economy principles, behavioral economics, and community-based initiatives. By providing an economic incentive for waste collection and offering affordable produce, we empower individuals and communities to make sustainable choices.  Benefits include:  - Reduced plastic waste and pollution - Increased food security and nutrition - Economic benefits for farmers, waste collectors, and local communities - Community engagement and education on sustainable practices  By addressing these interconnected challenges, Waste4Food creates a more sustainable, equitable food system for Lagos and Ogun States.

Project Title: PANGAN Program: Revitalizing indigenous farming and building a sustainable food system for a climate-resilient bioeconomy and community
Executive Summary: The PANGAN Program addresses food insecurity in West Timor by revitalizing indigenous farming practices, promoting diverse and nutritious local food, and utilizing effective technologies. PANGAN s next phase pilots a Local Food Hub, a scalable model connecting farmers and micro-agribusinesses  regenerative produce to local markets, building community bioeconomy and improving access to nutritious food. It will also continue raising awareness and building knowledge on indigenous regenerative farming s role in creating a resilient, sustainable food system.
Innovation Description: In West Timor, food insecurity is a critical issue exacerbated by the climate crisis, disproportionately affecting underserved communities. Limited access to diverse and nutritious food leads to widespread malnutrition, with the region experiencing the highest stunting rates in Indonesia. Degenerative farming practices, such as monoculture and excessive use of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, degrade soil health and reduce productivity. These challenges are further compounded by post-harvest losses due to inadequate storage and preservation. While initiatives like community gardens and regenerative farming have been introduced, many lack economic sustainability and fail to align with local livelihoods. This results in low adoption of sustainable practices, perpetuating vulnerable food systems, poor food access, and worsening community health. Addressing these issues requires solutions that integrate sustainability with economic incentives. The PANGAN Program has been working with farmers to test post-harvest technologies such as solar dryers and black soldier fly cultivation, while also revitalizing indigenous regenerative farming practices to enhance sustainability, productivity, and resilience in local agriculture. Building on two years of implementing this program, we have designed a Local Food Hub as a scalable, community-based solution to strengthen the local economy and food system. This hub will connect smallholder farmers and micro-agribusinesses practicing indigenous regenerative farming with local markets, facilitating access to fresh produce and value-added products. It will also serve as an education center, run by local food producers, offering economic empowerment opportunities while improving food availability and nutrition, and building a resilient, sustainable bioeconomy for the region s underserved populations.

The country suffers from serious environmental degradation due to effect of population pressure, expansion of croplands, and reliance on fuel-wood as the major source of energy supply and over grazing. Productive safety-net program of the government and resilience-relief-rehabilitation-development programs of a number of civil society organizations and non-governmental supports are vital pillars that maintain the survival of the society. Guraghe Zone is one of the most vulnerable areas in the country. The community is highly dependent on subsistence agriculture as justified by 88% of the population engaged, but incredibly unable to feed itself and dependent uniquely on its children in towns and on safety-net program. This calls for attention to curb the problem and transform the sector. For this, innovative and strategic agricultural direction should be pursued. Zebidar, in collaboration with the local government, has come up with a mid-term strategic plan to address the problem. Hence, the project s overall objective is to ensure food security and conserve the natural environment via integrated watershed management by introducing improved varieties of perennial trees of Avocado, Papaya, Apple, Mango and selected vegetables. A seedlings nursery design will be studied to establish the site with a capacity of 500,000 seedlings. The government is willing and committed to avail necessary land for the nursery. Project infrastructure and irrigation scheme will be constructed.

Project Title: Digitally Empowering Smallholder Farmers for Agroecological Transitions and Resilient Food Systems in Africa
Executive Summary: Our project leverages digital financial tools and market access pathways to empower Africa s smallholder farmers in transitioning to agroecological practices. Through a mobile wallet, multi-account debit card, and AI-powered credit scoring, we provide tailored savings, working capital, and insurance. By connecting farmers to verified buyers, we enhance productivity, reduce post-harvest losses, and boost incomes. This approach fosters sustainability, resilience, and inclusivity, transforming agri-food systems across Africa.
Innovation Description: Smallholder farmers, who produce 70% of Africa's food, face significant financial exclusion and limited market access, with over $250 billion in unmet annual financing needs. These barriers hinder the adoption of agroecological practices essential for improving productivity, resilience, and sustainability. Farmers struggle to access secure savings, working capital, and insurance, while inefficiencies in market linkages reduce their income and increase post-harvest losses.  eMaisha Pay solves this problem by leveraging digital financial tools and market linkages. Using a mobile wallet and multi-account debit card, farmers access tailored financial solutions, including secure savings, working capital for climate-smart inputs, and insurance to safeguard against climate shocks. Our AI-powered credit scoring system assesses creditworthiness, enabling farmers to access loans without collateral. Additionally, the platform connects farmers to verified buyers, ensuring better produce prices and reducing reliance on exploitative middlemen.  This innovation is driven by insights from eMaisha Pay s extensive work with over 14,000 farmers in Uganda, revealing that access to tailored financial tools and reliable markets significantly improves agroecological adoption. Immediate benefits include increased productivity (up to 28% per acre), reduced post-harvest losses (18%), and higher incomes (25% increase in produce prices). The platform also promotes inclusivity, with 68% of credit accessed by women and youth, fostering equity and resilience in rural communities.  Sustainably, the innovation drives agroecological transitions, supporting food security, environmental health, and socioeconomic development, transforming Africa s agri-food systems into equitable and resilient ecosystems.

Project Title: Transforming Post-Harvest Waste into Nutritious Food to Empower Communities and Combat Food Insecurity"
Executive Summary: Our project reduces post-harvest food waste by transforming visually rejected but high-quality produce into nutritious, affordable food. We empower smallholder farmers, women, and youth with agro-processing training, creating economic opportunities and promoting food security. Through innovative hubs and a tech-driven pricing platform, we ensure sustainable practices, minimize greenhouse gas emissions, and address malnutrition in vulnerable populations. This integrated approach fosters climate resilience, gender equity, and a circular economy in Kenya's agri-food systems
Innovation Description: The project addresses the dual challenges of post-harvest food waste and food insecurity, which disproportionately affect smallholder farmers, vulnerable urban populations, and the environment. In Kenya, up to 60% of fresh farm produce is discarded due to visual imperfections, resulting in significant income loss for farmers and environmental harm from decomposing waste. Simultaneously, urban slums and arid regions face widespread malnutrition due to limited access to affordable, nutritious food.  Our solution transforms visually rejected but high-quality produce into affordable, nutrient-rich food, including Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Foods (RUTFs). This reduces waste while boosting farmers' incomes by 60-80%. Women and youth are trained in agro-processing and entrepreneurship at community hubs, enabling them to establish small businesses and achieve financial independence.  The initiative leverages a tech-driven dynamic pricing and waste-tracking platform, which connects farmers, retailers, and processors, optimizing market efficiency and reducing waste. Circular economy principles ensure sustainable resource utilization, while reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting climate resilience.  Immediate benefits include increased income for farmers, nutritious food for underserved communities, and skill development for women and youth. Long-term impacts include sustainable livelihoods, reduced malnutrition, and enhanced environmental sustainability. This integrated approach demonstrates that empowering communities through innovation can address systemic challenges in food security and climate action while fostering economic and social equity.

Project Title: Empowering Smallholder Farmers with Climate-Smart Practices for Improved Food Systems and Resilience in West Africa.
Executive Summary: We will leverage our digital platform, input delivery, and tailored agricultural training to scale a pilot that increases smallholder farmer adoption of agroecological practices in Mali. Our focus will be on supporting farmers to improve their yields and income while investing in the long-term health of their soils by reducing reliance on chemical fertilizer and maximizing soil fertility through regenerative agricultural practices.
Innovation Description: In West Africa, there are 60 million farmers, a large proportion of whom live on less than $2 per day. Farmers face numerous challenges that keep them in a cycle of poverty:  -Farmers don t have money when they need it for planting. Their cash flow is strongest at harvest time; however, they lack access to bank accounts to save money to reinvest in their farms the next planting season; -Farmers lack access to high-quality inputs; -Farmers lack access to training on improved agronomic practices; -Many farmers depend on one rainy season for their farming and have no other income.  myAgro s solution disrupts this cycle:  -Our mobile layaway platform allows farmers to save money in small increments toward purchasing a package of high-quality seeds and fertilizer; -myAgro procures and delivers the inputs to farmers in time for planting season; -myAgro provides farmers with climate-smart training to improve soil fertility and maximize harvests; -myAgro provides farmers with access to dry season products that diversify their food sources and income.  This model was created by innovating on ideas generated by farmers. Our founder, Anushka, was working on microloan repayment for smallholder farmers at an organization in Africa. When some farmers asked her if they could pre-pay their loans, she recognized they were describing savings and designed a platform to help them save.  myAgro s solution is proven to increase yields and income at scale. In 2023, our 200k farmers, on average, grew 2.5 times more food and earned $164 more than control farmers.

Project Title: CLEAN ENERGY SOLUTIONS FOR POST HARVEST PROCESSING
Executive Summary: RVM Nepal is implementing clean energy solutions for post-harvest processing in Nepal, focusing on reducing energy consumption, improving storage conditions, and minimizing post-harvest losses. By integrating thermal energy storage systems, solar-powered solutions, and AI-driven monitoring, RVM Nepal aims to enhance efficiency, reduce costs, and increase the sustainability of agriculture and agro-processing. This initiative will benefit smallholder farmers, cooperatives, and rural communities, contributing to food security and sustainable agricultural practices in Nepal.
Innovation Description: RVM Nepal addresses the critical problem of high post-harvest losses and inefficiency in cold storage and food processing systems, especially in rural Nepal. Inadequate post-harvest management, energy-intensive cold storage, and lack of reliable solutions to preserve agricultural produce contribute to significant food waste and financial losses for farmers. This problem directly impacts food security and economic stability in rural communities. RVM Nepal s innovative solution involves integrating clean energy technologies, such as solar power, thermal energy storage systems, and AI-driven monitoring, to reduce energy consumption and extend the shelf life of perishable agricultural products. By implementing Phase Change Materials (PCM) for energy storage, RVM Nepal provides a sustainable, cost-effective alternative to traditional refrigeration methods. These systems use solar energy to generate cooling and store excess energy for use during off-hours, thus ensuring optimal storage conditions for perishable products.
